APPLIEDBeyond Independent Predictions: Learning the Browsing Journey for Sequence-Level Re-ranking
Jiayi Zhang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jingxin Hai (Xi’an Jiaotong University) · Zhenjia Ma (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Hongbin Pei (Xi’an Jiaotong University) · Dagui Chen (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Han Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jian Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
Re-ranking aims to present users with an ordered list that maximizes sequence-level utility. Industrial deployments widely adopt the Generator–Evaluator framework, where the generator proposes candidate sequences, and the evaluator scores them to select the best one for display. The fidelity of the evaluator's utility estimates thus directly governs recommendation quality. However, existing evaluators predominantly follow the Independent Behavior Modeling (IBM) paradigm, which simplifies the continuous user browsing journey into independent per-item predictions (e.g., CTR). This oversimplification ignores two physical realities: (i) a click can occur only after the item has been reached and impressed, and (ii) items compete for finite user attention. As a result, IBM produces systematically biased evaluations and suboptimal sequence selection. To address this, we propose a Joint Behavior Modeling (JBM) perspective that explicitly models the display → impression → click process to capture causal and competitive dependencies within a sequence. Building on JBM, we develop the Impression-Click Evaluator (ICE), a plug-and-play framework that (i) predicts a browsing-depth distribution to estimate per-position impression probabilities, (ii) leverages predicted impressions to suppress spurious context from unexposed items during click modeling, and (iii) introduces a click distribution matching objective to capture intra-sequence dependencies. Extensive offline experiments across diverse backbones, together with a 14-day online A/B test in the Taobao App (+0.70% clicks, +3.67% revenue) and full-traffic deployment, validate the effectiveness and robustness of our approach.
APPLIEDSARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking
Ruochen Yang (Institute of Information Engineering, CAS; School of Cyber Security, University of CAS) · Yueyang Liu (Kuaishou Technology) · Zijie Zhuang (Kuaishou Technology) · Changxin Lao (Kuaishou Technology) · Yuhui Zhang (Kuaishou Technology) · Jiangxia Cao (Kuaishou Technology) · Jia Xu (Kuaishou Technology) · Xiang Chen (Kuaishou Technology) · Haoke Xiao (Kuaishou Technology) · Xiangyu Wu (Kuaishou Technology) · Xiaoyou Zhou (Kuaishou Technology) · Xiao Lv (Kuaishou Technology) · Shuang Yang (Kuaishou Technology) · Tingwen Liu (Institute of Information Engineering, CAS; School of Cyber Security, University of CAS) · Zhaojie Liu (Kuaishou Technology) · Han Li (Kuaishou Technology) · Kun Gai (Kuaishou Technology)
Abstract
Large-scale live-streaming recommendation requires precise modeling of non-stationary content semantics under strict real-time serving constraints. In industrial deployment, two common approaches exhibit fundamental limitations: discrete semantic abstractions sacrifice descriptive precision through clustering, while dense multimodal embeddings are extracted independently and remain weakly aligned with ranking optimization, limiting fine-grained content-aware ranking. To address these limitations, we propose SARM, an end-to-end ranking architecture that integrates natural-language semantic anchors directly into ranking optimization, enabling fine-grained author representations conditioned on multimodal content. Each semantic anchor is represented as learnable text tokens jointly optimized with ranking features, allowing the model to adapt content descriptions to ranking objectives. A lightweight dual-token gated design captures domain-specific live-streaming semantics, while an asymmetric deployment strategy preserves low-latency online training and serving. Extensive offline evaluation and large-scale A/B tests show consistent improvements over production baselines. SARM has been fully deployed and serves over 400 million users daily at Kuaishou.
APPLIEDDecomposing Staleness in Recommender Systems: A Dual-Filter Framework for Supersession and Decay
Di Bai (Google LLC) · Feng Han (Google LLC) · Zhenwei Tang (Google LLC) · Jintao Liu (Google LLC) · Luoshu Wang (Google LLC) · Jialu Liu (Google LLC)
Abstract
Stale recommendations are a pervasive challenge and a leading source of user complaints on large-scale content platforms. Items lose relevance through two primary mechanisms: supersession, where emerging updates render prior coverage stale, and relevance decay, where an item's informational value naturally diminishes over its lifecycle. Traditional countermeasures serve as crude proxies: age cutoffs poorly reflect actual relevance loss, while engagement heuristics rely on lagging signals, broadly exposing users to stale content before the system adapts. We present SDF (Supersession-Decay Filtering), a staleness filtering system fully deployed in Google Discover, a personalized recommendation feed with hundreds of millions of daily and billions of monthly active users. SDF targets both mechanisms with complementary filters, each powered by a learned model: a relational staleness model that detects supersession between item pairs, and a predicted traffic ratio (PTR) model that forecasts relevance decay from the item's content, trained on lifetime visit traffic. Applied via disjunction upstream of the ranking stage, SDF prunes stale candidates, measurably reducing downstream serving costs. Online experiments demonstrate that these filters significantly reduce the prevalence of stale content while improving user engagement. Over a two-year production deployment, user-filed staleness reports (in-product user feedback) declined by 54.9% relative to the pre-deployment baseline, establishing SDF as a robust and scalable paradigm for resolving content staleness at industrial scale.
APPLIEDELBO_TDS: Temporal Distribution Shift Generalization for Industry-Scale Recommender Systems
Yuxuan Zhu (Shopee) · Cong Fu (Shopee) · Yabo Ni (Nanyang Technological University) · Anxiang Zeng (Nanyang Technological University) · Yuan Fang (Singapore Management University)
Abstract
Temporal distribution shift (TDS) degrades the generalization of recommender systems: models trained on past interactions face systematically different user behavior in future time windows. While incremental training on recent data is widely used in industry production, it can over-adapt to transient patterns and exacerbate instability. Existing approaches such as invariant learning and self-supervised learning offer partial solutions but often suffer from unstable temporal generalization, representation collapse, or inefficient data utilization. To address these limitations, we propose ELBOTDS, a probabilistic framework for temporally robust recommendation. First, we identify key shifting factors on real-world production data and design a simple yet effective data augmentation strategy that simulate realistic time-varying factors to extend the training support. Second, we derive a self-supervised variational objective ELBOTDS to harness the benefits of this extended distribution while preventing representation collapse. Extensive experiments on both a public benchmark and a large-scale industrial dataset demonstrate ELBOTDS consistently improves next-period ranking performance over strong baselines, yielding a 2.33% uplift in GMV per user online and has been successfully deployed in production. Code is available at https://github.com/FuCongResearchSquad/ELBO4TDS.
APPLIEDIntSR: A Deployed Generative System for Integrated Search and Recommendation at Amap
Huimin Yan (Alibaba Group) · Longfei Xu (Alibaba Group) · Junjie Sun (Alibaba Group) · Ni Ou (Alibaba Group) · Wei Luo (Alibaba Group) · Xing Tan (Alibaba Group) · Ran Cheng (Alibaba Group) · Kaikui Liu (Alibaba Group) · Xiangxiang Chu (Alibaba Group)
Abstract
At Amap, a leading mapping platform serving hundreds of millions of users, isolated search and recommendation systems posed significant challenges in engineering costs and user experience. To address this, we present IntSR, a generative system that successfully integrates search and recommendation (S&R) tasks. IntSR has delivered substantial business value across diverse scenarios, including a +9.34% relative increase in digital asset GMV, a +2.76% relative lift in POI recommendation CTR, and a +7.04% relative improvement in travel mode suggestion ACC. The system's success relies on two innovations designed for a real-world environment: (1) a novel Query-Driven Block (QDB) to manage the computational complexity of a unified model at scale, and (2) a time-aware negative sampling strategy to handle constantly changing corpus items. Our work provides a valuable reference and critical insights into deploying integrated generative models in industrial settings.
APPLIEDTransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation
Zhifei Zheng (Renmin University of China) · Yunfei Liu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Bin Liu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Qiren Zhu (Renmin University of China) · Hanbing Liu (Renmin University of China) · Ziru Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Han Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jian Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Qi Qi (Renmin University of China) · Bo Zheng (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
Applying scaling laws to recommendation retrieval is hindered by feature heterogeneity: naively stacking Transformer layers yields diminishing returns because heterogeneous fields produce severe token-norm divergence. We present TransRetrieval, a Transformer-based retrieval framework that scales with both computational budget and cross-domain data. The key enabler is (1) weighted average aggregation, which restores the homogeneous-token assumption Transformers rely on. Building on this, we introduce (2) target token compression that cuts per-candidate FLOPs by 85% while preserving cross-attention expressiveness, and (3) position-style domain embeddings that unify multiple domains at negligible additional cost, turning cross-domain data into a scaling asset. On a 40-billion-interaction industrial dataset and the public KuaiRand benchmark, scaling compute from 0.1 to 2 MFLOPs per target yields +19.3 / +22.2 pt Recall@2000, confirming robust log-linear scaling. In online A/B tests, TransRetrieval lifts platform revenue by 2.53% under the same end-to-end latency constraint as the production baseline.
APPLIEDSORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders
Chunqi Wang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Bingchao Wu (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Taotian Pang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Jiahao Wang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Jie Yang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Jia Liu (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Hao Zhang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Hai Zhu (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Lei Shen (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Shizhun Wang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Bing Wang (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group) · Xiaoyi Zeng (Alibaba International Digital Commercial Group)
Abstract
While Transformers have achieved remarkable success in LLMs through superior scalability, their application in industrial-scale ranking models remains nascent, hindered by the challenges of high feature sparsity and low label density. In this paper, we propose SORT (Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer), a scalable model designed to bridge the gap between Transformers and industrial-scale ranking models. We address the high feature sparsity and low label density challenges through a series of optimizations, including request-centric sample organization, local attention, query pruning and generative pre-training. Furthermore, we introduce a suite of refinements to the tokenization, multi-head attention (MHA), and feed-forward network (FFN) modules, which collectively stabilize the training process and enlarge the model capacity. To maximize hardware efficiency, we optimize our training system to elevate the model FLOPs utilization (MFU) to 45%. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SORT outperforms strong baselines and exhibits excellent scalability across data size, model size and sequence length, while remaining flexible at integrating diverse features. Finally, online A/B testing in large-scale e-commerce scenarios confirms that SORT achieves significant gains in key business metrics—including orders (+7.47%), buyers (+6.67%) and GMV (+8.65%)—while simultaneously cutting latency by 62% and boosting throughput nearly sevenfold (+589%). SORT has been fully deployed in production, serving all users on AliExpress.
APPLIEDAuxiliary Focal Discrimination for Recommendation
Kaiyi Liu (Tencent Inc.) · Hongda Hu (Tencent Inc.) · Xinyan Lu (Tencent Inc.) · Jin Chen (Tencent Inc.) · Junwei Pan (Tencent Inc.) · Shudong Huang (Tencent Inc.) · Lijie Wang (Tencent Inc.) · Lifeng Wang (Tencent Inc.) · Lei Xiao (Tencent Inc.) · Haijie Gu (Tencent Inc.) · Jie Jiang (Tencent Inc.)
Abstract
Scaling up recommender models has become a major route to improving recommendation performance, but effective scaling relies on learning robust and discriminative representations. We identify local representation collapse as a critical bottleneck in this process: under sparse feedback, label-distinct samples can be mapped to highly overlapping local neighborhoods, making fine-grained discrimination increasingly difficult. Existing studies of representation collapse mainly focus on global representation statistics, while auxiliary ranking objectives typically apply pairwise supervision broadly across samples, overlooking the localized nature and varying severity of collapse. To address this limitation, we propose Auxiliary Focal Discrimination (AFD), a geometry-aware framework that adaptively concentrates discriminative supervision on locally collapsed label-distinct pairs. AFD measures pairwise latent proximity using a closeness coefficient and employs it to weight an auxiliary ranking loss, assigning stronger supervision to more severely collapsed pairs while exerting less influence on already well-separated ones. Experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that AFD consistently improves ranking performance, enlarges positive–negative representation margins, and slows singular-value decay, indicating stronger discriminability and alleviated dimensional collapse. Moreover, AFD has been fully deployed in Tencent's online advertising system, achieving GMV lifts of 0.80% and 1.06% in Weixin Channels and Weixin Moments, respectively.
APPLIEDLFM4Ads: Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation
Jie Jiang (Tencent) · Shangyu Zhang (Tencent) · Shijie Quan (Tencent) · Zhongren Wang (Tsinghua University) · Tianqu Zhuang (Tsinghua University) · Junwei Pan (Tencent) · Bo Fu (Tencent) · Yilong Sun (Tencent) · Jieying Lin (Tencent) · Jushuo Chen (Tencent) · Xiaotian Li (Tencent) · Wenjie Li (Tsinghua University) · Zhixiang Feng (Tencent) · Xian Hu (Tencent) · Huiting Deng (Tencent) · Hua Lu (Tencent) · Jinpeng Wang (Tsinghua University) · Boqi Dai (Tencent) · Xiaoyu Chen (Tencent) · Bin Hu (Tencent) · Lili Huang (Tencent) · Yanwen Wu (Tencent) · Yeshou Cai (Tencent) · Qi Zhou (Tencent) · Huang Tang (Tencent) · Chunfeng Yang (Tencent) · Chengguo Yin (Tencent) · Tingyu Jiang (Tencent) · Lifeng Wang (Tencent) · Shudong Huang (Tencent) · Dapeng Liu (Tencent) · Yuekui Yang (Tencent) · Shu-Tao Xia (Tsinghua University) · Lei Xiao (Tencent) · Haijie Gu (Tencent)
Abstract
Recent work leverages large-scale pretrained foundation models (FMs) to transfer generalizable representations to downstream advertising tasks. Most existing paradigms transfer user representations (URs) and item representations (IRs), while underutilizing the user-item cross representations (CRs) generated by deeper interaction layers. Although a recent approach transfers target-aware embeddings (TAEs), it requires real-time upstream FM inference alongside downstream model inference, introducing additional engineering complexity and overhead. To address these limitations, we propose Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation (LFM4Ads), an efficient pretrain-then-transfer framework for cross-domain ad recommendation. LFM4Ads jointly exploits URs, IRs, and CRs from the upstream FM, covering both isolated user/item semantics and fine-grained user-item interactions. It extracts sample-level CRs from pretrained interaction layers and aggregates them into user-level CRs with temporal decay, thereby decoupling upstream FM inference from downstream online serving. To enable efficient utilization of CRs, we further propose multi-granular downstream usages, including feature-level gating for CR fusion, module-level fine-tuning to yield downstream CRs, and model-level retrieval by matching CRs with IRs. Since Q4 2024, LFM4Ads has been deployed on Tencent's advertising platform. It has supported 10+ launches across major scenarios, yielding a platform-wide gross merchandise value (GMV) lift of 2.45% and annual revenue gains in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Offline experiments on KuaiRand-1K also validate the effectiveness of LFM4Ads, and our code is available at https://github.com/ZhuangQu/LFM4Ads.
APPLIEDTask-Blind No MORE: Multi-Task Information Flow in Unified Ranking Backbones
Yuchen Wang (Hello Group) · Feng Niu (University of Science and Technology of China) · Qing Tan (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Junting Lu (Beijing Information Science and Technology University) · Baoxin Wu (Hello Group) · Jun Gao (Hello Group)
Abstract
Industrial ranking models for recommendation have scaled feature interaction and sequence modeling separately; recent architectures such as HyFormer and MixFormer unify both in a stackable backbone. Real-world recommender systems, however, nearly always require multi-task learning, yet existing unified architectures confine multi-task modeling to shallow post-backbone towers, leaving the backbone without task-aware information flow. We propose MORE (Multi-task cO-evolving Ranking modEl), which embeds multi-task information flow inside the backbone, enabling task-specific signals to co-evolve with sequence and feature representations at every layer rather than in a post-hoc fusion. It introduces Anchor Tokens that persist across backbone layers: Shared Anchors encode cross-task commonalities, while Private Anchors capture task-specific priors. In each block, Anchor Tokens (1) read task-conditioned signals from behavior sequences, (2) mix with non-sequential features under a task-boundary mask, and (3) refine per-task representations through independent branches; as blocks stack, each task obtains a differentiated representation refined through all backbone layers. Experiments on large-scale industrial datasets show that MORE consistently outperforms baselines across all tasks under comparable parameter and FLOPs budgets, and scales well with model size. Online A/B tests on Momo, a leading Chinese social discovery platform with tens of millions of monthly active users, yield 3% improvement in usage duration, 3.6% in interaction rate, and 2% in deep-chat rate. MORE is deployed in production with request-level shared computation reducing scoring latency by about 30%.
APPLIEDAn Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking
Lars Hertel (Linkedin) · Gaurav Srivastava (Linkedin) · Syed Ali Naqvi (Linkedin) · Satyam Kumar (Linkedin) · Yue Zhang (Linkedin) · Borja Ocejo (Linkedin) · Benjamin Zelditch (Linkedin) · Adrian Englhardt (Linkedin) · Hailing Cheng (Linkedin) · Andy Hu (Linkedin) · Antonio Alonso (Linkedin) · Daming Li (Linkedin) · Siddharth Dangi (Linkedin) · Chen Zhu (Linkedin) · Mingzhou Zhou (Linkedin) · Wanning Li (Linkedin) · Tao Huang (Linkedin) · Fedor Borisyuk (Linkedin) · Ganesh Parameswan (Linkedin) · Birjodh Tiwana (Linkedin) · Sriram Sankar (Linkedin) · Qing Lan (Linkedin) · Julie Choi (Linkedin) · Souvik Ghosh (Linkedin)
Abstract
LinkedIn Feed enables professionals worldwide to discover relevant content, build connections, and share knowledge at scale. We present Feed Sequential Recommender (Feed SR), a transformer-based sequential ranking model for LinkedIn Feed that replaces a DCNv2-based ranker and meets strict production constraints. We detail the modeling choices, training techniques, and serving optimizations that enable deployment at a scale of 1.2 billion members. Feed SR has been serving the majority of LinkedIn’s Feed traffic for over three months and shows significant improvements in member engagement (+2.10% time spent, +3.52% like, comments, or reshares) in online A/B tests compared to the existing production model. We also describe our deployment experience with alternative sequential and LLM-based ranking architectures and why Feed SR provided the best combination of online metrics and production efficiency.
APPLIEDScaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling
Maksim Utushkin (AI VK) · Andrei Ovsiannikov (AI VK) · Alexander D'yakonov (AI VK)
Abstract
Friend recommendation is inherently graph-structured: the relevance of a potential connection depends on multi-hop social context rather than user attributes alone. However, deploying message-passing GNNs on a production-scale social graph with hundreds of millions of users and tens of billions of edges requires addressing numerous modeling and systems challenges. We present a scalable end-to-end GNN ranking system for production social graphs, focusing on two design choices that are critical in this setting: multi-hash ID embeddings and temporal neighbor sampling. Multi-hash embeddings are common for high-cardinality features, but industrial GNN systems typically either ignore trainable IDs or accept full embedding tables — exceeding 200 GB for our graph. We integrate multi-hash as the primary node representation, reducing the ID-embedding table size by >98% while preserving ranking quality. Temporal neighbor sampling is well understood in principle, but existing implementations scan full adjacency lists — a non-starter for users with tens of thousands of friends. We implement timestamp-sorted CSR storage with binary search, reducing the per-node temporal sampling cost from O(deg(v)+k) to O(log deg(v)+k). Beyond these components, we show that this combination scales and yields measurable production impact. On a graph with 194M users and 28B edges, offline ablations isolate each design choice's contribution. In an online A/B test, our system increases friend additions from recommendations by 16% and unique friend adders by 11.5% over a strong production baseline. We release our framework for distributed training and inference on large temporal graphs.
1D · LLM Reasoning & EvaluationFull ResearchSala OspitiMonday 10:30 – 12:308 talksChair: Joemon Jose (University of Glasgow)
FULLCode-as-Auditor: Executable Compliance Reasoning via Regulation-to-Code
Jisoo Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Taeyoon Kwack (Sungkyunkwan University) · Jinwoo Jang (Sungkyunkwan University) · Woo Kyung Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Honguk Woo (Sungkyunkwan University)
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted for compliance and legal reasoning tasks, yet their outputs often lack explicit grounding in legal logic and evidence. We present Code-as-Auditor, an LLM-based framework that extends the model’s reasoning capability toward structured and evidence-grounded compliance assessment. The framework translates regulatory information into (1) formalized checklists and executable decision trees, encoding regulations and conditions as interpretable code structures. During inference, each checklist item is (2) dynamically expanded into factual and counterfactual questions, guiding the model to reason over case-specific evidence and potential violations. This process establishes a reasoning pipeline that proceeds from evidence identification, through rule application, to final decision-making, while a self-verification loop ensures logical consistency and traceability of outcomes. Experiments on privacy and data protection scenarios demonstrate that Code-as-Auditor delivers more accurate and evidence-backed evaluations, enabling automated compliance regulation checking grounded in explicit regulatory criteria.
FULLBridging Intuition and Logic: A Dual-Memory Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Narrative Reasoning
Feiyang Wu (National University of Defense Technology) · Ning Pang (Aviation University of Air Force) · Peixin Huang (Logistics University of People's Armed Police Force) · Zhen Tan (National University of Defense Technology) · Xiang Zhao (National University of Defense Technology) · Weidong Xiao (National University of Defense Technology)
Abstract
Narrative reasoning is defined as predicting future events from narrative context, requiring an understanding of event evolution and implicit causality. Current memory-augmented approaches follow two separate paradigms: episodic-memory retrieval, which leverages past analogies but often leads to logical hallucination due to surface-level similarity, and semantic-memory retrieval using Event-centric Knowledge Graphs (EKGs), which ensures logical consistency but suffers from sparsity in open-world settings. Inspired by the Complementary Learning Systems (CLS) theory in cognitive science, we propose a Dual-Memory Neuro-Symbolic Framework (DMNeS), which synergizes episodic intuition and semantic verification for logically reliable narrative reasoning. Specifically, the Episodic Intuition Reasoner generates intuitive predictions based on retrieved analogous episodes. To mitigate potential logical hallucination, these predictions are then validated by the Semantic Logic Verifier using causal-temporal evidence retrieved from an EKG. When an otherwise consistent candidate lacks an explicit EKG path due to sparsity, Abductive Reflection prompts the LLM to hypothesize a latent bridge event and connecting relations, and re-verifies the resulting chain under occurrence and temporal constraints. Finally, the Dynamic Memory Evolution module consolidates both memories, strengthening their interplay. As a fine-tuning-free inference framework, DMNeS achieves a 5.7 percentage-point average gain over the strongest baseline and improves LLM backbones by 7.5--9.7 percentage points across three benchmarks.
FULLFISolver: Data-Driven Discovery of First Integrals via Backward Generation and Guided Reinforcement Learning
Jingfeng Zhong (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Zhengxiang Liu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Zhijie Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Shuai Li (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
Abstract
The discovery of first integrals is of profound scientific significance for understanding physical conservation laws in dynamical systems. However, existing symbolic computation systems and Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle with this task due to the scarcity of high-quality training data and the reliance on mathematical intuition for finding solutions. This paper introduces FISolver, an LLM-based solver designed to bridge this gap. First, we propose a novel “Backward Generation” algorithm that systematically constructs large-scale datasets of (differential equations, first integrals) pairs by deriving equations from sampled integrals, effectively overcoming the data scarcity bottleneck. Second, we perform supervised fine-tuning on a compact mathematical model and further enhance its capabilities using reinforcement learning with a Levenshtein Distance-based shaped reward function. Additionally, we introduce data synthesis and blending techniques that enable effective adaptation to specific hard instances with sparse examples. Experiments demonstrate that FISolver, with significantly lower computational cost, substantially outperforms larger mathematical LLMs and commercial solvers like Mathematica on complex benchmarks, establishing a new data-driven paradigm for automated mathematical discovery.
FULLSteering Large Language Models toward Cross-Cultural Value Alignment via Activation Engineering
Jinchuan Zhang (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Jingyi Lin (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yukun Yang (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yan Zhou (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Songlin Hu (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Large language models increasingly shape human decision-making as conversational assistants and act on human behalf as autonomous agents, making the cultural values they encode consequential across both settings. Yet ensuring that these systems reflect the values of diverse cultural groups remains an open challenge, as existing alignment approaches offer limited ability to precisely control cultural value orientations on demand. In this work, we investigate cultural value representations in LLM activation space through the lens of Hofstede's six-dimensional framework. We first demonstrate that contrastive activation steering reliably controls individual cultural value dimensions, significantly and consistently outperforming prompt-based steering across two models and two independent evaluation protocols. We then show that cultural value dimensions are not geometrically independent: positively correlated value vectors mutually amplify each other's effects at the cost of response coherence, while negatively correlated vectors attenuate each other through directional cancellation. These interference patterns impose a fundamental constraint on naive multi-dimensional steering. Motivated by this geometric analysis, we propose a selective projection decoupling method that removes inter-dimension interference prior to joint injection and fits steering coefficients to country-level Hofstede profiles. Evaluated on Brazil, China, and the United States, our method achieves consistent improvements in alignment accuracy, direction hits, and cultural similarity across both Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct models, demonstrating that steered models are not only more culturally accurate but achieve high cultural similarity to their intended target profiles.
FULLFLoRE: A Formal Language Benchmark for Robustness and Effectiveness Evaluation of LLM Reasoning
Jinghao Zhang (Fudan University) · Shisong Chen (East China Normal University) · Zhixu Li (Renmin University of China) · Sihang Jiang (Fudan University) · Yanghua Xiao (Fudan University)
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs), especially recent reasoning-oriented models trained with reinforcement learning, achieve near-saturating accuracy on many reasoning benchmarks. However, it remains unclear whether these models truly reason over semantic structure or rely on superficial symbol patterns and familiar language forms. This issue is increasingly critical in the agent era, where reasoning systems must remain reliable under changing representations. We introduce FLoRE, a controllable evaluation benchmark for diagnosing LLM reasoning robustness and effectiveness using formal languages. By isolating reasoning from world knowledge, formal languages enable direct evaluation of structural reasoning with machine-verifiable ground truth. We defines two tasks: Formal Language Recognition and Grammar Induction and construct 25.5k data instances. Evaluating diverse reasoning and non-reasoning LLMs, we identify two universal failure modes. First, models exhibit severe symbol-binding fragility: changing symbolic representations while preserving semantics causes large drops on positive instances but increases accuracy on negative instances, revealing a strong default rejection bias under unfamiliar symbols. Second, many reasoning-oriented local LLMs show negation non-termination during grammar induction, failing to terminate reasoning on negative instances and instead exhausting large portions of the context window. Our results show that current LLM reasoning remains strongly dependent on surface symbol priors and lacks robust semantic invariance and termination stability. FLoRE provides a unified framework for systematically evaluating these properties in controllable formal-language settings. Code and data files are available at https://github.com/HoganZinger/FLoRE
FULLEfficient LLM Benchmark Evaluation with Bayesian Item Response and Routed Subspace Selection
Xin-Yi Zhang (School of Artificial Intelligence, Nanjing University) · Han-Jia Ye (School of Artificial Intelligence, Nanjing University) · De-Chuan Zhan (School of Artificial Intelligence, Nanjing University)
Abstract
As Large Language Models (LLMs) are evaluated on increasingly large and diverse benchmark suites, running an LLM on the entire benchmark incurs substantial costs. We study efficient LLM evaluation, where the goal is to accurately estimate full-benchmark performance by adaptively querying only a small subset of prompts. The key challenge is that selected prompts should be informative for the target model while remaining representative of diverse response patterns in the benchmark. To address this, we adopt a posterior-aware Bayesian perspective: historical response data are used to characterize complex prompt--model behaviors, and the resulting posterior information guides adaptive prompt selection under a limited budget. Specifically, we develop a variational Gaussian Process Item Response Theory (VGP-IRT) model, which leverages item-specific Gaussian process response functions to flexibly capture nonlinear prompt--model interactions beyond restrictive parametric response curves. Based on prompt features and predictive information derived from the VGP-IRT posterior, we further construct group-balanced candidate pools within local routed subspaces for adaptive selection. Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate improved score estimation through our method, with the strongest gains in the low-to-moderate budget regime.
FULLAutoRepairBench: Benchmarking Long-Tailed, Safety-Critical Automotive Repair Reasoning
Chenyu Zuo (Lingnan University) · Xuecheng Zhou (Sun Yat-sen University) · Yongqi Chen (Sun Yat-sen University) · Lei Xue (Sun Yat-sen University) · Shan Jiang (Sun Yat-sen University) · Jiaxing Shen (Lingnan University) · Chengzu Dong (Lingnan University)
Abstract
Vehicle diagnosis begins with structured signals—an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) identifier, a Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC), and trigger conditions—but technicians must translate them into an accurate fault description and appropriate repair measures. Automotive repair reasoning is both long-tailed and safety-critical: rare ECU/DTC combinations provide few training examples, while associating a fault with the wrong control unit or recommending unnecessary repairs can mislead maintenance decisions. Benchmarking this capability is challenging because diagnostic resources are fragmented, general-purpose large language models (LLMs) often fail to follow repair constraints, and exact-match metrics may reject valid answers expressed differently. We introduce AutoRepairBench, a BMW-centered benchmark and evaluation framework for long-tailed, safety-critical automotive repair reasoning. It supports single-turn diagnosis, multi-pair prompting, and frequency-aware analysis of common and rare cases. Its validated hierarchical evaluator accepts valid paraphrases while checking ECU/DTC associations, component relationships, repair severity, and unnecessary repair recommendations. We also develop RepairLLM-7B, a compact, retrieval-free model trained through two-stage distillation: the first stage reduces the dominance of frequent cases, while knowledge-graph-anchored online distillation emphasizes uncertain and rare cases. On a double-blind set of 585 cases labeled by three automotive experts, the evaluator achieved 94.19% accuracy and an F1 score of 94.67%. On the 500-instance main evaluation set, RepairLLM-7B achieved 95.0% single-turn joint accuracy (475/500) and 94.2% per-pair joint accuracy under multi-pair prompting (471/500); it also improved tail accuracy on the separate 100-instance generalization set and reduced safety-critical errors relative to supervised fine-tuning. These results demonstrate the importance of jointly benchmarking overall accuracy, rare-case performance, and repair safety in automotive repair reasoning.
FULLInternal Stability Signals for Selective Verification and Hallucination Mitigation in Vision-Language Models
Tong Zhang (Shanghai University of International Business and Economics) · Qingqing Ren (Independent Researcher) · Hualing Liu (Shanghai University of International Business and Economics) · Riquan Zhang (Shanghai University of International Business and Economics)
Abstract
Large vision-language models (LVLMs) are increasingly used for multimodal search, open-ended question answering, document understanding, and generated content analysis, yet they still produce claims that are fluent but unsupported by visual evidence. Existing hallucination mitigation methods often rely on external multimodal judges, language-model annotators, or human token labels to localize unsupported content, adding cost and introducing a mismatch with the target model's own failure modes. We propose HIS-Guard, a framework for trustworthy multimodal claim generation that diagnoses unsupported claims using the target LVLM's internal stability signals and routes those signals to selective verification or preference optimization. Its core diagnostic, Hallucination Instability Score (HIS), combines semantic convergence from cross-layer LogitLens entropy reduction with visual grounding coherence from cross-token attention-distribution consistency over image patches. By decomposing HIS into semantic and visual instability, HIS-Guard supports claim-level credibility analysis without external token-level hallucination localizers or auxiliary multimodal judges. We then instantiate a Diagnose-Treat-Prevent preference objective (DTP-DPO): semantic instability treats risky tokens by weighting DPO rewards, while visual and combined instability prevent visual neglect through gated auxiliary regularizers. Across Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and InternVL2.5-2B, HIS-guided optimization provides downstream evidence that the diagnostic captures useful failure modes. On Qwen2.5-VL-3B, HIS-Guard reduces CHAIR_s by 32.2% and CHAIR_i by 45.6% over the baseline, improves over standard DPO trained on identical data, and largely preserves POPE accuracy. Scaling to Qwen2.5-VL-7B keeps HIS-Guard best on both CHAIR and POPE, while InternVL results suggest that the diagnostic signal is useful but the regularization strength is architecture-sensitive. Together, these results position internal stability as a practical signal for trustworthy multimodal information systems, selective verification, and hallucination-aware evaluation. The public implementation is available at https://github.com/20508Z/HIS-DTP-DPO.
1E · AI for Education & HealthFull ResearchAuditoriumArteMonday 10:30 – 12:308 talksChair: Xinye Wanyan (RMIT University)
FULLEmulating Expert Intuition: Retrieval-Augmented Cognitive Diagnosis for Student Cold-Start
Yufan Lin (Central China Normal University) · Yuqian Hu (Central China Normal University) · Qiyuan Chen (Central China Normal University) · Le Li (Central China Normal University) · Jinrui Zhang (Central China Normal University) · Wenjing Zhou (Central China Normal University) · Bo Li (Central China Normal University)
Abstract
In intelligent education systems, cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) assess students' latent abilities through response records to enable personalized learning. However, existing CDMs struggle with inaccurate ability estimation under student cold-start conditions. Text-based CDMs, despite their strong generalization in data-rich scenarios, still suffer from ambiguous representations due to insufficient response records, which significantly hinders their practical deployment in real-world educational systems. Inspired by teachers' analogical reasoning when assessing new students, we propose Retrieval-Augmented Cognitive Diagnosis (RACD), a retrieval-augmented framework for CDMs. RACD fundamentally addresses student cold-start problems through a memory-retrieval-aggregation module that emulates teachers' analogical reasoning by retrieving and integrating similar student profiles from historical data. RACD is further enhanced by (1) Distinctiveness Regularization to align encoder outputs with distinctive representations and (2) Skill Shake that enforces contrastive learning for the retrieval module. Evaluations on three real-world datasets across four distinct cold-start configurations (different retention rates) show RACD outperforms both state-of-the-art CDMs and emerging LLM-based variants, with an average accuracy improvement of 1.2% and a peak gain of 2.1% over the best baseline in inductive scenarios, especially under student cold-start scenarios.
FULLPS²: Parameterized Control for Fine-Grained Student Proficiency Simulation
Ruochen Liu (Central South University) · Zhiyuan Wen (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University) · Hao Yan (Central South University) · Jun Yin (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University) · Senzhang Wang (Central South University) · Jiannong Cao (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
Abstract
Understanding how students with different proficiency levels respond to educational materials is a critical issue within the field of Education. However, acquiring sufficient real student response data for a robust evaluation is often hindered by cost, ethics, and security constraints. Consequently, LLM-based student proficiency simulation, especially prompt-based methods, has emerged as a practical alternative under data-scarce conditions. Despite their promise, current methods still exhibit limited controllability with coarse-grained proficiency representations, high sensitivity to prompt design, and the lack of calibration with academic performance. Therefore, we propose Parameterized Student Proficiency Simulation (PS²), an unsupervised and parameterized model-level framework that simulates students with different proficiencies by interpolating between a strong upper-bound LLM and a weaker, cognitive error-informed lower-bound student LLM via a hybrid ratio. Specifically, the lower-bound model is constructed by fine-tuning the weaker LM to exhibit cognitive errors when responding to educational materials. To ensure alignment with target proficiency levels, PS² further calibrates the interpolation ratio with academic performance. Experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that PS² achieves finer-grained and consistent proficiency simulation compared to existing baselines, leading to superior performance in student behavior similarity and item difficulty prediction.
FULLOPERA: Option-level Pedagogical Explanation via Reasoning for Augmented Knowledge Tracing
Zhiwei Huang (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Xueyi Li (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Jiaqi Zheng (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Xiangyu Zhao (City University of Hong Kong) · Zitao Liu (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University)
Abstract
Knowledge tracing (KT) aims to predict learners' future performance by modeling their historical interaction data. In real-world educational scenarios, multiple-choice questions are deliberately designed so that each distractor exposes a specific misconception; however, existing KT models rely on randomly initialized ID embeddings and reduce each interaction to a binary correctness label, making it difficult to exploit such option-level diagnostic signals. To address these problems, we propose an option-level pedagogical explanation framework for augmented KT, i.e., OPERA, which combines LLM-based option-level explanation generation, multi-judge quality assurance, and offline semantic embedding injection into existing KT backbones, with all LLM computation confined to one-time offline preprocessing. Experiments on three multiple-choice datasets demonstrate our framework's superior performance in terms of prediction accuracy, consistently improving lightweight ID-based backbones to match or surpass much heavier process-aware models. To encourage reproducible research, we have made our code publicly available at https://pykt.org/.
FULLSKG-KT: Semantic Knowledge Graph Construction and Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing by Large Language Models
Linqing Li (Centre for Change and Complexity in Learning, Adelaide University) · Xuri Ge (School of Artificial Intelligence, Shandong University) · Ying Zhou (School of Artificial Intelligence, Shandong University) · Xindi Wang (School of Artificial Intelligence, Shandong University) · Abhinava Barthakur (Centre for Change and Complexity in Learning, Adelaide University) · Vitomir Kovanovic (Centre for Change and Complexity in Learning, Adelaide University) · Srecko Joksimovic (Centre for Change and Complexity in Learning, Adelaide University)
Abstract
Knowledge Tracing (KT), a core component of intelligent tutoring systems, aims to model the dynamic evolution of students' knowledge states based on their historical interaction data. However, mainstream methods rely heavily on large-scale students' response logs, hindering generalization to unseen students, and often overlook the semantic structure of knowledge points in knowledge graph construction. In this paper, we propose Semantic Knowledge Graph-Based Knowledge Tracing (SKG-KT), a novel KT framework that leverages the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) to enhance the modelling of unseen students, without relying on numerous students with historical records. SKG-KT consists of two stages: ATC-ruled Semantic Graph Extraction and a Concept-aware Reasoning mechanism. In the first stage, we design a semantic student knowledge graph extraction method grounded in ATC rules, which captures the semantic structure across three hierarchical layers—domain, cluster, and standard—aligned with established educational theory. To extend beyond mathematics, we further introduce a multi-disciplinary semantic graph extraction method that induces an ATC-inspired hierarchical schema for other disciplines via LLM-based label induction. In the second stage, the Concept-aware Reasoning mechanism first applies knowledge concept reasoning to infer key knowledge concepts for unseen students with limited previous student data, and then fine-tunes an open-source LLM for correctness prediction based on the reasoned knowledge concepts, adapting the LLM to the KT task. Extensive experiments conducted on three publicly available educational benchmark datasets, namely Xes3g5m-small, Xes3g5m-large, and MOOCRadar, demonstrate that SKG-KT achieves state-of-the-art performance in knowledge tracing. Furthermore, SKG-KT has been validated to achieve robust predictive performance compared to others, while relying on a limited number of students with historical records. Our code and prompts are publicly available at the link (https://github.com/linqingliDestinyController/SKG_KT/tree/main).
FULLIncorporating Cognitive Load and Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Domain Knowledge Tracing
Haotian Zhang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Shucun Wang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Jinze Wu (iFLYTEK AI Research) · Liang Ding (iFLYTEK AI Research) · Shuochen Liu (University of Science and Technology of China) · Zhenya Huang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Jing Sha (iFLYTEK AI Research) · Shijin Wang (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence) · Qi Liu (University of Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to assess students' dynamic knowledge states from their learning histories. While most existing KT methods focus on single-domain learning with notable success, real-world learning scenarios often involve multiple domains simultaneously, introducing two critical factors: 1) Cognitive load, arising from managing learning across domains in both temporal and knowledge dimensions. 2) Knowledge transfer, where knowledge states in one domain influence related states both within and across domains. In this paper, we focus on exploring these factors to improve students’ knowledge state assessment in multi-domain learning scenarios and propose a novel method incorporating cognitive Load and knowledge Transfer for Multi-domain Knowledge Tracing (LT-MKT). Specifically, to bridge isolated domains, LT-MKT first integrates textual information from questions and their associated concepts to construct a Multi-domain Hierarchical Graph, leveraging the advanced representational capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Then, cross-domain features in both the temporal and knowledge dimensions are explicitly modeled to capture the effects of cognitive load. Additionally, a knowledge transfer module is designed to model the propagation of knowledge states within and across domains. By jointly modeling these factors, LT-MKT enables more accurate prediction of students’ future performance. Finally, extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.
FULLFoundation-Assisted Cross-Domain Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Molecular Property Prediction
Tianyi Jiang (Zhejiang University of Technology) · Shanqing Yu (Zhejiang University of Technology) · Qi Xuan (Zhejiang University of Technology)
Abstract
Molecular property prediction is important for drug discovery, but labeled molecules are often limited for new prediction tasks. The difficulty is amplified in cross-domain few-shot settings, where target tasks differ from available source tasks and the model must adapt from sparse target-domain supervision. Existing few-shot and transferable few-shot methods mainly condition adaptation on the target support set, which can be unstable when the support molecules provide limited coverage of the target distribution. We propose Foundation-Assisted Cross-Domain Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Molecular Property Prediction (FACML), which augments cross-domain episodic learning with property-aware priors from a frozen Structure-Property Multi-Modal foundation model (SPMM). FACML represents each molecule using SPMM-derived SMILES features and graph features, and constructs support Property Vector (PV) prototypes and query PV representations from SPMM-predicted PVs based on molecular SMILES. A property-conditioned relation graph then integrates molecular nodes and PV-based prior nodes to refine episode representations for target-task adaptation. Across cross-dataset few-shot molecular property prediction benchmarks, FACML improves the average ROC-AUC over the strongest baseline by 6.36% and 8.12% under the 1-shot and 10-shot settings, respectively. An auxiliary zero-target-label analysis further examines the use of SPMM-generated molecules when labeled target support molecules are unavailable.
FULLIM3: Interaction Region-Augmented Multimodal Molecular Modeling for Precision Prescription
Yujin Kim (Handong Global University) · Seoeun Park (Handong Global University) · Charmgil Hong (Handong Global University)
Abstract
Medication recommendation requires both therapeutic appropriateness and control of drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk. However, existing approaches face a semantic mismatch between the molecular mechanisms underlying DDIs and the clinical abstractions used for therapeutic assessment. This work addresses this limitation through a dual-level formulation that models interaction risk at the molecular level while incorporating therapeutic supervision and evaluation at the clinical class level. Building on this formulation, we propose IM3, an interaction region-augmented multimodal molecular modeling framework that integrates longitudinal electronic health records with quantum-informed drug representations. IM3 employs the Interaction Region Indicator (IRI) to encode interaction-relevant electronic regions of drug compounds and combines global electronic characteristics with local chemical substructures. This representation incorporates molecular interaction information beyond static molecular topology and prescription co-occurrence. Experiments on two real-world intensive care unit datasets show that IM3 substantially reduces DDI rates while maintaining competitive therapeutic performance relative to state-of-the-art baselines. These results indicate the complementary value of dual-level modeling and quantum-informed molecular representations for safer medication recommendation.
FULLHH-Track: Skeleton-Guided Visual Understanding with Prototype-Anchored RAG for Hand Hygiene Assessment
Dongxiao Li (City University of Macau) · Ruinan Chen (City University of Macau) · Weiyi Lyu (City University of Macau) · Haijuan Lian (Hangzhou Medical College) · Chi Liu (City University of Macau) · Gengshen Wu (City University of Macau) · Wenjian Liu (City University of Macau) · Fengshi Jing (City University of Macau)
Abstract
Knowledge-grounded assessment of procedural compliance is a growing challenge in healthcare informatics. Such assessment benefits from explicit grounding in authoritative clinical references. Hand hygiene assessment offers a canonical instance, since hand hygiene is the single most critical defense against healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). Existing automated solutions often provide only coarse-grained compliance signals, while fine-grained technique analysis can incur substantial computational cost. Direct application of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) introduces additional challenges because processing long-form clinical videos is expensive and generic MLLMs lack grounded procedural references. We propose HH-Track, a knowledge-grounded retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for fine-grained hand hygiene assessment. A skeleton-guided encoder first extracts structured clinical metrics and produces compact visual digests via boundary-progressive sampling. A prototype-anchored dual-stream RAG mechanism then retrieves step-aligned textual WHO guidelines and visual prototypes from curated reference resources. The MLLM uses these references for structured frame-level comparison during compliance assessment. To support this work, we construct Clinical-HHA, a hand hygiene dataset of 270 full-session recordings segmented into 1,408 step-level clips with template-guided expert compliance reports, paired with a curated visual prototype library. Release of both resources is subject to ongoing institutional review. Across five MLLM backbones, HH-Track improves compliance accuracy by an average of 36.1 percentage points over the Direct configurations, and the full dual-stream configuration further outperforms text-only grounding. Generated reports also show stronger agreement with expert-written references on average. These results support prototype-anchored multimodal retrieval for knowledge-grounded procedural assessment.

FULLDeDiff: Debiased Information Diffusion Prediction via Graph Disentanglement
Jiawei Chen (Tianjin University) · Song Cao (School of Computer Science and Technology, Tianjin University) · Wenjun Wang (School of Artificial Intelligence, Tianjin University)
Abstract
Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become a dominant paradigm for information diffusion prediction, yet their effectiveness can be undermined by biases inherent in observational diffusion data. In particular, skewed user activity and graph connectivity may encourage GNNs to exploit popularity-driven shortcuts rather than diffusion-relevant influence patterns. We attribute this limitation to the entanglement of predictive and bias-related signals in both graph structure and learned representations. To address this problem, we propose DeDiff, a disentangled graph debiasing framework that separates diffusion-relevant and bias-related signals at both the structural and representation levels. DeDiff first employs a low-rank adaptive edge mask to decompose the social and interaction graphs into complementary causal and bias views, preserving potentially informative diffusion pathways while isolating popularity-dominated shortcuts. It then introduces a dual-level representation disentanglement mechanism: causal–bias disagreement regularization discourages information leakage between the two branches, while inter-view contrastive learning preserves the distinct semantics of social and interaction relations and prevents excessive removal of useful structural information. Moreover, asymmetric branch supervision explicitly guides the bias branch to capture the empirical popularity distribution, reducing the incentive for the causal branch to encode the same shortcut and allowing it to focus on next-user prediction. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that DeDiff achieves consistently strong ranking performance and remains substantially more robust than competitive baselines under amplified popularity bias.
FULLLearning Latent Process Knowledge via Variational Distillation for Low-Resource Social Experiment Prediction
Yang Wu (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Zhicheng Zhang (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Xun Pang (Peking University) · Xiaolong Zheng (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have become a promising tool for scaling social experiments with silicon samples. However, fine-tuning LLMs for real randomized controlled trials faces a dual low-resource challenge: structurally balanced experimental data are often small, and the process knowledge that explains how respondent profiles and treatments jointly shape outcomes is unobserved. Without reliable process-level supervision, existing fine-tuning methods may struggle to learn why a respondent gives a particular outcome, as the model prior often provides too few useful trajectories for such domain-specific prediction tasks. To address this challenge, we propose VPKD, a Variationally motivated Process Knowledge Distillation framework. VPKD uses a teacher LLM to generate answer-conditioned posterior trajectories, filters them through masked reconstruction to retain student-useful process knowledge, and then distills the filtered trajectories into the student via SFT. By applying VPKD to a climate-policy attitude prediction task with only 500 data points and complex profile-treatment structure, we show that the learned process knowledge not only improves prediction accuracy, but also better recovers the causal effects of the original experiment.
FULLJECHO: Scalable Echo Chamber Detection via Jaccard-based Homophily and Seed Expansion
Ali Safarpoor Dehkordi (The Australian National University) · Atsushi Miyauchi (Intesa Sanpaolo) · Francesco Bonchi (Intesa Sanpaolo AI Research) · Ahad N. Zehmakan (The Australian National University)
Abstract
Detecting echo chambers is critical for understanding and limiting negative social phenomena, such as online polarization, misinformation, and conspiracy theory diffusion. However, the echo chamber detection (ECD) problem yet lacks a rigorous algorithmic foundation. We address this gap by formalizing a unified definition of echo chambers based on three principles: internal opinion homogeneity, opinion extremism, and structural isolation. Under such a definition, we establish the theoretical hardness of the ECD problem, proving it is NP-hard via a reduction from the conductance minimization problem. To circumvent this computational barrier, we derive a theoretical lower bound on the Jaccard-based homophily (JHO) of nodes that reside within valid echo chambers. This guarantee motivates JECHO, a novel algorithm that detects echo chambers via local seed expansion rather than global enumeration. JECHO first identifies seeds that exceed the JHO threshold and then applies a score-based expansion to optimize structural isolation. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic networks demonstrate that our theory-guided approach detects more structurally isolated echo chambers than state-of-the-art methods while reducing runtime by orders of magnitude.
FULLAdversarial Creation and Detection of AI-Generated Social Bot Content
Mykola Trokhymovych (Universitat Pompeu Fabra) · Ricardo Baeza-Yates (KTH Royal Institute of Technology) · Alessandro Flammini (Indiana University) · Diego Saez-Trumper (Universitat Pompeu Fabra) · Filippo Menczer (Indiana University)
Abstract
The convergence of large language models and social bots allows malicious actors to manipulate the information ecosystem by generating human-like content at scale. Existing models for detecting AI-generated content often fail in the wild, primarily due to the lack of ground-truth data. We address this gap through an adversarial methodology that models the impersonation of real social media users by malicious actors. Using this methodology, we curate a multilingual, cross-platform dataset of paired human and AI-generated messages. Training on such adversarial data yields accurate detection of AI-generated text. Our approach significantly outperforms existing models for content-based bot detection in real-world, out-of-distribution data.
FULLCSC: Calibrated Simplicity for Conflict-Aware Social Bot Detection in the LLM Era
Yipeng Qian (Minzu University of China) · Pengjie Zhao (Minzu University of China) · Chaoxi Niu (City University of Macau)
Abstract
Social bot detection is essential for protecting online platforms from misinformation amplification, coordinated manipulation, and distorted public discourse. However, large language models have made social bots much harder to detect from text alone because semantic camouflage is now cheap, fluent, and scalable. The resulting challenge is modality conflict: an account may look human-like in semantics while remaining suspicious in graph structure, profile attributes, or cross-modal consistency. Recent graph-based detectors tackle this limitation by adding graph-side complexity, such as sparse prototype selection, adaptive gating, or architecture-specific control logic, yet our experiments suggest that complexity alone is not the most reliable way to resolve such conflict. We therefore propose CSC, a calibrated-simplicity framework for conflict-aware LLM-era social bot detection. The framework combines three design choices: a simplified prototype-guided graph expert that retains useful structural biases while removing unstable graph-side heuristics, calibrated simplex-constrained fusion that aligns heterogeneous confidence spaces before late fusion, and a lightweight inconsistency expert that models cross-modal disagreement. Experiments on TwiBot-22, TwiBot-20, and MGStBot-large show that CSC improves calibrated operating-point decision quality while remaining competitive across external benchmarks. Further analyses show that calibration improves confidence reliability, the inconsistency expert mainly provides localized corrections in high-conflict or near-threshold regions, and simplified graph-side control yields a better stability-cost trade-off. A targeted semantic-camouflage stress test further shows that replacing selected bot text with matched human text sharply degrades the standalone text expert while leaving graph and fused evidence stable on a balanced challenge set. Overall, these results suggest that, when semantic evidence is easy to camouflage, robust bot detection benefits from preserving reliable structural signals and calibrating conflicting modalities before fusion, rather than continually increasing graph-side complexity.

Tao Yang (SKLCCSE, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Beihang University) · Yang Hu (SKLCCSE, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Beihang University) · Feihong Lu (SKLCCSE, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Beihang University) · Qingyun Sun (SKLCCSE, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Beihang University) · Jianxin Li (SKLCCSE, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Beihang University)
Abstract
To detect social bots, many advanced methods have been proposed, especially graph-based approaches, their effectiveness is undermined by sophisticated bots that create spurious associations in network structures. As a result, current methods often struggle to provide high-confidence detection results. This motivates us to quantify the uncertainty of the output and reduce the interference of misinformation on detection, so as to determine the confidence of the results and output high-confidence results. Therefore, we propose an uncertainty-aware bot detection method to inform the confidence and use the uncertainty score to pick a high-confidence decision from multiple views of a social network under different environments. Specifically, our proposed BotUmc uses LLM to extract information from tweets. Then, we construct a graph based on the extracted information, the original user information, and the user relationship, and generate multiple views of the graph by intervention. Lastly, an uncertainty loss is used to force the model to quantify the uncertainty of results and select the result with low uncertainty in one view as the final decision. Extensive experiments show the superiority of our method.
FULLLABRA: A Label-free Graph Neural Framework for Illicit Account Detection in Large-scale Blockchain Transaction Networks
Bi-Cheng Yan (National Taiwan Normal University, Taiwan) · Jhih-Rong Guo (National Taiwan Normal University, Taiwan) · Yin-Ju Wu (National Taiwan Normal University, Taiwan) · Fu-An Chao (National Taiwan Normal University, Taiwan) · Berlin Chen (National Taiwan Normal University, Taiwan)
Abstract
Illicit account detection in blockchain-based cryptocurrencies seeks to pinpoint anomalies within large-scale, decentralized transaction networks, figuring prominently in financial risk control systems. Existing efforts typically formulate transaction networks as directed multigraphs and leverage graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture topological information under limited supervision. Despite their decent performance, supervised GNN models are capped by data scarcity and structural noise, with the former arising from the lack of annotated data and the latter stemming from malicious actors forging deceptive connections. In light of these, we in this paper propose LABRA, a novel label-free graph modeling for detecting illicit accounts in blockchain transaction networks. Operating in an unsupervised manner, LABRA (The source code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/bicheng1225/LABRA.) leverages a discrepancy-aware graph encoder to produce discriminative node representations, and subsequently employs an anchor-guided scoring mechanism to designate anchor nodes for anomaly detection. Furthermore, a tailor-made message-passing scheme is introduced to mitigate structural noise, which captures atypical financial flows within a transaction graph while attenuating the feature-smoothing effect caused by high-degree nodes. Extensive experiments on several cryptocurrency benchmark datasets demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of our method over several cutting-edge methods. To our knowledge, LABRA is among the first training-free frameworks for illicit account detection in cryptocurrencies, delivering robust performance without resorting to any learnable parameters or iterative model optimization.
FULLLENS: Reliability-Aware Stock Prediction via LLM-Extracted Priors and News-Driven Semantic Graphs
Hao Zhou (The University of Edinburgh) · Tiejun Ma (The University of Edinburgh) · Luis Felipe Costa Sperb (Kingston Business School)
Abstract
Predicting stock returns requires modeling persistent company relations and time-varying market signals. Graph Neural Network (GNN) approaches combine static priors with dynamic relational graphs, but treat every extracted edge as a trustworthy binary fact, ignoring heterogeneous reliability across relational sources. We propose LENS (LLM-Extracted priors and News-driven Semantics), a static–dynamic graph framework for stock return prediction and ranking that models relational reliability as a first-class signal across the pipeline. On the static side, we extract a multi-relational company graph from a Large Language Model and aggregate it over multiple runs with confidence weighting to downweight low-consistency edges. On the dynamic side, we build a news-driven semantic graph with exponential-decay temporal aggregation to capture changing market context under uneven coverage. A context-dependent gated fusion module rebalances the two graphs at the per-stock, per-day level. On S&P 500, LENS improves AR@5 by 16.4% and SR@5 by 22.6% over the strongest baseline, and on NASDAQ 100 it achieves comparable improvements (15.5% and 20.9% respectively). Ablations isolate each component's contribution, and a human-validation study of sampled relations supports that the aggregation is grounded, providing evidence that reliability-aware LLM relations and news-based semantic graphs carry complementary information for graph-based financial prediction.
