FULLFedMem: Memory-Aware Federated Continual Learning via Dual-Channel Memory Control
Shiyang Li (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yuan Ma (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Weining Weng (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yuchen Liu (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Qianzhong Chen (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yiqiang Chen (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yang Gu (Beijing Key Laboratory for Multimodal Collaboration and Advanced Application, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Federated continual learning (FCL) suffers from complex spatio-temporal catastrophic forgetting, driven by distribution drift along task streams and aggregation conflicts under non-IID client data. Existing studies often treat temporal and spatial forgetting as decoupled objectives, overlooking their interaction in the overall memory dynamics of the federation, where client-side acquisition and server-side consolidation jointly shape long-term performance. Motivated by the structural and functional correspondence between the dual-channel memory mechanism in collective cognition and FCL's client-server collaboration, we introduce Federated System Memory (FSM), a system memory metric that jointly models client-side short-term retention and server-side long-term consistency. Based on FSM, we further propose FedMem, a memory-aware FCL framework that utilizes dual-channel memory control to enable system-level closed-loop optimization. On the client side, FedMem constrains local learning with dual-channel decay indicators: short-term decay strengthens prototype-based retention, while long-term decay enhances memory-guided regularization for stable task-memory retrieval. On the server side, it regulates global updates through collective-consistency gated aggregation and adaptive update scaling based on long-term decay, while maintaining global prototypes and memory. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedMem consistently outperforms existing methods in both learning performance and system memory retention.
FULLProRC: Prototype Personalization with Reliability Calibration in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
Yanchao Tang (Guangdong University of Technology) · Baoyao Yang (Guangdong University of Technology) · Yuhao Chen (Guangdong University of Technology) · Chenxiang Zhao (Guangdong University of Technology)
Abstract
Prototype-based federated learning (FL) provides a promising route for federated heterogeneity. By exchanging class prototypes rather than model parameters, it provides class-level semantic guidance under non-IID data and accommodates heterogeneous client backbones. Under severely skewed label distributions, however, two coupled limitations emerge. The broadcast global prototype is a cross-client average, and direct adoption can cause client semantic dilution. Meanwhile, local prototypes of rare classes are estimated from a few samples, leading to local margin erosion against well-supported neighbours. To address both, we propose ProRC, a prototype personalization framework grounded in shrinkage estimation. ProRC replaces naive alignment with a reliability-calibrated, margin-aware interpolation between global and local prototypes, and comprises two complementary client-side modules. The first module, Reliability-Calibrated Prototype Adaptation (RaPA), calibrates each global prototype by the reliability of its local counterpart, restoring client-specific semantics only to the extent the data warrant. The second module, Margin-Aware Prototype Refinement (MaPR), audits the candidate against the local true-class margin and attenuates margin-reducing steps. Together, the two modules are designed to mitigate client semantic dilution and local margin erosion, while preserving the prototype-exchange protocol and per-round payload of prior methods. Extensive experiments on label-skewed and real-world image benchmarks, together with ablation and reliability analyses, show that ProRC achieves the best overall average accuracy among the compared methods and improves the strongest prototype baseline in most heterogeneous settings.
FULLProgressive Collaboration Pruning for Federated Learning
Siyao Cheng (Beihang university) · Boyi Liu (Beihang University) · Zimu Zhou (City University of Hong Kong) · Zheng Wu (Beihang University) · Yongxin Tong (Beihang University)
Abstract
Collaboration-based personalized federated learning (Co-PFL) mitigates data heterogeneity by enabling clients to selectively exchange knowledge through a learned collaboration graph. Despite their success, existing Co-PFL methods often update collaboration weights mainly from pairwise similarity, which can produce graphs that are either overly sparse and hinder knowledge propagation or overly dense and weaken personalization, leaving graph connectivity largely uncontrolled. In this paper, we propose FedPGP, a Co-PFL framework that explicitly schedules collaboration from dense to sparse over training rounds, enabling clients to first exploit broadly shared knowledge and then refine specialized knowledge aligned with their local distributions. FedPGP builds on a connectivity-aware similarity regularization that jointly accounts for global graph connectivity and client-model similarity, together with an efficient greedy pruning rule that removes edges with the least contribution to the regularized objective. We further present FedPGP+, a module-specific extension that learns different collaboration graphs for different model modules, allowing collaboration intensity to vary along model depth. Extensive experiments across diverse non-IID settings show that FedPGP and FedPGP+ consistently outperform state-of-the-art Co-PFL baselines, achieving up to 5.52% absolute accuracy improvement, while producing interpretable dense-to-sparse collaboration schedules.
FULLFedCSOT: Model-Heterogeneous Personalized Federated Learning via Channel Semantic Optimal Transport
Yiheng Li (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Huan Zhou (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Xiuhua Li (Chongqing University) · Yuanchao Shu (Zhejiang University)
Abstract
Federated Learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative learning across distributed clients. In practical FL systems, clients often exhibit non-IID data distributions and deploy diverse model architectures under resource constraints. While model heterogeneity improves deployment flexibility under client resource constraints, it prevents direct parameter aggregation and makes cross-architecture knowledge transfer challenging. Existing methods mainly rely on shared structures, coarse-grained distillation, or projection-based feature alignment, which cannot explicitly capture channel-level semantic correspondences across heterogeneous architectures. This paper proposes FedCSOT, a model-heterogeneous personalized FL framework based on channel semantic optimal transport. FedCSOT induces sequence-driven channel semantics from channel responses over a shared unlabeled sequence, establishing a common semantic space for cross-architecture alignment. The framework models cross-architecture semantic alignment through entropy-regularized optimal transport to facilitate knowledge transfer. It further designs a divergence-aware personalized fusion strategy to adaptively balance consensus knowledge and local personalization under non-IID data distributions. Extensive experiments under diverse data and model heterogeneity settings demonstrate that FedCSOT consistently improves average test accuracy, convergence behavior, and robustness over representative baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/greenhead01/FedCSOT.
FULLDICE: Decentralized Incentive-driven Federated Learning for Efficient & Scalable Customization of Pretrained Models in Web3
Hong Lin (The State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security, Zhejiang University) · Zhongle Xie (The State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security, Zhejiang University) · Lidan Shou (The State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security, Zhejiang University) · Ke Chen (The State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security, Zhejiang University) · Gang Chen (The State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security, Zhejiang University)
Abstract
Customizing Pretrained Models (PMs) for downstream tasks demands task-specific data, which burgeoning Web3 applications provide abundantly. Blockchain-powered federated learning (BCFL) offers a secure and privacy-preserving paradigm to customize PMs among self-interested and untrusted Web3 participants. Yet, existing BCFL algorithms face severe efficiency and scalability challenges when applied to large PMs, due to their substantial computational and memory requirements and the hardware constraints of many participants. This paper introduces DICE, a novel BCFL algorithm that addresses the efficiency and scalability challenges of customizing large PMs in Web3 via two sets of synergistic techniques: (i) a dynamic progressive learning scheme and a model slice verification scheme to enable a wider range of honest participants, including those unable to deploy the full model, to engage in customizing PMs, while preserving model utility; (ii) a tree-structured committee consensus protocol and an efficiency-driven incentive scheme to address the dominant bottleneck that hinders existing BCFL algorithms from scaling to a larger number of data holders for customizing data-hungry large PMs, while maintaining security. Theoretical analysis and extensive experimental results on customizing vision and language PMs demonstrate DICE's efficiency, effectiveness, and security. A comprehensive technical report of DICE including its implementation details, extended analyses, discussions, and experiments is available at https://github.com/Hoho-Lin/DICE.
FULLRelease the Potential of Relative Feature Consistency for Data Heterogeneous Federated Learning
Yibin Wang (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yucan Zhou (College of Intelligence and Computing, Tianjin University) · Xiaoyan Gu (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Hongcheng Li (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Jiang Zhou (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Weiping Wang (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Federated Learning is a promising paradigm to achieve privacy-preserving collaborative training. However, its performance degrades severely under data heterogeneity. A main obstacle is the divergent local representations induced by data heterogeneity, which will degrade the quality of the aggregated global representations. In this paper, we discover that although local representation spaces contain client-specific biases, their internal inter-class structure remains consistent across clients, which we identify as relative consistency. Through theoretical and empirical analyses, we further show that a proxy dataset can serve as a common anchor to translate class prototypes into a relative space, where client-specific shifts are suppressed and cross-client class centers become better aligned. Based on these findings, we propose a novel framework named Federated learning with Relative Representation Alignment (FedReRA) with Relative Knowledge Extraction (RKE) and Relative Ensemble Inference (REI) to extract and leverage the relative consistency to address data heterogeneity. Specifically, RKE debiases the prototypes by translating absolute prototypes into the aligned relative space via a flexible proxy dataset, while REI conducts collaborative inference with bias-reduced prediction in the relative space. Extensive experiments validate FedReRA’s superiority over state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 3.83% average improvement under high heterogeneity and notably sustaining nearly 10% improvement on CIFAR-100 even when using random noise as the proxy data.
FULLFedEMoE: Towards Class-Aware Federated Learning via Evidential Mixture-of-Experts
Linbo Zhou (China University of Petroleum (East China)) · Weishan Zhang (China University of Petroleum (East China)) · Tao Chen (China University of Petroleum (East China)) · Lingzhao Meng (China University of Petroleum (East China))
Abstract
Federated learning under non-IID data suffers from client drift. Recent work introduces Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to handle data heterogeneity by routing inputs to specialized experts, but two problems remain. Softmax routing produces overconfident expert assignments with no reliability measure. The parameter space carries no class-level information, forcing the server to aggregate all clients uniformly and destroying the expert specialization built during local training. We call this class-level specialization invisibility. To address these problems, we propose FedEMoE. On the client side, Evidential Mixture-of-Experts equips router and experts with evidential heads, dynamically adjusts the number of active experts based on routing uncertainty, and compresses accumulated evidence into a per-client signature. On the server side, Evidence-Guided Class-Aware Aggregation takes the signatures as input and adaptively performs class-aware parameter fusion and component recombination. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and FEMNIST show that FedEMoE consistently outperforms eight baseline methods across all settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/Stephen-Chow1/FedEMoE-CIKM.
FULLWhen Geometry Becomes Unreliable: Robust Federated Aggregation via Bounded Influence
Yitong Ma (Jilin University) · Gang Yan (Jilin University)
Abstract
Robust aggregation in federated learning is often framed as down-weighting abnormal client updates. However, in realistic cross-device regimes, each round observes only a small number of high-dimensional updates, while benign updates can already be anisotropic, heavy-tailed, and strongly affected by non-IID data. In this setting, robustness depends not only on the final weighting rule, but also on whether the server-visible update geometry is estimable. We propose FedBIG (Federated Bounded-Influence Geometry), a server-side aggregation framework that separates geometry construction from influence control. Instead of scoring raw updates directly, FedBIG builds a stabilized sketch-space geometry using robust centering, low-dimensional projection, calibrated scatter estimation, shrinkage, and whitening. It then maps stabilized deviations to bounded-influence weights and aggregates the original client updates. Experiments on heterogeneous federated learning benchmarks show that FedBIG improves the robustness–utility trade-off under statistical and triggered poisoning. Ablations, boundary stress tests, and runtime analysis further support the central claim: robust aggregation is effective when server-visible geometry is estimable, and weakens when this geometry collapses under extreme heterogeneity or sparse participation. Our code is available at https://github.com/ytma-phoenix/FedBIG.
1H · Query Processing & Database SystemsFull ResearchStudio 3Monday 10:30 – 12:308 talksChair: Tracy King (Adobe)
FULLOperation-Guided Schema Evolution and Migration for Document Databases
Yu Zhuang (University of Science and Technology Beijing) · Wendi Du (University of Science and Technology Beijing) · Xi Guo (University of Science and Technology Beijing) · Qi Zhang (University of Science and Technology Beijing) · Cheng Xu (University of Science and Technology Beijing) · Jie He (University of Science and Technology Beijing) · Xiaotong Zhang (University of Science and Technology Beijing)
Abstract
Document databases provide flexible data modeling, but long-running applications still rely on implicit schemas that evolve continuously. Legacy documents do not automatically follow schema changes, so a collection may contain documents conforming to different historical schema versions. This makes schema evolution an execution problem that spans change representation, operation reconstruction, and legacy-data migration. Existing studies typically address these tasks separately, leaving schema-level changes disconnected from the instance-level migration decisions. This paper proposes an operation-guided framework for executable schema evolution and migration in document databases. We first define a unified operation framework over field paths, types, and constraints, with explicit User-Defined Function (UDF) contracts for destructive changes. This framework specifies the valid operations from which schema evolution sequences are composed. We then reconstruct executable schema evolution sequences from schema snapshots through a two-stage method that combines multi-channel field-evolution association with instruction-tuned sequence generation. Finally, the generated sequences drive progressive migration: an instance-level Benefit–Cost Optimization (BCO) selector prioritizes affected documents, while a window-level allocator distributes migration budget under live workloads. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework directly expresses all 32 curated evolution cases, improves end-to-end sequence executability by 29.44%–31.51%, and reduces residual migration debt by 24.73% over the strongest adaptive migration baseline.
FULLAligning Predicates with Database Content: A Type-Specific Query Reformulation Framework for Database Semantic Gaps
Shiwen Wu (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology) · Wen Hua (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University) · Yao Chen (Inspur Cloud Information Technology Co., Ltd.) · Jiao Xue (Inspur Cloud Information Technology Co., Ltd.) · Xue Xiao (Inspur Cloud Information Technology Co., Ltd.) · Jingzhi Fang (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology) · Yue Pang (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology) · Xiaofang Zhou (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Filtering textual columns based on user intent is a pervasive task in database applications, yet discrepancies between user predicates and concrete database values often cause keyword searches to fail. The Recall-Then-Verify (RTV) paradigm, which first retrieves a budget of candidate values and then verifies them using Large Language Models (LLMs), has emerged as a promising and widely adopted strategy; however, its overall efficacy remains inherently bounded by the recall of the initial retrieval stage. To improve this recall, we propose a type-specific query reformulation framework that adaptively aligns predicates with database content by addressing database semantic gaps. Specifically, the framework categorizes these semantic discrepancies into three distinct types—synonymy, conceptual hierarchies, and format inconsistencies—and executes a specialized, type-specific reformulation strategy tailored to each gap. The framework further grounds reformulation in the target database by reusing LLM-verified column values as feedback, enabling the system to capture database-local variants. Furthermore, to maintain low latency, it introduces an on-demand triggering mechanism that activates LLM reformulation only when a significant semantic gap is detected, supplemented by adaptive selection and early stopping strategies to prune redundant computation. Compared to existing RTV methods, experimental results demonstrate that the framework consistently enhances retrieval recall by up to 45.45% and improves end-to-end F1 score by up to 26.72%.
FULLThe Backbone of Consistent Query Answering
Antonio Morgado (IST/INESC-ID) · Jordi Planes (University of Lleida) · Alexey Ignatiev (Monash University) · Joao Marques-Silva (ICREA and University of Lleida)
Abstract
The existence of inconsistencies in databases has motivated the study of Consistent Query Answering (CQA) since the 1990s. Recent work proposed the use of Maximum Satisfiability (MaxSAT) for solving CQA for concrete types of inconsistencies. This paper shows that, for the types of inconsistencies solved with MaxSAT, it is the case that CQA corresponds to finding the backbone of a propositional formula. This observation not only yields a novel characterization in terms of the computational complexity of the problem, but it also enables significantly more efficient practical solutions. The experiments confirm that significant performance improvements can be obtained by computing the backbone instead of solving MaxSAT.
FULLBounded-Memory Aggregate Query Processing on Streaming Temporal Graphs
Tianyi Gao (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Hongchao Qin (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Haotian Jiang (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Guang Zeng (Ant Group) · Rong-Hua Li (Beijing Institute of Technology)
Abstract
Time-window aggregate queries over temporal graph streams—COUNT, COUNT_DISTINCT, and label-filtered predicates—are central to agent memory, communication monitoring, and knowledge-base analytics, yet exact evaluation becomes increasingly costly as timestamped edges accumulate. Sketch-based approximate query processing (AQP) offers compact summaries, but the standard per-bucket design couples temporal resolution with cardinality state: placing a HyperLogLog (HLL) inside every Count-Min Sketch (CMS) bucket leaves only coarse time partitions under a fixed budget and still does not natively support all three query types. We present the Cardinality-Aware Multi-Resolution Sketch (CAMRS), a budget-decoupled multi-resolution sketch built on the observation that CMS and HLL have distinct budget elasticities. CAMRS separates fine-grained CMS buckets from coarse HLL segments, achieving a 9.6× temporal-resolution gain under the same 1 MB budget, and augments each bucket with Space-Saving label tracking to support predicate queries without global label thresholds. We further derive a closed-form COUNT error bound showing that temporal resolution, rather than CMS width, is the dominant accuracy lever; this bound drives a reliability-aware fallback mechanism that controls tail risk when predicted sketch error exceeds a user tolerance. Experiments on six real-world temporal graphs (60K–17.8M edges) show that CAMRS reduces COUNT error by up to 29.7× and predicate error by up to 7.9× over the coupled baseline while preserving native COUNT_DISTINCT support. The adaptive fallback policy further reduces worst-case tail error by up to 667×.
FULLRewriting Ontology-Mediated Property Graph Queries into GQL
Bianca Löhnert (University of Salzburg) · Nikolaus Augsten (University of Salzburg) · Cem Okulmus (Paderborn University) · Magdalena Ortiz (TU Wien)
Abstract
Ontology-based data access is intended for graph data, but practical support remains limited to SQL-like languages lacking the navigational and path-matching features fundamental to graph querying. Theoretical algorithms for navigational queries have long been available. Still, they have never been implemented, largely because practical graph query languages fell short of their theoretical counterparts and lacked the expressive power needed to support rewriting common ontology languages. The recent standardisation efforts around GQL and SQL/PGQ finally allow us to overcome this barrier and present a practical query rewriting technique for ontology-mediated navigational graph queries. Ontologies are written in a DL-Lite variant tuned to property graphs, and the queries in a GQL fragment with nested two-way regular path queries and which can be evaluated in Cypher. Preliminary experiments with our proof-of-concept prototype suggest that querying graph data with ontological knowledge may finally be within reach.
FULLPath-Aware GQL Triggers for Property Graphs
Francesco Invernici (Politecnico di Milano) · Amedeo Pachera (Lyon 1 University, CNRS Liris) · Francesco Cambria (Politecnico di Milano) · Stefania Dumbrava (ENSIIE, INRIA, IRIF, SAMOVAR) · Riccardo Tommasini (INSA Lyon) · Andrea Mauri (Lyon 1 University) · Andrea Colombo (Politecnico di Milano) · Anna Bernasconi (Politecnico di Milano) · Angela Bonifati (Lyon 1 University, CNRS Liris, IUF) · Stefano Ceri (Politecnico di Milano)
Abstract
As property graphs become central to domains like network analysis, legislative and financial monitoring, there is an urgent need for reactive processing capabilities that can respond to complex structural changes. At the same time, the standardization of property graph processing has culminated in the ISO Graph Query Language (GQL) standard, which establishes a uniform and portable foundation for expressing triggers, ensuring portability across implementations. This paper introduces GQL-Triggers, the first trigger framework fully aligned with the ISO GQL standard that treats paths as first-class citizens. Unlike traditional approaches, GQL-Triggers allow developers to define declarative events, conditions, and actions over complex path patterns, incorporating GQL-specific features. We provide a formal semantic model for path-level event detection and transition sets computation. We present two alternative implementations of GQL-Triggers on top of Neo4j, respectively named Index-based and Query-based, and provide their experimental comparison in terms of time and memory efficiency.
FULLCimos: Cost-Effective Multi-Query Oriented Continuous Subgraph Matching
Ziqi Zou (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Kangfei Zhao (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Qiyan Li (The Chinese University of Hong Kong) · Zhiwei Zhang (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Lizhong Ding (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Xuefeng Zhao (China Mobile Jiutian Research) · Peng Wu (China Mobile Jiutian Research)
Abstract
Continuous subgraph matching over dynamic graphs is a fundamental problem in graph databases, with broad applications in real-time pattern monitoring and risk control. In practice, applications often require monitoring multiple graph patterns simultaneously, making multi-query oriented continuous subgraph matching (MCSM) an increasingly important research topic. Although existing methods have achieved performance gains, their indexes offer limited filtering power and they lack high-quality query plans tailored to the multi-query setting. To address these limitations, we propose Cimos, a novel index-based framework for cost-effective MCSM. First, we design a data-centric index called DCL that serves multiple query graphs and prunes more non-candidate vertices by jointly considering the matching constraints of ancestor and descendant vertices in query DAGs. Second, we adopt a hybrid-order planning strategy that separates the query plan into static and dynamic ordering components. For the static component, we introduce a prefix order tree to extract isomorphic subgraphs shared across query graphs, and optimize vertex orderings using statistical upper-bound obtained via DCL-based subgraph sampling. For the dynamic component, we employ DCL-based cardinality estimation to adaptively determine vertex orderings during the matching process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Cimos achieves notable speedup of more than 4.2x against state-of-the-art CSM and MCSM methods.
FULLBLADE: A Bit-Level Learned Architecture for Dynamic Environments
Zhenfei Wang (Zhengzhou University) · Ruojia Liu (Zhengzhou University) · Pengyu Pan (Zhengzhou University) · Liying Zhang (Zhengzhou University) · Haixia Li (Zhengzhou University)
Abstract
Learned indexes have significantly improved the query performance of in-memory databases by transforming traditional structural traversals into cumulative distribution function model predictions. However, existing dynamic learned indexes rely heavily on the core assumption of "local linear data distribution." Under highly skewed dynamic workloads in real-world scenarios, this linear assumption frequently fails, forcing the system to trigger extremely expensive model retraining and horizontal data shifting. This incurs severe cascading splits and leads to a sharp degradation in dynamic write throughput. To break this architectural bottleneck, this paper proposes BLADE, a bit-level learned index architecture designed for dynamic mixed workloads. BLADE abandons the strong reliance on complex mathematical models and achieves a structural decoupling of routing addressing and underlying data storage at the physical level. In the upper routing module, BLADE employs a pure integer bitwise partitioning mechanism for stateless memory addressing, eliminating the overhead of floating-point model computation. In the underlying leaf nodes, the system inherits the contiguous array layout with reserved gaps to absorb insertions efficiently. To address local congestion caused by data skew, BLADE introduces a vertical splitting strategy, which redistributes data by extending the routing level downwards, effectively avoiding large-scale physical data copying at the bottom layer. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that under read-only and read-heavy workloads, BLADE achieves point lookup throughput of 8.2×, 4.1×, 3.2×, and 1.3× that of B+-trees, PGM-index, ART, and ALEX, respectively. Under high-frequency write dynamic mixed workloads, its throughput reaches up to 4.5×, 4.0×, 2.3×, and 1.2× that of PGM-index, B+ Tree, ART, and ALEX. Furthermore, by replacing learned internal-node models with deterministic bitwise routing, BLADE eliminates the iterative model fitting overhead, accelerating the index initialization and bulk-loading speed by 16× to 48.8× compared to the most advanced learned indexes. Under the tested skewed insertion patterns, BLADE's maximum observed RSS is only 1.17× that of its Uniform baseline. Parameter-sensitivity experiments further validate the default 30% target gap and 16 MiB maximum leaf capacity as a balanced configuration for insertion performance and space efficiency.

2A · Industrial Recommender Systems IIApplied ResearchTeatro StudioMonday 16:00 – 18:0012 talksChair: Fedelucio Narducci (Politecnico di Bari)
APPLIEDHigh Fidelity Textual User Representation over Heterogeneous Sources via Reinforcement Learning
Rajat Arora (Linkedin) · Ye Tao (LinkedIn) · Jianqiang Shen (Linkedin) · Ping Liu (Linkedin) · Muchen Wu (Linkedin) · Qianqi Shen (Linkedin) · Benjamin Le (LinkedIn) · Fedor Borisyuk (LinkedIn) · Jingwei Wu (Linkedin) · Wenjing Zhang (Linkedin)
Abstract
Effective personalization on large-scale job platforms requires modeling members based on heterogeneous textual sources, including profiles, professional data, and search activity logs. As recommender systems increasingly adopt Large Language Models (LLMs), creating unified, interpretable, and concise representations from heterogeneous sources becomes critical, especially for latency-sensitive online environments. In this work, we propose a novel Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework to synthesize a unified textual representation for each member. Our approach leverages implicit user engagement signals (e.g., clicks, applies) as the primary reward to distill salient information. Additionally, the framework is complemented by rule-based rewards that enforce formatting and length constraints. Extensive experiments across multiple LinkedIn products serving one of the world’s largest job platforms demonstrate significant improvements in key downstream business metrics. This work provides a practical, labeling-free, and scalable solution for constructing interpretable user representations that are directly compatible with LLM-based systems.
APPLIEDBeyond End-to-End: A Low-Latency, Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Thought for Scalable and Explainable Industrial Recommendation
Wanjie Tao (Mashang Consumer Finance Co., Ltd) · Zhumei Gou (Alibaba Group) · Zulong Chen (Alibaba Group) · Qun Dai (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Quan Lu (Mashang Consumer Finance Co., Ltd) · Ning Jiang (Mashang Consumer Finance Co., Ltd)
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide semantic reasoning for recommendation, but direct LLM invocation is incompatible with the latency, stability, and reliability requirements of industrial ranking systems. We propose RA-CoT (Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Thought), a deployment-oriented framework that uses LLM-derived structured reasoning without replacing the production CTR/CVR backbone or placing LLM inference on the blocking serving path. RA-CoT asynchronously generates schema-constrained CoT-derived representations from pre-impression behavior summaries, caches them with validity checks, and falls back to the backbone when no valid reasoning vector is available. Valid reasoning is injected through an availability-aware gated residual module as bounded logit-space compensation, making the LLM signal reusable, safely ignorable, and compatible with millisecond-level serving. We evaluate RA-CoT on a large-scale industrial advertising dataset and a public recommendation benchmark, and deploy it in a two-week online A/B test. RA-CoT yields modest but consistent offline ranking improvements across DNN, DIEN, BST, and SIM backbones. In production, it improves CTR by 2.48%, CVR by 1.95%, and RPM by 2.12%, while keeping P99 serving latency at 54 ms. These results show a practical path for using cached and bounded LLM-derived structured reasoning in industrial recommender systems.
APPLIEDLarge Language Model as Universal Retriever in Industrial-Scale Recommender System
Junguang Jiang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Yanwen Huang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Bin Liu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Xiaoyu Kong (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Xinhang Li (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Ziru Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Han Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jian Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Bo Zheng (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
In real-world recommender systems, different retrieval objectives are typically addressed using task-specific datasets with carefully designed model architectures. We demonstrate that Large Language Models (LLMs) can function as universal retrievers, capable of handling multiple objectives within a generative retrieval framework. To address the model expressiveness and inference efficiency issues of generative retrieval, we propose multi-query representation and transferable discriminative mapping layers to model complex user-item relationships, and incorporate probabilistic sampling to reduce computation costs. Finally, our Universal Retrieval Model (URM) can adaptively generate a set from tens of millions of candidates based on an arbitrary given objective while keeping the latency within tens of milliseconds. Applied to industrial-scale data, URM outperforms expert models elaborately designed for different retrieval objectives in offline experiments and achieves a 3.13% revenue increase on our online advertising platform. URM also demonstrates strong performance in impression and GMV for long-tail and cold-start items.
APPLIEDHiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent
Yunsheng Pang (Tencent) · Zijian Liu (Tencent) · Yudong Li (Tencent) · Shaojie Zhu (Tencent) · Zijian Luo (Sun Yat-sen University) · Chenyun Yu (Sun Yat-sen University) · Sikai Wu (Tencent) · Shichen Shen (Tencent) · Cong Xu (Tencent) · Bin Wang (Tencent) · Kai Jiang (Tencent) · Chengxiang Zhuo (Tencent) · Zang Li (Tencent)
Abstract
Slate recommendation, which presents users with a ranked item list in a single display, is ubiquitous across mainstream online platforms. While recent generative recommendation methods have shown strong potential in modeling item sequences with semantic IDs, directly applying them to industrial-scale slate recommendation faces a fundamental disconnect: entangled SID spaces confound high-level list planning, fine-grained autoregressive decoding over long sequences limits semantic planning efficiency, and token-level objectives misalign with holistic slate quality. In this paper, we propose HiGR, an industrial-scale hierarchical generative framework for slate recommendation that bridges this disconnect through a co-designed pipeline. First, HiGR learns structured SIDs via a Prefix-Contrastive Residual Quantized VAE (PCRQ-VAE). By enforcing high-level prefixes to capture shared semantics, PCRQ-VAE creates a controllable discrete space that acts as a prerequisite for efficient planning. Leveraging this structured space, our Hierarchical Slate Decoder (HSD) shifts autoregressive modeling from entangled token-level decoding to coarse-grained preference embeddings. This design significantly reduces inference latency while allowing explicit global slate structure planning. Finally, this stable planning space enables an ORPO-based listwise alignment mechanism to optimize triple-objective implicit feedback—ranking fidelity, genuine user interest, and diversity. Extensive offline experiments show that HiGR outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by over 10% in offline recommendation quality while achieving a 5× inference speedup. Online A/B tests on Tencent platforms further improve average watch time by 1.22% and average video views by 1.73%. HiGR has been deployed on multiple Tencent platform surfaces (e.g., news, videos, and web novels), serving hundreds of millions of users and proving its industrial-scale applicability.
APPLIEDDecoupled Temporal Encoding for Generative Recommendation
Pengfei Jia (Rajax Network Techology (Taobao Shangou of Alibaba)) · Jingjian Wang (Rajax Network Techology (Taobao Shangou of Alibaba)) · Jingmao Li (Department of Biostatistics, Yale School of Public Health) · Ge Zhang (Rajax Network Techology (Taobao Shangou of Alibaba)) · Feng Shi (Rajax Network Techology (Taobao Shangou of Alibaba))
Abstract
Positional encoding is a fundamental component of Transformer-based generative recommendation models, where user histories are modeled as autoregressive item sequences. Most positional encoding methods are inherited from natural language processing and mainly represent discrete item order. However, recommendation sequences go beyond ordered lists, as timestamps and temporal effects also shape item relations. Our work is motivated by a real-world food delivery and instant retail recommendation system, where user behavior exhibits multi-level temporal regularities, including recency effects, meal-time peaks, weekday-weekend shifts, and promotion-driven traffic bursts. Existing methods partially address this issue through timestamp features, interval embeddings, decay functions, or attention biases, but they usually inject heterogeneous temporal signals through a unified representation or a single modeling pathway, making it difficult to distinguish broad temporal dynamics from local order cues. To address this limitation, we propose Decoupled Temporal Encoding (DTE), a lightweight framework for generative recommendation. DTE separates temporal dynamics from order information through two complementary modules: a personalized macro-temporal module that injects compact temporal primitives into item embeddings, and a time-gated micro-sequential module that introduces relative-order bias only when interactions are temporally dense. DTE is also parameter-efficient and deployment-friendly, allowing easy integration into existing systems. Offline experiments on public and industrial datasets demonstrate DTE’s superior performance. Online A/B tests further show improvements of +1.8% Click-through Rate (CTR) and +3.0% Revenue Per Mille (RPM) with only +0.3% serving latency overhead over the baseline positional encoding scheme. DTE has been deployed to the full Shangou ad recommendation traffic in the Taobao App since January 2026, highlighting the practical value of decoupling macro-temporal context from sequential order in real-world generative recommendation.
APPLIEDLASER: Label-Anchored Semantic Encoding with Multimodal-Collaborative Signals Harmonization for Generative Recommendation
Shiyu Song (Hangzhou Dianzi University) · Xiaofei Ding (NetEase Fuxi AI lab) · Jie Gao (Hangzhou Dianzi University) · Yile Liang (NetEase Fuxi AI lab) · Dongjing Wang (Hangzhou Dianzi University) · Xudong Shen (NetEase Fuxi AI Lab) · Xin Zhang (Hangzhou Dianzi University) · Tangjie Lv (NetEase Fuxi AI lab) · Runze Wu (NetEase Fuxi AI Lab)
Abstract
Generative recommendation has emerged as a transformative approach in industrial-scale systems, yet faces critical challenges in production environments, including Semantic Drift/Gap and cold start, and preference inconsistency. As NetEase's game platform serving more than 6 Million users, we identified that hash ID-based generative models suffer 84.6% performance degradation on the 60% long-tail items that generate minimal revenue but are crucial for user retention. Although multimodal content features could enrich item representations via semantic IDs, extracting and storing them can be tens of times higher than compact semantic IDs. Moreover, existing semantic IDs can be inconsistent with collaborative signals in industrial scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose LASER, a Label-Anchored Semantic Encoding with Multimodal-Collaborative Signals Harmonization for Industrial-Scale Generative Recommendation. LASER introduces two novel components: (1) Multimodal Semantic ID Learning, which constructs semantic IDs from multimodal features and aligns them with collaborative signals, via label-driven residual quantization and Swing-weighted pairwise alignment; and (2) Preference-aligned generative sequential recommendation, which leverages hierarchical semantic IDs to improve robustness under sparse interactions and cold-start, via popularity-aware fusion and preference-aligned autoregressive training. We conduct extensive experiments on real-world datasets and industrial scenarios to demonstrate the effectiveness of our model.
APPLIEDTlow: Flow-based Item Tokenizer for Recommendation
Nian Li (Tsinghua University) · Chonggang Song (Tencent Inc.) · Jingtao Ding (Tsinghua University) · Lingling Yi (Tencent Inc.) · Yong Li (Tsinghua University) · Qingmin Liao (Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University)
Abstract
Item tokenizer encodes semantic embeddings into token IDs to replace the randomly assigned item IDs used in traditional recommendation models, fundamentally addressing the problems of excessive parameters and cold starts. However, the most common tokenizer, RQ-VAE, suffers from low decoding efficiency due to the inherent dependencies among its codebooks. Meanwhile, efficient independent tokenizers such as optimized product quantization (OPQ) still struggle with dimensional correlations and distribution complexity of semantic embeddings. In this work, we propose a flow-based item Tokenizer (Tlow) to transform raw semantic embeddings into a latent space where embeddings conform to a unified standard normal distribution, achieving dual advantages of dimensional independence and distributional simplicity. Independent tokenization performed on these latent embeddings yields semantically clear token IDs. Additionally, we introduce a novel codebook guidance to align the codebook space with the token embedding space, further aiding the learning of more semantically distinct token embeddings. Offline experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that Tlow's tokenization and codebook guidance significantly improve recommendation performance. The improvement on cross-domain and multi-modal recommendations also proves the effectiveness of item tokenization in a simplified embedding space. Online experiments for a multi-modal retrieval task on China's largest social media platform WeChat validate Tlow's powerful distribution transformation capability. The retrieval model based on token IDs improves user CTR by 10.32% globally and by 11.64% for new items. Our codes are available at https://github.com/wjjln/Tlow.
APPLIEDLEMUR: Large scale End-to-end MUltimodal Recommendation
Xintian Han (ByteDance) · Honggang Chen (ByteDance) · Quan Lin (ByteDance) · Jingyue Gao (ByteDance) · Xiangyuan Ren (ByteDance) · Lifei Zhu (ByteDance) · Zhisheng Ye (ByteDance) · Shikang Wu (ByteDance) · Xionghang Xie (ByteDance) · Xiaochu Gan (ByteDance) · Bingzheng Wei (ByteDance) · Peng Xu (ByteDance) · Zhe Wang (ByteDance) · Yuchao Zheng (ByteDance) · Jingjian Lin (ByteDance) · Di Wu (ByteDance) · Junfeng Ge (ByteDance)
Abstract
Traditional ID-based recommender systems often struggle with cold-start and generalization challenges. Multimodal recommendation systems, which leverage textual and visual data, offer a promising solution to mitigate these issues. However, existing industrial approaches typically adopt a two-stage training paradigm: first pretraining a multimodal model, then applying its frozen representations to train the recommendation model. This decoupled framework suffers from misalignment between multimodal learning and recommendation objectives, as well as an inability to adapt dynamically to new data. To address these limitations, we propose LEMUR, the first large-scale multimodal recommender system trained end-to-end from raw data. By jointly optimizing both the multimodal and recommendation components, LEMUR ensures tighter alignment with downstream objectives while enabling real-time parameter updates. Constructing multimodal sequential representations from user history often entails prohibitively high computational costs. To alleviate this bottleneck, we propose a novel memory bank mechanism that incrementally accumulates historical multimodal representations throughout the training process. In a 14-day online A/B test on Douyin Search, LEMUR has led to a significant 0.843% reduction in query change rate decay, a 0.558% increase in staytime and a 0.81% improvement in QAUC. Additionally, LEMUR has shown significant gains across key online or offline metrics for Douyin Advertisement, Tiktok Search and Ecom Search. Our results validate the superiority of end-to-end multimodal recommendation in real-world industrial scenarios.
APPLIEDNative Multimodal Representation Learning for Click-Through Rate Prediction in E-Commerce Scenarios
Chao Yi (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Feifan Yang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jiawei Feng (University of Science and Technology of China) · Sishuo Chen (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Zhangming Chan (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Xiang-Rong Sheng (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Han Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
Multimodal representations have been widely adopted in industrial e-commerce recommendation systems. Due to their strong semantic understanding and generalization capabilities, they enhance the performance of traditional sparse ID-based Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction models. Current multimodal application frameworks in the CTR prediction task typically follow a two-stage paradigm: first, pre-training a multimodal encoder on data from specific recommendation scenarios; second, extracting items' multimodal representations using this pre-trained multimodal encoder and integrating them into the CTR prediction model. However, the training objectives and data distribution of multimodal pre-training tasks often differ from those of the CTR prediction task, which limits the effectiveness of multimodal representation on downstream tasks. In this paper, we focus on how to learn Native Multimodal Representation for the CTR prediction task. One intuitive solution is to jointly train the multimodal encoder and CTR model end-to-end on the CTR task, with the expectation that the encoder can automatically learn downstream-relevant knowledge. However, we find that the end-to-end training does not bring performance improvements to existing multimodal application paradigms. Our analysis reveals that user behaviors in raw CTR data are driven by both multimodal semantics and non-multimodal factors, leading to ambiguous supervision and inconsistent encoder updates. To address this, we propose a Mine-Then-Train method that mines high-quality, multimodally interpretable training samples from CTR data and uses them to fine-tune the multimodal encoder for better alignment with user click preferences. Offline and online experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
APPLIEDBasisLTV: Ordinal-Guided Basis Reconstruction for Long-Tailed Lifetime Value Prediction via Semantic Behavior Compression
Xiaoqi Bai (Nanjing University) · Shuaiqi Chen (Bilibili Inc.) · Chun Tang (Hohai University) · Guodong Liu (Bilibili Inc.) · Lei Wang (Bilibili Inc.)
Abstract
The zero-inflated and extreme long-tailed nature of Lifetime Value (LTV) data poses a dilemma for existing methods: ranking-oriented methods lack fine-grained value estimation, while regression-oriented methods struggle to converge in high-variance spaces. We propose BasisLTV, a novel framework that integrates efficient semantic representation with robust value reconstruction. To address feature sparsity and computational bottlenecks, we introduce Efficient Semantic Behavior Compression. This mechanism compresses high-dimensional attribute tuples into compact, attribute-aware behavior representations, enriching input context while maintaining low inference costs. Building on this, BasisLTV tackles long-tailed regression via Ordinal-Guided Basis Reconstruction. Specifically, it imposes macro-constraints through ordinal classification and reconstructs micro-values using interval basis vectors. Furthermore, a Null-Space Constraint is introduced, leveraging a null-space vector strictly orthogonal to the reconstruction basis to decouple out-of-interval noise. Experiments on both a real-world industrial dataset of 10 million users and a public benchmark demonstrate that BasisLTV significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both ranking and regression metrics. Furthermore, online A/B testing verifies its robust efficacy and significant practical value in a real-world advertising system.
APPLIEDChoirRec: Semantic User Grouping via LLMs for Conversion Rate Prediction of Low-Activity Users
Dakai Zhai (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jiong Gao (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Boya Du (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Ning Tang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Junwei Xu (Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University) · Qijie Shen (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jialin Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Yuning Jiang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
Accurately predicting conversion rates (CVR) for low-activity users remains a fundamental challenge in large-scale e-commerce recommender systems. For these users, existing approaches face three critical limitations: (i) data dominated by high-activity users may introduce noisy and mismatched signals for learning low-activity users' preferences; (ii) insufficient interaction information; and (iii) a systemic training bias toward high-activity users. To address these challenges, we propose ChoirRec, a novel framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify semantically similar users and transfer reliable knowledge from richer user groups to low-activity users.ChoirRec comprises three components: (i) a Semantic Group Generation module that utilizes LLMs to form reliable, cross-activity user clusters, thereby filtering out noisy signals; (ii) a Hierarchical Representation module that enriches sparse user embeddings with informative group-level priors to mitigate data insufficiency; and (iii) a Multi-granularity Module that employs a dual-channel architecture and adaptive fusion mechanism to ensure effective learning and utilization of group knowledge. We conduct extensive offline and online experiments on Taobao, a leading industrial-scale e-commerce platform. ChoirRec improves GAUC by 1.16% in offline evaluations, while online A/B testing reveals a 7.24% increase in order volume, highlighting its substantial practical value in real-world applications.
APPLIEDLIFT: A Learning-aware Intervention Framework for Cold-Start Recommendation on TikTok Live
Zhili Tang (Bytedance) · Qiyu Fang (Bytedance) · Qingyu Bing (Bytedance) · Qi Wang (Bytedance) · Yuhan Li (Bytedance) · Runze Yu (Bytedance) · Zhuang Cai (Bytedance) · Qinglei Wang (Bytedance) · Zuotao Liu (Bytedance)
Abstract
On billion-scale live streaming platforms such as TikTok, a core challenge is to distribute millions of newly initiated live streams to potential viewers. The ephemerality and real-time variability of live streams demand an aggressive and dynamic cold-start strategy to capture value within an extremely limited window. Beyond this temporal urgency, the system faces a unique challenge: a two-way interactive feedback loop in which recommendations directly influence streamer behavior and subsequent viewer feedback. Traditional methods, however, lack the ability to intervene at critical learning moments and fail to provide the active incentives needed to optimize the streamer-user feedback loop. In this paper, we propose LIFT (Learning-aware Intervention Framework for Cold-Start Recommendation on TikTok Live), a novel paradigm designed specifically for this real-time intervention. LIFT employs three adaptive modules to optimize traffic allocation throughout the cold-start phase: (1) Phase-Aware Exploration Module, which identifies optimal learning windows by analyzing the dynamics of item embeddings, enabling precisely timed exploration of live streams; (2) Incentive-Driven Interaction Module, which distills LLM-derived interaction quality signals into the recommender system to prioritize targeted streams, effectively incentivizing content-rich interaction; (3) State-Based Gating, which determines whether the current state of a live stream merits exposure within the dynamic listwise context, ensuring that interventions are both reasonable and efficient. Extensive offline and online experiments demonstrate that LIFT outperforms standard production baselines with statistically significant improvements. Since its full deployment on TikTok, the framework has achieved an evaluated 8.91 increase in live viewing duration and an observed 9.65 increase in accumulated stream duration. These results validate that our proactive, real-time intervention strategy yields effective performance, given the unique nature of live streams.
2B · Federated Recommendation & PrivacyFull ResearchSala SinopoliMonday 16:00 – 18:008 talksChair: Qi Cao (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
FULLPrivacy-Aware Representation Decoupling in Federated Recommendation against Attribute Inference Attacks
Xuhao Zhao (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Yanmin Zhu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Wenze Ma (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Qihao Luo (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Chenhao Zhai (Alibaba Group) · Chunyang Wang (East China Normal University) · Zhaobo Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Jiadi Yu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Feilong Tang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
Abstract
Federated recommender systems (FedRec) aim to preserve user privacy by keeping sensitive data on client devices and sharing only model parameters with a central server. However, FedRec is still vulnerable to attribute inference attacks (AIAs), where server-side adversaries exploit uploaded parameters to infer users’ private attributes. Existing FedRec approaches face a suboptimal privacy-performance trade-off. Privacy-focused methods mask attribute-related features in representations to protect sensitive information, but degrade recommendation accuracy. In contrast, performance-focused methods preserve accuracy by retaining these features but risk privacy leakage through uploaded representations. To balance privacy and performance, we propose PARD, a privacy-aware representation decoupling framework that explicitly decomposes representations into privacy-relevant and privacy-irrelevant components. Only the privacy-irrelevant part is uploaded to the server, and the privacy-relevant part is retained locally. We leverage Mutual Information (MI) objectives to facilitate this decoupling: (1) suppressing sensitive leakage by minimizing the MI between privacy-irrelevant representations and attributes, and (2) retaining attribute signals by maximizing the MI for privacy-relevant representations. Since exact MI computation is intractable, we derive variational bounds and estimate them using privacy estimators under adversarial and cooperative training paradigms. Experimental results demonstrate that PARD outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both recommendation accuracy and privacy preservation. The code is available at https://github.com/XuHao-bit/PARD.
FULLDynamic Feature-Embedding Communication via Codebook Distillation for Federated Recommendation
Mingzhe Han (Fudan University) · Jiahao Liu (Fudan University) · Dongsheng Li (Microsoft Research Asia) · Jiankui Zhou (Fudan University) · Yaqiong Li (Fudan University) · Hansu Gu (Independent) · Peng Zhang (Fudan University) · Ning Gu (Fudan University) · Tun Lu (Fudan University)
Abstract
Federated recommendation systems commonly protect user privacy by keeping user parameters on local devices, while exchanging item parameters for collaborative model training. However, such item parameters usually model items independently and suffer from both efficiency and effectiveness challenges, making communication costs grow with the item space and limiting cross-item generalization and robustness to noisy feedback. To address these limitations, we propose to model items via shared latent feature embeddings for communication. Residual Quantization (RQ) provides a natural way to instantiate this communication by representing each item with a short sequence of discrete code IDs, i.e., Semantic IDs (SIDs). However, directly applying centralized and static RQ-based recommendation to federated learning is non-trivial due to 1) private and biased historical interactions and 2) evolving collaborative information. We propose RQFedRec, an RQ-based federated recommendation framework for dynamic feature-embedding communication. To construct globally aligned codebooks without accessing private interactions, RQFedRec introduces an information distillation module. Each client first learns item embeddings that encode local collaborative information from private interactions, and then distills such information into feature-indexed codebooks under globally shared SIDs, making sparse and biased local signals more compatible with server aggregation. To adapt to evolving collaborative information, RQFedRec introduces a self-refining SID update module that dynamically refines global SID assignments from aggregated codebooks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RQFedRec improves recommendation performance and reduces communication costs without relying on semantic information, while further benefiting from public semantics when available. Code is available at https://github.com/Mingzhe-Han/RQFedRec.
FULLMoSA: Multi-Modal Semantic-Anchored Feature Alignment for Federated Recommendation
Tianzi Zang (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Jiayi Sun (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Cheng Xu (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Mingyuan Gao (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Yicong Li (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Juan Li (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics)
Abstract
Federated recommendation (FedRec) suffers from sparse and highly heterogeneous interaction data, which can drive client-side item representations toward inconsistent semantic directions and cause feature conflict during aggregation. Addressing feature conflict in FedRec is non-trivial, as implicit feedback reflects user-specific preferences rather than stable item semantics, making it difficult to support prototype-based alignment as in standard FL. To address this issue, we propose MoSA, a FedRec-specific feature alignment framework that introduces multi-modal semantic anchors via item clustering. MoSA uses the resulting cluster assignments as globally consistent pseudo-labels and performs dual-level alignment: (i) a cluster-aware item representation alignment module to guide client-side item embedding matrix under partial item coverage, and (ii) a recommender modulation module to improve cross-client parameter compatibility while preserving personalization. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that MoSA consistently improves recommendation performance across representative federated recommendation backbones, and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component. The codes are available here. (https://github.com/SunJY1116/MoSA_Code.git)
FULLFedPerGen: A Personalized Generative Augmentation Framework for Federated Recommendation
Tianzi Zang (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Cheng Xu (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Jiayi Sun (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Mingyuan Gao (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Yicong Li (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Juan Li (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Wenze Ma (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
Abstract
Federated recommendation is an emerging paradigm that enables collaborative model training while preserving user privacy by keeping raw interaction data on local devices. However, in this setting, each client performs local training solely on a single user's limited historical interactions, which further exacerbates the data sparsity issue that has long been a bottleneck limiting recommendation performance. In this paper, we delve into the data sparsity problem in federated recommendation and propose FedPerGen, a personalized generative augmentation framework for federated recommendation. Specifically, each client is required to upload a user preference proxy to the server. The server then feeds this proxy along with diversity-constrained random noise into a generative network to synthesize personalized pseudo-item embeddings for each client. To ensure the informativeness and diversity of the generated embeddings, we design three complementary optimization objectives: feature-contrastive loss, model-alignment loss, and embedding-diversity loss. Furthermore, a two-stage warm-up training strategy is proposed to guarantee reliable user preference proxies and high-quality pseudo embeddings. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that FedPerGen consistently improves various federated recommendation baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/xcheng202202/FedPerGen .
FULLFedHUR: Learning Hierarchical Utility-Guided Client Relations for Personalized Federated Recommendation
Mingzhe Han (Fudan University) · Jiahao Liu (Fudan University) · Dongsheng Li (Microsoft Research Asia) · Jiankui Zhou (Fudan University) · Hansu Gu (Independent) · Peng Zhang (Fudan University) · Ning Gu (Fudan University) · Tun Lu (Fudan University)
Abstract
Federated recommendation enables collaborative model training while keeping user interaction data on local clients. A central problem in federated recommendation is how to aggregate useful information across clients for personalized recommendation. Existing personalized aggregation methods usually construct client relations from predefined parameter-based assumptions, such as parameter similarity or complementarity, and use these relations to determine aggregation weights. However, such methods construct a single global relation, which is insufficient to capture the hierarchical and multi-granularity nature of user relations in recommendation. Moreover, these predefined relations cannot directly reflect whether the related clients can improve prediction performance after aggregation. To address these limitations, we propose FedHUR, a federated recommendation framework for learning hierarchical utility-guided client relations. FedHUR takes item-item filters as the object for relation construction and aggregation. Specifically, it first aggregates and clusters each client's local information to obtain global hierarchical information. Each client computes hierarchical utility signals based on its local information and the global hierarchical information, indicating which collaborative information is useful for improving its prediction. The server uses these utility signals to retrieve clients that are useful to that client for further personalized aggregation. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets show that FedHUR consistently outperforms existing federated recommendation baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of hierarchical utility-guided client relation learning. Code is available at https://github.com/Mingzhe-Han/FedHUR.
FULLTranscending the Semantic Chasm: Knowledge-Graph Guided Aggregation for Cross-Silo Federated Session Recommendation
Changjie Wang (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Bohan Li (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Wenlong Wu (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Meng Ma (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Yuanyang Zhang (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Yuhang Dai (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Chenhui Feng (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Liang Liu (Nankai University) · Hua Dai (Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications) · Haofen Wang (TongJi University)
Abstract
Session-based Recommendation (SBR) achieves high performance in traditional centralized settings by using global item transition graphs to capture user intent. However, Federated Learning (FL) mandates collaborative training on isolated data, which makes the construction of such global structures unattainable. We identify this critical dilemma as “Structure Collapse”, where the global graph remains fragmented despite model averaging. This collapse induces a “Semantic Chasm,” resulting in incompatible knowledge fusion and imprecise intent prediction. To break this impasse, we propose a novel Cross-Silo Federated Session-based Recommendation framework (CSFSR), which reconstructs global connectivity by harmonizing knowledge priors with local intents. Specifically, our Knowledge-Aware Initialization counteracts Structure Collapse by synthesizing shared attributes into a unified semantic space that anchors isolated clients. Further addressing the Semantic Chasm, the Graph-Guided Aggregation mechanism uses client signatures to direct personalized fusion, effectively filtering noise and ensuring robustness. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that CSFSR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art federated baselines and exhibits superior noise robustness. Our code is available at https://github.com/Is-Jiejie/CSFSR.
FULLFedCGR: Federated Cross-Domain Generative Recommendation
Zhuodong Liu (Beijing Jiaotong University) · Hugen Lv (Beijing Jiaotong University) · Xiangyu Li (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Bohan Guo (University of Malaya) · Peiyu Hu (Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University)
Abstract
Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) transfers preference knowledge across related domains, but federated deployment makes cross-domain alignment difficult because the behavioral anchors that align item spaces, such as overlapping users and shared interaction signals, are often sparse, unavailable, or privacy-sensitive across clients. To address this tension, we revisit federated CDR as generation over a stable semantic item language. By representing items as discrete semantic ID (SID) sequences derived from public item-side metadata, cross-domain item alignment is induced by a shared vocabulary rather than by exchanging private interactions or aligning domain-specific embeddings. Directly federating SID-based generators, however, introduces two design constraints: the SID tokenizer must remain fixed to preserve cross-client token consistency, which creates a semantic-only bottleneck because local collaborative filtering (CF) signals cannot be globally shared or aligned; meanwhile, standard federated averaging can cause negative transfer under domain heterogeneity. To overcome these constraints, we propose FedCGR, a federated generative CDR framework that keeps the item language stable and makes adaptation explicit. FedCGR injects local CF evidence through a reliability-aware semantic interface and trains a prototype-personalized generator that selectively aggregates shared parameters according to domain relatedness while keeping domain-specific quantities local. Experiments on six Amazon cross-domain scenarios show that FedCGR consistently outperforms federated generative baselines and achieves competitive performance against strong sequential and federated CDR methods under both full-ranking and sampled evaluation protocols. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZhuodLiu/FedCGR.
FULLAn Unseen Threat in Cross-Domain Recommendation: User Re-Identification Attacks and Practical Defenses
Tianzi Zang (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Shuaijie Zhou (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) · Yicong Li (Nanjing University Of Aeronautics And Astronautics) · Juan Li (Nanjing University Of Aeronautics And Astronautics) · Wenze Ma (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) · Ji Zhang (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics)
Abstract
Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) boosts personalization by transferring knowledge across domains, but its privacy implications remain largely overlooked. In this paper, we uncover a critical threat in CDR: cross-domain user re-identification can be performed in realistic black-box settings using only the top-K recommended items returned by deployed systems. We propose a list-supervised shadow-model attack that treats the target model's top-K lists as implicit feedback and mimics its ranking behavior through a pairwise ranking objective. To amplify identity signals that persist across domains—even with disjoint item sets—the attacker learns disentangled user interests, separating domain-specific preferences from domain-invariant representations through contrastive constraints. The resulting representations support an effective classifier for determining whether two cross-domain accounts belong to the same individual. Extensive experiments across multiple CDR settings show that re-identification leakage is pervasive in modern models. Finally, we present practical defense mechanisms that mitigate linkability while preserving recommendation utility, highlighting the need for privacy-aware CDR design. The codes are available here. (https://github.com/SleepingZSJ/LiSA-Link.git)
2C · Retrieval Models & RelevanceFull ResearchSala PetrassiMonday 16:00 – 18:008 talksChair: Morteza Zihayat (Toronto Metropolitan University)
FULLSandwich Reasoning: An Answer-Reasoning-Answer Approach for Low-Latency Query Correction
Chen Zhang (Renmin University of China) · Kepu Zhang (Renmin University of China) · Jiatong Zhang (Renmin University of China) · Xiao Zhang (Renmin University of China) · Jun Xu (Renmin University of China)
Abstract
Query correction is a critical entry point in modern search pipelines, demanding high accuracy strictly within stringent latency constraints. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning improves accuracy but introduces excessive latency that limits real-time deployment. A natural alternative is to output an answer before reasoning to reduce latency; however, under autoregressive decoding, such an answer-first paradigm suffers from a decoupling problem: the early answer is generated independently of the subsequent reasoning, and therefore cannot benefit from it. To address this issue, we propose Sandwich Reasoning (SandwichR), a novel approach that explicitly aligns a fast initial answer with post-hoc reasoning, enabling low-latency query correction without sacrificing reasoning-aware accuracy. SandwichR follows an “Answer–Reasoning–Answer” paradigm, producing an initial correction, an explicit reasoning process, and a final refined correction. To align the initial answer with post-reasoning insights, we design a consistency-aware reinforcement learning (RL) strategy: a dedicated consistency reward enforces alignment between the initial and final corrections, while margin-based rejection sampling prioritizes borderline samples where reasoning drives the most impactful corrective gains. Additionally, unlike existing datasets that primarily focus on simple spelling errors, we construct a high-quality query correction dataset tailored to semantically sensitive errors. Experiments on three real-world domains show that SandwichR delivers the best accuracy-latency trade-off among evaluated methods at comparable model scale, achieving accuracy on par with standard CoT while reducing inference latency by 40–70%, and offering a promising solution for latency-sensitive applications.
FULLThe ''Curse of Knowledge'' in LLM Query Simulation: Concept Provenance for Tracing Answer-Side Intrusion
Chenglong Ma (RMIT University) · Xinye Wanyan (RMIT University) · Danula Hettiachchi (RMIT University) · Ziqi Xu (RMIT University) · Jeffrey Chan (RMIT University)
Abstract
LLM-generated search queries are widely used to augment IR evaluation, yet they may contain concepts that presuppose answer-side document knowledge, violating the information-access boundary of pre-search users. Existing validation metrics—overlap, diversity, effectiveness—cannot distinguish rare human-tail variation from candidate answer-side intrusion. We introduce concept provenance, a framework that assigns query concepts to backstory-supported, human-central, human-tail, and candidate answer-side zones, operationalizing a boundary that retrieval metrics alone cannot detect. Applying concept provenance to 77,004 queries across 100 UQV100 topics, 8 LLMs, and 5 prompt conditions with two extraction pipelines (cross-pipeline token-HCIR Spearman ρ = 1.0 over five condition means), we find candidate answer-side concepts constitute 7.40% of non-generic concepts, appearing in 97 of 100 topics with topic explaining ≈67% of variance. Human validation yields 68.2% relaxed precision, revealing a dual mechanism: knowledge intrusion (45.5%) and deployment intrusion (45.0%). The implementation is available at https://github.com/inu0104/MRP.

Static pruning is widely used to accelerate sparse neural retrieval, yet existing studies each validate their conclusions within a single custom pipeline, leaving it unclear which findings transfer to modern engines with different index organizations and dynamic pruning mechanisms. FULLTwo important things you must know! Revisiting Clickbait Detection from Perspectives of Humans' Cognition and Emotion
Changrong Min (Criminal Investigation Police University of China) · Changchun Li (Jilin University) · Jiayin Yan (Dalian University) · Bing Wang (Jilin University) · You Lu (Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology) · Ximing Li (Jilin University)
Abstract
Clickbait headlines are purposefully designed to omit crucial news information, thus evoking strong curiosity and enticing readers to click. Naturally, such heightened curiosity is typically accompanied by more diverse imaginings of the news content and stronger emotional arousal among readers. Inspired by these cognitive and affective reactions, we develop a novel clickbait detection method, entitled Clickbait Detector with Augmentation of Cognitive Imagining and Emotion Arousal (CACIA). Meanwhile, we suggest a dimensional emotion recognition (DER) task within a multi-task learning framework to estimate the emotional arousal elicited by the headline. Accordingly, clickbait headlines tend to induce more diverse imaginings and stronger emotional arousal than non-clickbait ones. These relative differences are formulated as additional training objectives, thus enabling a more effective capturing of curiosity semantics in clickbait headlines. Finally, CACIA derives discriminative clickbait features augmented by human-like imaginings and emotion knowledge. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CACIA consistently outperforms strong baseline methods.

Mohamed Ahmed (Georgetown University) · Lisa Singh (Georgetown University) · Sejin Paik (Georgetown University)
Abstract
Online platforms are increasingly shaping political communication, influencing how narratives emerge and gain traction. Unfortunately, this has led to an acceleration in the spread of false information. One way to analyze misinformation dynamics is to measure whether public discussions support or refute verified claims. However, most existing stance detection methods struggle to keep up with novel claims without retraining on new labeled data. In this paper, we extend claim-based stance detection research, explicitly focusing on generalization to unseen claim targets and model performance in-the-wild. Intuitively, this approach combines both instance-level reasoning associated with claim and post tokens and higher order reasoning associated with the stance detection task. Finally, we conduct a case study that uses our proposed model to measure the stance of voting claims on social media from the 2024 U.S. election, highlighting variations in misinformation across different voting-related themes and the benefit of our model for timely and scalable analysis of online discourse.

The source code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/PAGE.

Wenqing Wang (Soochow University) · Xi Chen (Soochow University) · Xiangmin Zhou (RMIT University) · Wei Chen (Soochow University) · Pengpeng Zhao (Soochow University) · Lei Zhao (Soochow University)
Abstract

By constructing hypothetical variations of posts, the model learns invariant propagation patterns that reflect stable causal structure rather than spurious correlations. Recent large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved strong performance on complex reasoning tasks by generating a long chain-of-thought (Long-CoT). Existing approaches to adaptive reasoning typically rely on retraining the model or designing sophisticated prompting, which are either prohibitively expensive or highly sensitive to the prompt formulation. To balance reasoning accuracy and reasoning efficiency, collaborative approaches combining long and short CoT have been widely explored. Large reasoning models (LRMs) achieve strong performance on complex reasoning tasks, but their long chain-of-thought trajectories incur substantial inference latency and computational cost. Specifically, structural criticality measures how sensitive the SLM's next-step generation is to perturbations in earlier reasoning history, and low-criticality steps are viewed as locally stable and delegated to the SLM, whereas high-criticality steps are treated as history-sensitive and routed to the LLM. The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) has created demand for faster responses and lower costs. Evaluations on diverse datasets show that while frequency based policies are strong baselines, our novel variant improves semantic accuracy.
