Jiancheng Dong (City University of Hong Kong) · Pengyue Jia (City University of Hong Kong) · Jingyu Peng (City University of Hong Kong) · Maolin Wang (City University of Hong Kong) · Yuhao Wang (City University of Hong Kong) · Lixin Su (Baidu Inc.) · Xin Sun (Baidu Inc.) · Shuaiqiang Wang (Baidu Inc.) · Dawei Yin (Baidu Inc.) · Xiangyu Zhao (City University of Hong Kong)
Abstract
Long system prompts are widely used to steer Large Language Models (LLMs), but repeatedly processing them at inference time is inefficient and consumes valuable context budget. This motivates a central question: can the behavioral effect of a long system prompt be retained using only a minimal learned representation? To enable this, we propose a lightweight training framework that learns a single Behavior-Equivalent Token ([BE]). The framework first trains [BE] to encode the semantic content of the original system prompt via reconstruction, and then distills the prompt's downstream behavior into this single token. Importantly, our method requires no update to the pretrained LLM weights, no auxiliary compression models, and no labeled responses. Empirical evaluations on three datasets show that replacing long prompts with a single [BE] token yields up to a 3000x prompt compression ratio, while retaining about 98% of the downstream performance of the original system prompts. This substantially reduces inference cost and frees nearly the entire context window for user inputs and model outputs. The implementation code is publicly available for reproduction.
FULLDATP: Training-Free Depth-Aware Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
Qingxin Liu (National University of Defense Technology) · Jinzhi Liao (National University of Defense Technology) · Xiang Zhao (National University of Defense Technology)
Abstract
The massive redundancy of visual tokens in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) creates a critical computational bottleneck during large language model (LLM) prefill. Recent training-free pruning methods provide plug-and-play acceleration, yet their pruning decisions often rely on limited visual states or delayed in-LLM signals, which may underexploit both the layer-wise evolution of visual representations and the query-specific relevance of local regions. We propose DATP (Depth-Aware Token Pruning), a training-free early-pruning framework that selects compact visual tokens before they enter the LLM. DATP combines two complementary signals: Depth-aware Layer Aggregation (DALA), which aggregates multi-layer visual saliency trajectories to construct a high-recall structural prior, and Cross-modal Attention Gating (CMAG), which introduces a lightweight prompt-conditioned relevance signal to suppress visually salient but task-irrelevant tokens. Experiments on LLaVA-v1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Qwen2.5-VL show that DATP achieves a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off under aggressive token budgets. On LLaVA-v1.5, DATP preserves 95.7% of the full-token performance while retaining only 11% of the visual tokens. Across the reported multimodal reasoning and hallucination-sensitive benchmark settings, DATP generally outperforms the evaluated training-free pruning baselines.
FULLRI-Prune: Relation and Information Aware Visual Token Pruning for Multi-Image Vision-Language Models
Dongjin Lee (Chung-Ang University) · Eunju Lee (Chung-Ang University) · Jinhee Jang (Chung-Ang University) · Yoonji Lee (Chung-Ang University) · Youngbin Kim (Chung-Ang University)
Abstract
Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have recently been extended to handle multiple input images, but this extension dramatically increases the visual token budget, making visual-token pruning not merely an efficiency option but a practical necessity. Existing visual-token pruning methods, primarily designed for the single-image setting, rely on attention-derived saliency signals to estimate per-token importance. However, this attention-centric design transfers poorly to the multi-image regime: it causes substantial performance degradation on multi-image benchmarks, suffers from strong positional bias, and loses discriminative attention signals as the number of input images increases. To test whether attention-selected tokens are truly important for multi-image reasoning, we conduct two complementary causal probes—Leave-One-In and Leave-One-Deletion—which measure token importance by restoring individual tokens to a zeroed visual sequence or removing them from the full sequence. Attention-based pruners provide only marginal gains over random selection, showing that attention is a weak proxy for visual-token importance in multi-image reasoning. Motivated by this gap, we propose Relation and Information Aware Pruning (RI-Prune), a training-free, attention-free pre-decoder selector for multi-image visual token pruning. RI-Prune scores each visual token using a z-normalized combination of three signals computed from projector outputs: query relevance, cross-image correspondence with compact per-image prototypes, and intra-image representativeness. By integrating these signals, RI-Prune performs balanced per-image Top-K selection to preserve information across input images. Across multiple multi-image benchmarks and three LVLM backbones, RI-Prune achieves a stronger trade-off between token reduction and task performance than prior pruning methods, particularly under aggressive token budgets.

FULLMKG-CARE: Case-Aware Reasoning with Multimodal Knowledge Graphs for Explainable Medical Image Diagnosis
Yiming Xu (University of Science and Technology of China) · Yixuan Liu (University of Science and Technology of China) · Yuhang Zhang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Ling Zheng (University of Science and Technology of China) · Yihan Wang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Qi Song (University of Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
Medical image diagnosis has achieved significant progress with deep learning, yet existing methods often rely on isolated visual evidence and lack the ability to effectively leverage similar cases and external knowledge. In clinical practice, diagnosis is typically supported by similar historical cases and their associated symptoms. To explicitly model this evidence-based diagnostic process, we propose MKG-CARE, a framework that performs case-aware reasoning using multimodal knowledge graphs for explainable medical image diagnosis. Specifically, we construct a case-aware multimodal knowledge graph as a structured diagnostic memory, where diseases, images, and symptoms are hierarchically organized. Given an input image, MKG-CARE adaptively retrieves similar cases from this memory and extracts their corresponding case-centered subgraphs. We further introduce a knowledge propagation and injection mechanism, where an image-centric Graph Attention Network aggregates heterogeneous semantics within the retrieved case subgraphs, followed by bidirectional cross-modal attention to align and inject the aggregated case knowledge into visual representations. To mitigate retrieval noise, we design a confidence-calibrated decision refinement scheme that estimates each retrieved case’s reliability from prediction confidence and sample similarity, and reweights its contribution to the final prediction for interpretable case-level evidence attribution. Extensive experiments on multiple medical imaging datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines, while ablation and qualitative analyses validate the effectiveness and interpretability of our method. The code is available at https://github.com/lyxuan1022/MKG-CARE.
FULLDAMEC: Disease-Aware Multi-Expert Consensus Framework for Study-Level Radiology Report Generation
Junyeong Maeng (Korea University) · Eunsong Kang (Kangwon National University) · Heung-Il Suk (Korea University)
Abstract
Radiology report generation (RRG) translates medical images into clinical reports, yet existing systems diverge from real radiological practice in three respects. First, they are formulated at the image level, consuming a single image or a fixed pair of current/prior images, and discarding the variable visual evidence within a patient study. Second, report generation flows through a single end-to-end pipeline. Even when auxiliary classifiers or retrieved priors are incorporated, they remain auxiliary inputs rather than independent sources of clinical judgment. Third, both retrieval and validation operate without a finding-level clinical anchor: retrieval falls back on image-feature similarity, while validation relies on prompt-level heuristics, leaving generated reports weakly grounded. We propose DAMEC, a Disease-Aware Multi-Expert Consensus framework that recasts RRG as study-level, clinical-context generation. Four heterogeneous experts process a variable number of images from a patient study and emit per-expert clinical signals, which a trainable disease-aware consensus module aggregates into a unified consensus. The consensus, together with disease states, uncertainty, longitudinal changes, and attribute modifiers, is externalized into a structured Clinical Findings (CF) descriptor, serving as the finding-level anchor for both clinical-context retrieval and post-generation validation. On MIMIC-CXR, MIMIC-ABN, Two-view CXR, and CheXpert Plus, DAMEC consistently improves both natural language generation and clinical efficacy metrics over strong baselines. Code is available at: https://github.com/ku-milab/DAMEC.
FULLDiscovering Hierarchy-Grounded Domains with Adaptive Granularity for Clinical Domain Generalization
Pengfei Hu (Stevens Institute of Technology) · Xiaoxue Han (Stevens Institute of Technology) · Fei Wang (Cornell University) · Yue Ning (Stevens Institute of Technology)
Abstract
Domain generalization has become a critical challenge in predictive healthcare, where different patient groups exhibit shifting data distributions that degrade model performance. Still, regular domain generalization approaches often struggle in clinical settings due to (1) the absence of domain labels and (2) the lack of clinical insight integration. To address these challenges in healthcare, we aim to explore how medical ontologies can be used to discover dynamic yet hierarchy-grounded patient domains, a partitioning strategy that remains under-explored in prior work. Hence, we introduce UdonCare, a hierarchy-pruning method that iteratively divides patients into latent domains and retrieves domain-invariant (label) information from patient data. On public datasets (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU), UdonCare shows superiority over eight generalization baselines across four representative clinical prediction tasks with substantial domain gaps, highlighting the potential of medical knowledge for enhancing model generalization.
FULLWeak Ordinal Supervision for Causal Structure Learning from Clinical Narratives
Anne I. R. Carvalho (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Gabriel P. Oliveira (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Luis A. Duarte (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Eduardo Birchal (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Matheus C. Teixeira (Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia de Mato Grosso) · Gustavo Jacob (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Ana Paula Couto da Silva (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Gisele L. Pappa (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais) · Anisio Lacerda (Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais)
Abstract
Causal structure learning in clinical domains faces a persistent challenge: tabular datasets are often limited, while valuable domain knowledge exists primarily in unstructured clinical narratives. Recent work has explored large language models (LLMs) as sources of knowledge to refine causal graph discovery or define causal relations. However, relying directly on LLM-generated causal judgments can be problematic, as such outputs may reflect spurious associations, domain bias, or statistical patterns learned from text rather than reliable causal mechanisms. In this work, we propose a different perspective: instead of treating LLM outputs as definitive causal judgments, we use them as weak ordinal supervision integrated into the Hill-Climbing score through a soft regularization mechanism that remains correctable by observational data. Our framework extracts candidate causal relations from clinical narratives and assigns them ordinal plausibility labels using a domain-specialized LLM. We evaluate this approach on three established Bayesian network benchmarks (Alarm, Child, and Hepar II) and a real-world clinical dataset from cBioPortal, comparing Hill Climbing with and without ordinal priors across varying sample sizes. The framework consistently improves structural recovery, with statistically significant gains persisting even in high-data regimes. Overall, the results suggest that ordinal LLM supervision provides a robust inductive bias that helps resolve statistical ambiguities and mitigate structural errors in clinical causal discovery.
FULLClinSDT: LLM-Encoded Clinical Semantic Guidance for Sepsis Treatment via Decision Transformer
Yanyan Wu (East China University of Science and Technology) · Guanyu Zhu (South China Agricultural University) · Changbin Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China) · Jin Zhang (Lanzhou university) · Dexu Yu (Fenz.AI) · Tianmin Sun (City University of Hong Kong) · Jining Luan (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Chunxiao Li (University of Science and Technology of China) · Hanwen Du (The Ohio State University) · Youhua Li (City University of Hong Kong)
Abstract
Offline sepsis treatment aims to learn treatment policies from retrospective ICU trajectories. Decision Transformer-based methods provide a natural sequence modeling framework for this task, but they mainly rely on raw physiological states and historical clinician actions. Such raw trajectory tokens may not explicitly capture clinical semantics that clinicians use in practice, such as patient severity, recent treatment response, and current risk priorities. To address this limitation, we propose ClinSDT, an LLM-assisted Decision Transformer framework for offline sepsis treatment. ClinSDT uses a frozen LLM as a semantic bridge rather than a treatment decision maker. It constructs three clinical semantic views from ICU trajectories, namely Profile, Context, and Advisory, and inserts their encoded representations as independent tokens into a Decision Transformer policy. To support policy refinement and rollout, ClinSDT further trains a Treatment-Response Forecaster to estimate the next physiological state, SAPS-II change, and predictive uncertainty from state–action inputs. In the second training stage, the forecaster screens local counterfactual treatment candidates, and only low-uncertainty candidates with lower predicted SAPS-II increase are distilled into the policy after semantic regeneration. During inference, ClinSDT performs closed-loop treatment rollout by refreshing semantic inputs from the currently available patient state. Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV show that ClinSDT achieves consistent relative improvements over representative imitation learning, offline reinforcement learning, and Decision Transformer baselines under the same rollout protocol. Code and data are available at ClinSDT (https://github.com/KAG778/ClinSDT).
FULLConstructing Patient-Aligned References via Composition Modeling for Medication Recommendation
Yanda Wang (Nanjing Normal University) · Weitong Chen (Adelaide University) · Yanhui Gu (Nanjing Normal University) · Lin Yue (Adelaide University) · Haifeng Liu (Nanjing Normal University)
Abstract
Medication recommendation aims to generate effective drug combinations based on longitudinal clinical records of patients, where historical prescriptions and relevant candidate medications serve as important references to improve performance. However, existing methods treat these medications as individual entities and overlook structured interactions among clinically co-occurring drugs that jointly contribute to treatment effects. In addition, medications lack intrinsic principles to guide the modeling of semantic compositions describing such interactions, making it challenging to capture coherent clinical structures and resulting in a gap between structured patient representations and flat medication references. To address these challenges, we propose PACRM, a novel medication recommendation framework that captures semantic compositions to summarize collective drug effects through multi-level structures. Specifically, the model introduces a GAT-based voting strategy to organize drugs working as combinations jointly into structured compositions, and further performs temporally constrained and dynamically determined cross-combination voting over historical prescriptions and selected candidate medication to complete hierarchical effect propagation. This design summarizes individual drug effects into collective effects aligned with patient conditions, which are then integrated to generate effective prescriptions. Moreover, PACRM adopts a two-stage optimization to sequentially learn candidate relevance modeling and structured effect summarization. Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV demonstrate that PACRM consistently outperforms competitive baselines, remains robust across varying sizes of medication sets, and is compatible with existing methods that leverage medication references.
FULLECGTwin: Personalized ECG Generation Using Controllable Diffusion Model
Yongfan Lai (Peking University) · Bo Liu (Peking University) · Xinyan Guan (Peking University) · Qinghao Zhao (Peking University People's Hospital) · Hongyan Li (Peking University) · Shenda Hong (Peking University)
Abstract
Personalized electrocardiogram (ECG) generation is to simulate a patient's ECG digital twins tailored to specific conditions. It has the potential to transform traditional healthcare into a more accurate individualized paradigm, while preserving the key benefits of conventional population-level ECG synthesis. However, this promising task presents two fundamental challenges: extracting individual features without ground truth and injecting various types of conditions without confusing generative model. In this paper, we present ECGTwin, a two-stage framework designed to address these challenges. In the first stage, an Individual Base Extractor trained via contrastive learning robustly captures personal features from a reference ECG. In the second stage, the extracted individual features, along with a target cardiac condition, are integrated into the diffusion-based generation process through our novel AdaX Condition Injector, which injects these signals via two dedicated and specialized pathways. Both qualitative and quantitative experiments have demonstrated that our model can not only generate ECG signals of high fidelity and diversity by offering a fine-grained generation controllability, but also preserving individual-specific features. Furthermore, ECGTwin shows the potential to enhance ECG auto-diagnosis in downstream application, confirming the possibility of precise personalized healthcare solutions. Our code is available at https://github.com/Raiiyf/ECGTwin.
FULLIC-DVLoRA: Input-Conditioned Dynamic Adaptation for Endoscopic Depth Foundation Models
Zeyun Liu (Beijing Information Science and Technology University) · Ke Niu (Beijing Information Science and Technology University) · Xue Feng (Beijing Information Science and Technology University) · Jiadong Guo (Beijing Information Science and Technology University) · Heng Li (Southern University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Transferring depth foundation models to endoscopic videos is promising for surgical geometric perception, but remains challenging under patient-level visual heterogeneity. Natural-scene depth models provide strong geometric priors, yet endoscopic imagery differs substantially in specular reflection, weak texture, tool occlusion, close-range anatomy, and acquisition conditions. Existing parameter-efficient adapters, including DV-LoRA-based methods, are typically static after training and apply the same adaptation to all frames, limiting their ability to handle input-dependent appearance shifts. We propose IC-DVLoRA, an input-conditioned dynamic adaptation framework for endoscopic depth foundation models. For each frame, a lightweight condition encoder extracts a compact token that captures appearance, texture, gradient, and structural cues. This token dynamically routes multiple DV-LoRA experts in a frozen transformer backbone and modulates a DPT-style decoder through feature-wise transformations, enabling sample-specific low-rank adaptation while preserving pretrained geometric knowledge. We train and validate IC-DVLoRA on SCARED and evaluate its zero-shot generalization on Hamlyn and C3VD without target-domain fine-tuning. Experiments show improved overall performance over static adaptation baselines and competitive results against recent endoscopic depth estimation methods. Further analyses of routing utilization, top-k selection, trainable parameters, and inference latency demonstrate that IC-DVLoRA provides an effective and efficient adaptation strategy for endoscopic depth foundation models.

FULLBridge-Adaptive Continual Knowledge Graph Embedding with Topology-Aware Negative Sampling
Xudong Wang (China University of Mining and Technology) · Xiaotian Yu (China University of Mining and Technology) · Dan Li (Sun Yat-Sen University) · See-Kiong Ng (National University of Singapore) · Bo Zhang (China University of Mining and Technology)
Abstract
Real-world knowledge graphs evolve continuously, making retraining from scratch impractical. Continual knowledge graph embedding (KGE) updates representations with new triples while preserving historical knowledge. However, current methods face two challenges: (1) the stability-plasticity dilemma is pronounced for bridge entities connecting old and new subgraphs, where uniform updates may cause forgetting or rigidity; and (2) random negative sampling yields easy negatives and weak supervision near evolving graph boundaries. We propose KG-BRACE, a bridge-adaptive continual KGE framework combining topology-aware negative sampling with differentiated low-rank updates. KG-BRACE learns new entities via DoRA, updates bridge entities through a restricted Mini-DoRA branch, and freezes inactive historical entities. It also retrieves hard negative candidates from local neighborhoods. Experiments on six benchmarks show best or tied-best results on five datasets, consistent Hits@1 improvements, and competitive stronger freezing in extremely sparse graphs.
FULLFIETA: Few-Shot Inductive Knowledge Graph Completion via Task-Aware Graph Neural Networks
Chanyoung Chung (KAIST) · Minsung Hwang (KAIST) · Joyce Jiyoung Whang (KAIST)
Abstract
Few-shot knowledge graph completion aims to predict missing triplets involving few-shot relations, where each few-shot relation is associated with only a few examples of the relation, called support triplets. In few-shot knowledge graph completion, each few-shot task corresponds to predicting triplets for a few-shot relation. Most existing few-shot knowledge graph completion methods assume all entities and relations in knowledge graphs to be observed during training, making it challenging to deal with new entities and relations appearing at inference time. In this paper, we propose FIETA, a Few-shot InductivE knowledge graph completion method that introduces Task-Aware graph neural networks to handle few-shot tasks in knowledge graphs containing entities and relations unseen during training. Based on the local structures of support triplets, FIETA conducts task-centric modeling of relations to obtain relation representations reflecting relative positions to the few-shot relation, and performs task-guided message passing to compute entity representations optimized for each task by prioritizing triplets that are crucial in prediction. By learning to compute task-aware representations with structures, FIETA effectively handles few-shot relations on knowledge graphs with new entities and relations appearing at inference time. Experimental results show that FIETA outperforms 19 state-of-the-art baselines in various inductive scenarios.
FULLStructure-Conditioned Missing Modality Generation for Multi-modal Knowledge Graph Completion
Ran Yang (Dalian Maritime University) · Bo Ning (Dalian Maritime University) · Chengfei Liu (Swinburne University of Technology) · Xin Zhou (Dalian Maritime University) · Yucen Shi (Dalian Maritime University) · Le Wang (Dalian Maritime University)
Abstract
Multi-modal Knowledge Graph Completion (MMKGC) leverages entity-associated visual and textual information to infer missing facts in multi-modal knowledge graphs. However, real-world multi-modal knowledge graphs often suffer from modality missingness. Existing methods typically rely on deterministic reconstruction or modality alignment, which fail to model the uncertainty and diversity of missing modalities and overlook the impact of intra-modality noise and structural semantics, thereby limiting their reasoning capability. In this paper, we propose Structure-Conditioned Missing Modality Generation (ScMMG), a generative framework for MMKGC that recovers missing entity modalities under knowledge graph semantic guidance. ScMMG leverages diffusion-based modality generation to model the latent distribution of missing modalities and incorporates adversarial structural optimization to enforce relational consistency within a unified semantic space. As a result, the generated modality representations are encouraged to be both distributionally plausible and structurally coherent. To provide reliable semantic anchors, we introduce a Fragment-level Magnitude-aware Fusion (FlMaF) module that suppresses noise and captures intrinsic entity semantics at a fine-grained level. Furthermore, a Structure-Conditioned Driven Diffusion Generation (ScDDG) module with Adversarial Optimization Scoring (AOS) is designed to enforce structural consistency and improve training stability within a shared semantic space constructed by RotatE, a rotation-based knowledge graph embedding model. Experimental results on DB15K, MKG-Y, and MKG-W demonstrate that ScMMG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, while ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each proposed component.
FULLStructural Knowledge Induced Logical Learning for LLM Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs
Lei Gao (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Ben Zhang (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Jinchuan Zhang (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Ling Tian (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Hui Gao (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Junliang Xing (Tsinghua University) · Yuanchun Shi (Tsinghua University)
Abstract
Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are fundamental for grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) in factually consistent reasoning across diverse data-mining tasks. However, when reasoning over complex graph topologies, LLMs can be brittle in maintaining structural consistency and may rely on spurious correlations. We propose SKILL (Structural Knowledge Induced Logical Learning), a novel paradigm that transforms relational rules from passive symbolic patterns into explicit, generation-time symbolic guidance for LLM-based reasoning. Unlike existing methods that isolate symbolic mining from neural inference, SKILL introduces a semantically aligned rule synthesis framework that filters spurious patterns and enables LLMs to leverage relational regularities during inference. By grounding generation in pruned, query-specific subgraph structures together with rule–path evidence, SKILL improves inductive generalization while preserving generative flexibility. Extensive experiments on three inductive benchmarks demonstrate that SKILL achieves state-of-the-art performance, with up to a 5% absolute improvement in Hits@1, highlighting a new and effective way to integrate symbolic structure into LLM reasoning over knowledge graphs. Source code is available at https://github.com/luilui97/SKILL.
FULLExistentially Consistent Skolemized Reasoning for Complex Query Answering on Knowledge Graphs
Yuyin Lu (Sun Yat-sen University) · Hegang Chen (Sun Yat-sen University) · Shanrui Xie (Sun Yat-sen University) · Yanghui Rao (Sun Yat-sen University) · Haoran Xie (Lingnan University) · Fu Lee Wang (Hong Kong Metropolitan University) · Qing Li (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
Abstract
Complex Query Answering (CQA) over incomplete Knowledge Graphs (KGs) formalizes compositional reasoning as Existential First-Order logic with one free variable (EFO1), where existential variables link multiple atomic constraints within a query. Maintaining existential consistency helps prevent reasoning shortcuts that satisfy only part of these constraints. We identify a Grounding–Skolemization dichotomy in existing CQA approaches. Grounding-based methods preserve logical equivalence but incur combinatorial enumeration costs, whereas Skolemization-based methods enable efficient latent reasoning over KGs while risking reasoning shortcuts arising from existential inconsistency. To address this tradeoff, we propose existentially consistent Skolemized reasoning, instantiated by the Logic-constrained Vector Symbolic Architecture (LVSA). LVSA uses vector-symbolic operations to compose atomic constraints and differentiable Skolemization to construct and reuse a constraint-conditioned latent state for each existential variable. Logical negation is handled through a logic-regularized neural negator. Theoretically, LVSA is structurally expressive for EFO1 queries with acyclic query graphs and offers favorable complexity. Experiments show that LVSA outperforms prior Skolemization-based methods in reasoning performance and empirical existential consistency, while incurring substantially lower inference costs than Grounding-based approaches.
FULLSEMAPHORE: Semantic Detour over Incomplete Knowledge Graphs for Multi-hop Numerical QA
Hojun Lee (Sungkyunkwan University) · Hogun Park (Sungkyunkwan University)
Abstract
Numerical question answering (QA) over Knowledge Graphs (KGs) requires retrieving numerical values from structured sources. Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) and KG-augmented Large Language Model (LLM) methods exploit multi-hop connectivity for entity-centric questions but remain brittle for numerical queries, whose values typically appear as sparse attribute leaves. When required triples are missing, target values can become unreachable by explicit traversal; structural methods may retrieve values from the wrong numerical attribute, while numerical solvers assuming directly attached values cannot access non-local evidence. We propose SEMAPHORE, a neuro-symbolic framework that reformulates numerical QA over KGs as a semantic detour problem. SEMAPHORE combines symbolic path planning with embedding-based geometric navigation and decoupled scoring that separates relational navigation from numerical attribute grounding. This design identifies plausible detours while preserving the metric semantics required for accurate numerical answers. On numerical QA benchmarks derived from FB15K-237 and YAGO15K, SEMAPHORE outperforms strong LLM and KG-augmented baselines, demonstrating the value of semantic detours for robust numerical knowledge access over KGs. Sparsity and cross-dataset transfer experiments show that this advantage persists under severe graph incompleteness and when target-specific Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) training is replaced with transferred schema embeddings. Code is available at https://github.com/orcies8147/SEMAPHORE.
FULLCausality-Guided Spurious Evidence Pruning with GFlowNet for Faithful Graph Retrieval
Jinho Choi (Konkuk University) · Hye-Yoon Baek (Konkuk University) · Sang-Hyun Park (Konkuk University) · Sang-June Kim (KAIST) · Hyeongjun Yang (Samsung Electronics) · Byungkook Oh (Konkuk University)
Abstract
Knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) increasingly relies on graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG). However, graph retrievers are trained under path-level weak supervision, which treats every triple on an answer-reaching path as equally informative. Retrieved subgraphs thus contain spurious triples that reach the answer without causally supporting it, leaving noise filtering to the reasoner. We propose Causality-Guided Spurious Evidence Pruning with GFlowNet (CaseFlow), which internalizes spurious-evidence pruning into the retriever by reformulating retrieval as a flow-guided pruning process. Repurposed from a candidate generator into a pruner, the GFlowNet removes spurious evidence while retaining answer-supporting causal structure. To make this pruning causally informed and tractable, a relation-conditioned disentanglement encoder supplies a causal-relevance proxy for the chunk-level pruning prior, and adaptive relation-coherent chunks bound the action space. CaseFlow outperforms strong GraphRAG retrievers on the WebQSP, CWQ, and MetaQA-3hop benchmarks, with the largest gains in complex multi-hop reasoning. Our code is available at https://github.com/ChoiPi2/CaseFlow
FULLRole-Specific Agentic RAG: Asymmetric Hybrid-Path Reasoning over Semi-structured Knowledge Bases
Yutian Shi (Southeast University) · Dian Shen (Southeast University) · Meng Wang (Tongji University) · Beilun Wang (Southeast University)
Abstract
Hybrid Question Answering (HQA) over semi-structured knowledge bases (SKBs) is vital for high-stakes domains like clinical precision medicine. However, HQA over SKBs is challenging because evidence is split across documents and relations, while answers must satisfy both semantic and structural constraints. Standard RAG pipelines retrieve evidence from textual or relational sources separately, failing to jointly capture the semantic conditions and relational constraints required by HQA over SKBs. Meanwhile, advanced agentic RAG systems that rely on computationally intensive models incur prohibitive inference latency and cost. To address these limitations, we introduce RSA-RAG, a Role-Specific Agentic RAG method with an asymmetric hybrid-path reasoning framework. We propose Role-Specific Asymmetric Collaboration for Hybrid-Path Reasoning, which assigns high-level roadmap planning and final answer generation to the large model, while lightweight role-specific agents handle frequent retrieval-control operations. Additionally, we introduce Strategy-Guided Candidate Navigation for Semi-Structured Retrieval, where compact agents perform strategy routing, constraint extraction, and hybrid navigation over an initial candidate set to retrieve textual and relational evidence around candidate targets. Furthermore, we implement Candidate-Support Evidence Structuring for Grounded Generation, which uses evidence verification to organize supported textual-relational evidence into structured grounding contexts for final generation. Extensive experiments show that RSA-RAG achieves strong retrieval performance on STARK, with an average MRR of 54.6% and competitive top-ranked performance across the three subsets. It further improves CRAG accuracy by 11.1% relative to Agentic RAG and reduces token consumption by up to 56.9% compared with implemented LLM-intensive baselines.

FULLCompact Representations of Geometric Bipartite Graphs via Weighted Biclique Covers
Aryan Esmailpour (University of Illinois Chicago) · Khoi Le (University of Illinois Chicago) · Stavros Sintos (University of Illinois Chicago)
Abstract
Bipartite graphs are a fundamental representation for relational data arising in recommendation systems, market-basket analysis, social networks, and communication graphs. A key challenge in these settings is to store and transmit large bipartite graphs compactly while preserving exact structural and path information. We study biclique-based representations of bipartite graphs G=(V,U,E), where the edge set is encoded using a collection of complete bipartite subgraphs. We focus on the Weighted Biclique Covering problem, which minimizes the total number of vertices used across all bicliques, and introduce a generalized variant that additionally penalizes the number of bicliques, capturing practical overheads in storage, transmission, and model complexity. While the weighted biclique covering problem is known to be NP-Complete, we show that the generalized variant is also NP-Complete. Despite this hardness, many real-world bipartite graphs admit low-dimensional geometric embeddings or can be well approximated by them. Leveraging this observation, we develop the first approximation algorithms with provable guarantees for the (generalized) weighted biclique covering problem on geometric bipartite graphs. Specifically, for δ-disk bipartite graphs in low-dimensional ℓ∞d spaces, we design a polynomial-time algorithm that achieves an O(log |U| · logd |V|)-approximation, combining ideas from greedy set cover, geometric range searching, and densest subgraph optimization. We also show how our algorithms extend to ℓαd metrics for any α≥ 1. Finally, we evaluate our algorithms on real-world bipartite datasets and show that they efficiently compute significantly smaller biclique-based representations than natural baselines, while scaling to large graphs.
FULLAuthenticated K-core Community Search in Dynamic Graphs in Hybrid-Storage Blockchains
Siyu Li (Renmin University of China) · Kai Zhong (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Zhiwei Zhang (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Zhixu Li (Renmin University of China) · Ye Yuan (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Guoren Wang (Beijing Institute of Technology)
Abstract
Graphs model complex relationships in domains such as social networks, bioinformatics, and the Web, where structures evolve continuously. Many studies focus on k-core community search for applications like recommendation and advertising. Due to frequent graph updates and the large scale of real-world graphs, data owners often outsource graph maintenance and execution to third parties. This raises concerns that third parties may forge query results intentionally or due to external attacks, making it essential to ensure the integrity of query results. Blockchain offers transparency and reliability for secure data storage, and hybrid-storage blockchains use off-chain storage with smart contracts for scalability. However, current authenticated query methods in hybrid-storage blockchains primarily focus on key-value data or other types of graph queries, which cannot be applied to authenticated community searches. This is the first study on the authenticated k-core community search in dynamic graphs. We propose a baseline scheme enabling clients to verify query integrity via verification objects (VO) and design a precomputation-based authenticated data structure, the Merkle Core Tree (MCTree), to enhance efficiency and reduce communication costs. Considering that both of the above solutions are based on Merkle hash trees (MHT), MHT-based updates require modifying paths from leaf to root upon each change, limiting update efficiency. To address this issue, we introduce HCoreGen, an HMAC-based algorithm that updates only affected tuples without precomputation, significantly improving update efficiency. The effectiveness and efficiency of authentication solutions are verified by the extensive experiment results on real large dynamic graphs.
FULLRethinking Community Consistency in Heterogeneous Networks
Yanghao Liu (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Fangda Guo (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Huawei Shen (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Xueqi Cheng (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Community discovery in heterogeneous networks commonly assumes that graph topology provides semantically useful neighborhoods. In human-centered systems, however, structural proximity may be weakly aligned with latent cognitive similarity, causing graph propagation to introduce psychologically inconsistent information. We revisit community discovery from this perspective and propose CogPHGNN, a cognition-aware graph learning framework that integrates multi-view psychological representations, semantic graph construction, and gated propagation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that graph learning becomes effective only when graph topology is sufficiently aligned with latent semantic and psychological similarity. The results show that graph construction quality and selective propagation critically affect cognition-aware community consistency, while mismatched neighborhoods or propagation mechanisms may degrade representation quality. Across graph constructions, propagation mechanisms, and psychological theories, the results consistently highlight structure-cognition alignment as a key factor governing cognition-aware community discovery.
FULLRepresentation-Aware Modularity with a Distance-Calibrated Null Model
Taejoon Han (Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology) · Dahee Kim (Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology) · Junghoon Kim (Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology) · Taeho Ha (Soonchunhyang University)
Abstract
Modularity is a standard objective for community detection, comparing observed intra-community connectivity with its null-model expectation. Modern node embeddings capture structural and semantic proximity beyond raw topology, but replacing adjacency with representation-induced affinity while retaining the classical degree-based null model makes the observed term geometry-dependent and the expected term geometry-agnostic. This creates a null-model mismatch: the objective may reward affinity already expected from representation proximity. This paper introduces RAM, a representation-aware modularity objective with a distance-calibrated null model. RAM preserves the observed-minus-expected principle by calibrating expected affinity with both degree heterogeneity and representation distance. We analyse its relation to classical modularity and develop divisive and multi-level greedy optimisers. Experiments on seven real-world datasets and synthetic scalability tests show that RAM improves over topology-only, direct embedding-clustering, and deep learning-based baselines, remains competitive under classical modularity while improving community quality on large graphs, and scales efficiently. Ablations confirm that both degree correction and distance calibration are essential.
FULLBeyond Locality: Multi-scale Structural Tokenization for Unsupervised Community Search
Xiujin Yue (Northeastern University) · Chuanhou Sun (Northeastern University) · Ying Yin (Northeastern University) · Yuhai Zhao (Northeastern University) · Yuan Li (North China University of Technology)
Abstract
Community Search (CS) aims to retrieve query-dependent cohesive subgraphs from networks, playing a crucial role in modern applications such as computing power networks and biological systems. Given the high cost of labeling, unsupervised CS has emerged as a scalable paradigm. However, existing approaches often suffer from restricted structural receptive fields and the limitation of static node representations, which fail to perceive the evolving community boundaries during expansion.To address these, this paper explores the potential of unsupervised CS by proposing the ComPass framework. We first design an incremental graph augmentation strategy to generate views with enriched community information. These views are then processed via a multi-scale structural tokenization mechanism, which transforms the graph into hierarchical sequences that bridge fine-grained topological associations with coarse-grained community contexts. By feeding these sequences into a Transformer-based encoder, ComPass effectively captures discriminative community representations without supervision. During online search, an iterative score refinement mechanism enables the co-evolution of community structure and node scoring, mitigating semantic drift.Extensive experiments illustrate the promising performance of ComPass as an exploratory step. Notably, ComPass achieves a competitive advantage over the strongest baseline, TransZero, with an average F1-score improvement of 15.23%. This exploration suggests that integrating incremental augmentation, multi-scale tokenization, and adaptive search offers a potentially effective direction for advancing unsupervised community search.
FULLWhen Does Structural Entropy Track Labels? Margins, Diagnostics, and Failure Modes in Graph Clustering
Dingli Su (Beihang Univesity) · Hao Peng (Beihang University) · Yicheng Pan (Beihang University) · Angsheng Li (Beihang University)
Abstract
Structural entropy (H2) is often reported beside normalized mutual information (NMI) and the adjusted Rand index (ARI), inviting the assumption that a lower structural objective implies better agreement with external labels. However, these metrics need not agree: H2 measures random-walk compression, whereas NMI and ARI measure agreement with an external partition. For a fixed graph, we show that if every partition that differs substantially from a reference labeling has an H2 value at least γ greater than that labeling's H2 value, then any partition whose H2 value is at most ε<γ above the reference labeling's H2 value must also be close to the reference labeling. We measure this closeness using variation of information (VI), a standard distance between partitions, and derive a corresponding lower bound on NMI. These VI and NMI guarantees require a positive H2 margin. Theoretically, we derive exact, checkable gap criteria for specified merge/split perturbations in balanced stochastic block models and for specified contact-domain boundary shifts. These criteria characterize when H2 tracks external labels under the specified perturbations. Empirically, a sampled perturbation diagnostic assesses whether a graph–label pair exhibits a positive margin. Across 11 synthetic and eight real benchmarks, the pooled Spearman correlation between H2 and NMI is -0.83 and -0.60, respectively. We identify four failure modes associated with departures from this trend: near-binary strong homophily, free-K over-segmentation, elongated-community fragmentation, and hub mis-assignment. A multistart local search makes the diagnostic practical. A Hi-C case study illustrates the method on two chromosome-19 contact maps. Code, experiment configurations, and saved result summaries are available at https://github.com/SuuTTT/se-when-tracks-labels.
FULLInductive Correlation Clustering with Graph Neural Networks
Francesco Paolo Nerini (Sapienza University of Rome) · Francesco Bonchi (Intesa Sanpaolo AI Research) · Arijit Khan (Bowling Green State University) · André Panisson (Intesa Sanpaolo AI Research)
Abstract
Correlation Clustering (CC) is a natural formulation of clustering in combinatorial optimization, which uses a graph representation of the input and does not require a pre-specified number of clusters. Given n objects and a pairwise similarity function, the goal is to cluster the objects so that similar objects are put in the same cluster and dissimilar objects are put in different clusters. Despite its versatility, existing CC algorithms suffer from significant scalability issues and are inherently transductive: i.e., the algorithm must be executed from scratch for any new problem instance. In this work, we bridge this gap by leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to solve Inductive Correlation Clustering, a novel generalization of the CC problem designed to handle unseen graph instances. By learning to exploit common structural patterns and node features during training, our framework generalizes to new graphs drawn from the same distribution with minimal computational overhead with respect to standard algorithms. We demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of our approach through extensive experiments. Our framework not only excels in the inductive setting, e.g., lowering the inference time up to 5 order of magnitude, while maintaining an approximation ratio within 10% of the best baseline solution, but also achieves competitive results on standard (transductive) CC benchmarks. Finally, we showcase a practical application of our framework as a learnable pooling mechanism for graph classification. Our results indicate that our method serves as an efficient pooling layer, enhancing the ability of GNNs to capture hierarchical structural information in networks.
FULLExplainCC: Explaining Correlated Clusters by Node Labels
Nadeesha Shyami Kumari Herath Mudiyanselage (University of Helsinki) · Florian Adriaens (University of Helsinki) · Nikolaj Tatti (University of Helsinki)
Abstract
An increasingly important requirement for clustering algorithms is that decisions and outcomes need to be clearly understandable for human users. We address this requirement for the Correlation Clustering (CC) problem, in case the objects to be clustered are accompanied by labels. In CC one seeks to partition a set of objects into clusters based on pairwise similarity and dissimilarity information. Our proposed model only considers clusters that can be explained by a label tree, which is essentially a decision tree that partitions the objects according to labels. The goal is to find an explainable partition of the data that minimizes the CC objective function. We formalize this problem from a theoretical viewpoint, and prove several hardness of approximation results, also when constraining the size of the tree. Our proposed greedy method finds locally optimal splits, and works recursively in a top-down approach. To efficiently compute the best split, we carefully maintain certain counters. An experimental evaluation demonstrates its effectiveness. The proposed algorithm processes graphs with over million edges in a few minutes, can find the ground truth in synthetic data, and is able to produce interpretable clusters in real world networks.

3A · LLM-based RecommendationFull ResearchTeatro StudioTuesday 10:30 – 12:308 talksChair: Mirko Marras (University of Cagliari)
FULLTowards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
Yunze Luo (Peking University) · Gaode Chen (Kuaishou Technology) · Yinjie Jiang (Kuaishou Technology) · Xinghua Zhang (Unaffiliated) · Kaigui Bian (Peking University)
Abstract
Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-collaborative gap. To address these issues, we propose a novel Content Understanding from a Collaborative Perspective framework (CURec), which generates collaborative-aligned content features for more comprehensive recommendations. CURec first adapts the LLM with recommendation objectives through post-training, equipping it with instruction-following and chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Next, we use the LLM-generated features to train the recommender model. Then, we treat the user–item prediction scores produced by the trained recommender model as reward signals to guide RL-based refinement of the LLM, thereby improving the quality of generated reasons and pattern. The corrected reasons are directly integrated into the recommender model to enhance comprehensibility and recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of CURec over existing methods.
FULLSelfDR: Self-Distillation from Reasoning for LLM-Based Recommendation
Chumeng Jiang (Tsinghua University) · Jiayin Wang (Tsinghua University) · Xinjie Lin (Tsinghua University) · Zhiqiang Guo (Tsinghua University) · Hengliang Luo (Meituan) · Min Zhang (Quan Cheng Laboratory)
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful backbones for recommendation. To better elicit their capabilities, reasoning has been widely incorporated to help LLMs interpret rich textual signals and improve recommendation accuracy. However, explicitly generating intermediate reasoning traces often incurs substantial computational costs, which limits practical deployment in real-world recommender systems. To address this challenge, we propose SelfDR, a Self-Distillation from Reasoning framework for LLM-based Recommendation. SelfDR distills an LLM's own reasoning-enhanced predictions to produce recommendations directly, improving recommendation effectiveness while maintaining inference efficiency. All components in the framework are built on the same base LLM, without relying on any external models. Specifically, the teacher recommender is constructed by training a reasoner with downstream performance as the reward, enabling it to generate targeted rationales that are later incorporated into the teacher’s input. A student recommender for direct recommendation, with the same underlying model, then learns from the teacher through self-distillation with a dynamic weighting strategy. Extensive experiments on three public datasets validate the effectiveness, rationality, and efficiency of SelfDR. Codes are available at https://github.com/JiangDeccc/SelfDistillation.
FULLSCoRD: Semantic-Assisted Continual Retriever-Reranker Distillation for LLM-Based Recommendation
Seunghyun Baek (Korea University) · Gyuseok Lee (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign) · Seunghan Lee (Korea University) · Wonbin Kweon (Sungkyunkwan University) · Dong Wang (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign) · Seongku Kang (Korea University)
Abstract
Recommendation systems increasingly adopt a two-stage pipeline, where an ID-based retriever retrieves candidates and an LLM-based reranker refines their rankings. To improve retrieval quality, reranker-to-retriever distillation is commonly used to transfer the reranker’s knowledge to the retriever. For practical deployment, however, this pipeline must continually adapt to evolving interests and incoming interactions. A naive solution is to repeatedly update the LLM reranker and distill its latest knowledge, but this incurs prohibitive costs. Updating the retriever alone is cheaper, but its limited capacity makes adaptation from sparse data difficult. We propose SCoRD, a continual knowledge distillation framework for LLM-based reranking pipelines under a non-stationary data stream. SCoRD introduces a semantic reasoning assistant that distills the LLM’s ability to infer underlying user intents into reusable intent-level guidance. It selectively distills reranker knowledge to the retriever on low-confidence sequences, guides retriever-only updates without repeated LLM inference, and feeds retriever-derived representations and intent-drift signals back to the reranker. Experiments on real-world datasets show that SCoRD enables effective and efficient retriever-reranker co-adaptation.
FULLSCAU-REC: Subspace-Constrained Adapter Updates for LLM-Based Recommendations
Tong Zhang (University of Technology Sydney) · Nitin Bisht (The Education University of Hong Kong) · Chongjun Xia (University of Technology Sydney) · Xianzhi Wang (University of Technology Sydney) · Jing Long (University of Technology Sydney) · Guandong Xu (The Education University of Hong Kong)
Abstract
LLM-based recommender systems increasingly adapt frozen backbones with parameter-efficient adapters as user-item interactions arrive. However, continual updates can overfit transient feedback, amplify noise, and degrade long-term preferences. We therefore propose SCAU-Rec, a drift-conditioned adapter-control framework that uses an evolving reference coreset to detect preference shifts and trigger updates only when warranted. When triggered, SCAU-Rec modulates risk-aware alignment between consecutive model states and projects adapter gradients away from an online low-rank stability subspace, reducing interference with retained preferences. We provide theoretical analyses of interference control, bounded predictive shift, and robustness to approximate stability subspaces. Across multiple benchmarks, SCAU-Rec improves recommendation utility, retention, update efficiency, and robustness over representative continual adaptation and LLM-based recommendation baselines.
FULLTRACER: Balancing Stability-Plasticity-Cognitivity Trilemma for LLM Enhanced Continual Recommendation
WooJoo Kim (Pohang University of Science and Technology) · HyunSik Yoo (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign) · JunYoung Kim (Pohang University of Science and Technology) · JaeHyung Lim (Pohang University of Science and Technology) · SeongKu Kang (Korea University) · HwanJo Yu (Pohang University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Continual recommendation aims to capture evolving user interests from streaming data but struggles with sparsity. LLM enhancers mitigate this with semantic knowledge, but naive integration creates a new conflict. We identify this as the Stability-Plasticity-Cognitivity (SPC) Trilemma, where generalized LLM semantic priors (Cognitivity) conflict with retaining personalized historical preferences (Stability) and adapting to individual interest shifts (Plasticity). To address this, we propose Trilemma-Responsive Adaptive Continual Enhancement for Recommendation (TRACER). TRACER synergistically combines three specialized modules, each targeting stability, plasticity, or cognitivity, while preventing any single lemma from dominating. This holistic design enables semantic knowledge to support history retention and adaptation to evolving interests without disrupting continual learning. Across five real-world datasets, TRACER effectively harmonizes the SPC trilemma and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by up to 14.38%. Our code is available at https://github.com/woo-joo/TRACER_CIKM26.
FULLPSCRec: Preference-Conditioned Semantic Calibration for LLM-Enhanced Graph Recommendation
Jingwei Ma (Shandong Normal University) · Li Sun (Shandong Normal University) · Jiahui Wen (Defense Innovation Institute) · Mingyang Zhong (Southwest University)
Abstract
Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become a dominant paradigm in recommender systems by modeling collaborative signals over user--item interaction graphs. Recent LLM-enhanced recommenders seek to complement such structural signals with semantic knowledge from Large Language Models (LLMs). However, most existing methods implicitly follow a direct semantic fusion paradigm, where LLM-derived representations are treated as reliable semantic features and directly fused with collaborative representations. We argue that this paradigm is incomplete: LLM semantics are informative, but not directly trustworthy for recommendation. Through controlled diagnostic analyses, we identify two failure modes of raw LLM semantics: Unreliable Semantic Signals, where representations are sensitive to task-irrelevant textual noise, and Semantic--Behavioral Misalignment, where semantic proximity does not necessarily imply behavioral relevance. To address these issues, we propose PSCRec, a model-agnostic framework for preference-conditioned semantic calibration in LLM-enhanced graph recommendation. PSCRec progressively transforms noisy LLM-derived priors into behavior-consistent semantic evidence by structuring semantic profiles, grounding them in dynamic user preferences, filtering unreliable semantic associations, purifying residual semantic redundancy, and aligning calibrated semantic representations with collaborative signals. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that PSCRec consistently improves multiple graph-based backbones and outperforms representative LLM-enhanced recommendation methods. Further ablation, robustness, semantic--behavioral calibration, and efficiency analyses demonstrate the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the proposed calibration framework.
FULLScoring-to-Ranking: A Language Model-Guided Graph Framework for Multi-Criteria Preference Ranking
Zhenhua Meng (Inner Mongolia University)
Abstract
Multi-criteria ratings provide user feedback on multiple aspects of an item, offering richer preference signals than a single overall rating. Early work mainly focused on predicting criterion or overall ratings, whereas practical scenarios require ranking items according to their overall utility inferred from sparse and heterogeneous criterion-level evidence, which constitutes the core problem of multi-criteria recommendation (MCR). This ranking-oriented formulation of MCR gives rise to two key challenges: learning reliable criterion dependencies under sparse interactions, and bridging the mismatch between semantic preference signals and collaboratively learned representations. To address these issues, we propose S2R-LMG, a scoring-to-ranking framework that jointly learns from semantic and collaborative views. Specifically, we construct a user–item–criterion tripartite graph to model criterion dependencies in the collaborative view, while using large language models (LLMs) to transform sparse multi-criteria feedback into criterion-aware contextual preference priors for users and items. These priors are then projected into the ranking space and coupled with collaborative representations via alignment and retrieval-based distillation, so that semantic guidance directly contributes to preference ranking. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that S2R-LMG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models on top-N ranking, achieving an average improvement of 4.84% across all datasets and evaluation metrics over the strongest baseline. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/nunu1995/S2R-LMG.
FULLThe Recall Ceiling of LLM Recommendation Reranking
Zhaohui Wang (University of Southern California,Viterbi School of Engineering)
Abstract
Some LLM-based recommendation rerankers are evaluated under an oracle protocol that guarantees the ground-truth item is present in the scored set, either by injecting it into the candidate list or by scoring it against sampled negatives. We show that this protocol overestimates realistic performance by 92-95% in NDCG@10 across three primary Amazon datasets, so oracle results do not transfer to deployment. The root cause is a recall ceiling: realistic retrieval covers only 2-19% of relevant items at K=100 across eight datasets in three domains (Amazon products, MovieLens movies, MIND news), placing a deterministic upper bound on any closed-candidate reranker's top-k NDCG (Theorem 1, E[NDCG@k] <= Recall@|W_pi| under LOO evaluation, where W_pi is the reranker's own candidate window). Under realistic retrieval, every optimisation strategy we tested fails to produce a statistically significant improvement over the CF baseline on our primary Amazon datasets: prompt engineering, model scaling across a 168x parameter range, sequential models, three supervised neural rerankers (LambdaMART, RankNet, MLP) under a disjoint train/eval user split, a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B reranker, and a hybrid CF+BM25+Dense retrieval with reciprocal-rank fusion. Adding text-aware retrieval raises recall on Beauty but does not lift end-to-end NDCG. Giving the LLM the upstream CF ranks and scores directly--the fairest setting we can construct--narrows but does not close the gap to CF, and does so by making the LLM adhere more closely to the CF order rather than by adding information; an LLM+CF fusion tuned on the evaluation users themselves recovers CF's performance and no more. We propose the Recall-Aware Evaluation Protocol (RAEP) as a diagnostic: classify the regime by retrieval recall, then evaluate reranking only where the ceiling permits differentiation. In the retrieval regimes we can measure (Recall@100 of 2-19%), the path to effective LLM recommendation runs through retrieval improvement rather than reranker sophistication; we do not claim this ordering holds at the higher recall, richer feature sets, and online feedback available to production systems.
3B · Time Series Forecasting IFull ResearchSala SinopoliTuesday 10:30 – 12:308 talksChair: Seungeon Lee (Max Planck Institute for Software Systems)
FULLSliding-Window Reordering with Overlap Averaging: A Simple Time-Domain Augmentation for Multivariate Forecasting
Jafar Bakhshaliyev (University of Hildesheim) · Johannes Burchert (University of Hildesheim) · Niels Landwehr (University of Hildesheim) · Lars Schmidt-Thieme (University of Hildesheim)
Abstract
Augmentation has become a central technique for improving deep forecasting models, but classification-style transformations tend to break the coherence between the look-back window and its continuous future target. We describe a simple procedure that unfolds the joint input-target sequence into overlapping sliding windows, randomly reorders a controlled fraction of them-prioritized by a lightweight variance criterion-and reconstructs the sequence by averaging across the overlaps, producing synthetic samples with controlled variation while limiting temporal distortion. The procedure is model-agnostic, introduces only three interpretable hyperparameters, and achieves strong improvements over a comprehensive set of competing augmentations across nine long-term forecasting benchmarks with five backbone families (TSMixer, DLinear, PatchTST, TiDE, LightTS) and four short-term traffic benchmarks with PatchTST. Component-wise ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, distributional-alignment diagnostics, probabilistic forecasting evaluation, and a transfer experiment to univariate and multivariate time series classification clarify the contribution of each design choice.
FULLSeleRT: Selective Retrieval of LLM Representations for Long-term Time Series Forecasting
Hyunwook Jeong (Yonsei University) · Youngwan Jo (Yonsei University) · Minwoo Hong (Yonsei University) · Sanghyun Park (Yonsei University)
Abstract
Recent studies have explored the use of pretrained large language model (LLM) representations for long-term time series forecasting.While direct LLM-based forecasting methods adapt time series into LLM-compatible inputs, recent multimodal approaches further use LLM representations as auxiliary semantic representations and introduce interaction mechanisms between time series and language branches. However, existing methods mainly focus on aligning or combining these representations, leaving underexplored how LLM representations should be selectively utilized for different forecasting inputs. In particular, not all LLM layers are equally informative for time series forecasting, and different temporal regions may require different predictive cues from LLM representations. To address these challenges, we propose SeleRT (Selective Retrieval of LLM Representations for Long-term Time Series Forecasting), a multimodal forecasting framework designed to selectively utilize LLM representations for time series prediction. SeleRT consists of two key components: Statistics-Aware Dynamic Layer Fusion (SADLF), which dynamically generates layer weights from input time series statistics, and Patch-Wise Learnable Query Retrieval (PLQR), which enables patch-grounded queries to retrieve information from the fused LLM representation. We evaluate SeleRT on eight standard long-term forecasting benchmarks under full-shot and few-shot protocols. Experimental results show that SeleRT achieves state-of-the-art overall performance, with particularly strong gains in the few-shot setting. Ablation and visualization analyses further support the effectiveness of input-adaptive layer fusion and patch-wise selective retrieval.
FULLRecovering Lost Details: Multi-Scale Frequency Compensation for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
Runmin Zou (Central South University) · Siyi Xie (Central South University) · Yaohui Huang (Central South University) · Yun Wang (Central South University)
Abstract
Long-term time series forecasting has made significant progress by leveraging multi-scale information to capture hierarchical temporal patterns and model long-range dependencies. However, temporal downsampling in existing multi-scale methods inevitably smooths detailed temporal fluctuations, and this information loss is further aggravated by their emphasis on dominant trends across scales, resulting in insufficiently expressive representations. To address this, we propose a Multi-Scale Wavelet Mixing (MWMixer) model, which incorporates a Bidirectional Frequency-Bands Mixing strategy to recover lost temporal details across scales, enabling complementary cross-scale information interactions. Then, a Dynamic Scale-Adaptive Fusion module learns time-varying weights for each scale to fuse multi-scale forecasts into the final prediction, enhancing the flexibility of multi-scale aggregation. In addition, a cross-scale consistency loss aligns each coarse-scale prediction with the interval-averaged fine-scale outputs, while a multi-scale supervision loss enforces prediction accuracy at each scale, promoting consistent learning across scales. Extensive experiments on seven real-world datasets demonstrate that MWMixer achieves competitive performance in long-term forecasting.
FULLFAME: Frequency-Enhanced Pre-trained Model for Time Series Forecasting
Hao Guo (Hikvision Research Institute) · Ruiheng Yang (Hikvision Research Institute) · Hong Zhao (Hikvision Research Institute) · Yao Fu (Hikvision Research Institute) · Weihao Jiang (Hikvision Research Institute) · Wenqi Ren (Hikvision Research Institute)
Abstract
General time series forecasting models pre-trained on extensive datasets have recently gained significant attention for their strong domain generalization capabilities. Nevertheless, existing time series pre-trained models confront two critical challenges. First, previous approaches are insufficient in capturing the intricate relationships among variables from a global perspective. Second, the temporal relationships in time series are explored using a fixed patch size from a single frequency perspective that discards important information hidden in the data. To address these challenges, we propose a frequency-enhanced pre-trained model (FAME) for multivariate time series forecasting, which captures the temporal and variable relationships separately from a frequency perspective. In the temporal relation learning module, we design a multi-expert architecture that automatically determines the size of patches for time series and process them using the customized models based on the determined patch size. In the variable relation learning module, we model the variable dependencies from a global perspective in the frequency domain and propose to employ a frequency characteristic prompt which enhance the extraction of relationships between more correlated variables. Finally, the outputs of the two modules are aggregated to generate the final prediction. We pre-train FAME on the Time-300B datasets and extensive experiments on public real datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves superior performance. Our code is published for further research.
FULLTime Series Forecasting via Reasoning: A Slow-Thinking Approach with Reinforcement Fine-Tuned LLMs
Yitong Zhou (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Yucong Luo (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Cheng Mingyue (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Qi Liu (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Jiahao Wang (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Daoyu Wang (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Enhong Chen (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
To advance time series forecasting, a wide range of methods—from statistical techniques to deep learning architectures—have been proposed to improve prediction accuracy; however, most still follow a fast thinking paradigm that maps historical patterns to future values with limited explicit reasoning or interpretable intermediate steps, undermining adaptability to evolving temporal dynamics. Although slow-thinking LLMs exhibit strong multi-step reasoning, prompt-only solutions are constrained by cost, privacy, and insufficient domain alignment, motivating the training of LLMs to acquire slow thinking time-series reasoning skills. In this paper, we propose Time-R1, a reinforcement fine-tuning framework designed to enhance the multi-step reasoning ability of LLMs for time series forecasting. Training starts with supervised fine-tuning for warm-up adaptation, followed by reinforcement learning that improves the model’s generalization ability via reward-driven reasoning optimization. Specifically, we introduce a fine-grained multi-objective reward to provide training signals tailored to time series forecasting, and GRIP (group-based relative importance for policy optimization) to leverage non-uniform sampling for encouraging the exploration of effective reasoning paths. Experiments show that Time-R1 achieves competitive forecasting performance across diverse datasets (Code is at https://github.com/ustc-time-series/Time-R1).
FULLBeyond Noisy Temporal Contexts: Selective Event-Level Revision for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
Jian Chen (Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics & Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yixiao Ren (Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics & Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yi Wang (Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics & Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yunfei Han (Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics & Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Yupeng Ma (Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics & Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Textual context can enhance time series forecasting when future dynamics are shaped by external events. In realistic forecasting pipelines, however, such context is typically retrieved rather than synchronously observed. Retrieved text is often sparse, temporally misaligned, and entangled with stale or non-predictive background information, making conventional multimodal fusion prone to negative transfer. We argue that the central challenge in multimodal forecasting is not to design increasingly sophisticated fusion mechanisms, but to determine when external textual context should revise a numerical forecast.To address this challenge, we propose Temporal Contextual Event Fusion (TCEF), an asymmetric selective revision framework that allows external textual context to influence numerical forecasts only when supported by relevant event evidence. TCEF first distills raw retrieved text into discrete timestamped events and estimates their horizon-specific relevance by jointly modeling event semantics, temporal recency, and the current state of the target series. Rather than treating text as an unconstrained forecasting signal, TCEF employs a prior-anchored revision branch to generate bounded residual corrections over a reliable numerical baseline. A reliability-guided trust gate then adaptively modulates textual influence across forecasting horizons, attenuating stale, weakly aligned, or uninformative signals while preserving the predictive structure of the temporal backbone.Experiments across nine Time-MMD domains and six temporal forecasting backbones show that TCEF consistently outperforms numeric-only forecasting and performs strongly against recent multimodal baselines. Further analysis shows that these gains are primarily driven by selective event-level revision rather than by simply incorporating more textual context.
FULLKoopman-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
Haokai Wang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Chang Fang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Wangqiu Zhou (Hefei University of Technology) · Yufan Wang (University of Science and Technology of China) · Qi Song (University of Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
While diffusion models have achieved impressive success in probabilistic time series forecasting, directly applying conventional noise injection may disrupt the continuity inherent in temporal data. Fundamentally, such additive Gaussian perturbations may sever the underlying dynamic continuity, generating intermediate states that are misaligned with the system's inherent evolution and making the recovery of valid sequential evolution exceptionally difficult. To resolve this misalignment, we introduce Koopman-Guided Diffusion (KoopDiff), a novel framework that restricts the generative process within an evolution-aligned subspace. Grounded in Koopman operator theory, our method lifts the diffusion dynamics into a coherent subspace where complex temporal dependencies are approximately linearized. Specifically, we establish this dynamically stable subspace by optimizing a Dynamical Subspace Alignment (DSA) objective, with analytical Koopman predictions serving as a Dynamical Prior to guide generative trajectories. Both theoretical analysis and a case study demonstrate that this formulation aligns the propagated noise with the dominant transition directions of the system, effectively maintaining dynamic continuity throughout the generative process. Extensive experiments on eight datasets show that KoopDiff achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance while substantially enhancing inference efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/khwhk/KoopDiff.
