APPLIEDJointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework
Siyun Yang (Kuaishou Technology) · Shixiao Yang (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Jian Wang (Kuaishou Technology) · Di Fan (Kuaishou Technology) · Kehe Cai (Kuaishou Technology) · Haoyan Fu (Beijing Institute of Technology) · Jiaming Zhang (Kuaishou Technology) · Wenjin Wu (Kuaishou Technology) · Peng Jiang (Independent Researcher)
Abstract
In online advertising, marketing interventions such as coupons introduce significant confounding bias into Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction. Observed clicks reflect a mixture of users' intrinsic preferences and the uplift induced by these interventions. This causes conventional models to miscalibrate base CTRs, which distorts downstream ranking and billing decisions. Furthermore, marketing interventions often operate as multi-valued treatments with varying magnitudes, introducing additional complexity to CTR prediction. To address these issues, we propose the Unified Multi-Valued Treatment Network (UniMVT). Specifically, UniMVT disentangles confounding factors from treatment-sensitive representations, enabling a full-space counterfactual inference module to jointly reconstruct the debiased base CTR and intensity-response curves. To handle the complexity of multi-valued treatments, UniMVT employs an auxiliary intensity estimation task to capture treatment propensities and devise a unit uplift objective that normalizes the intervention effect. This ensures comparable estimation across the continuous coupon-value spectrum. UniMVT simultaneously achieves debiased CTR prediction for accurate system calibration and precise uplift estimation for incentive allocation. Extensive experiments on synthetic and industrial datasets demonstrate UniMVT's superiority in both predictive accuracy and calibration. Furthermore, real-world A/B tests confirm that UniMVT significantly improves business metrics through more effective coupon distribution.
APPLIEDTUGB: A Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding Framework
Luzhan Yuan (JD.com) · Chao Mi (JD.com) · Xiahao Shi (JD.com) · Yi Mao (JD.com) · Shengsheng Niu (JD.com) · Xin Zhu (JD.com) · Jie He (JD.com) · Zhangang Lin (JD.com) · Ching Law (JD.com)
Abstract
Generative modeling, particularly Decision Transformers, shows promise in auto-bidding strategies. However, it struggles with limited exploration in static offline datasets, vulnerability to dynamic environmental shifts, and a reliance on heuristic return-to-go (RTG) specifications that may yield suboptimal performance on unseen traffic. To address these challenges, we propose the Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding (TUGB) framework. TUGB integrates generative sequence modeling with Reinforcement Learning (RL). It employs a two-stage pipeline where a pre-trained Generative Bidding Model is fine-tuned via an ensemble-based Uncertainty-aware Environment Model. This approach quantifies epistemic uncertainty to penalize high-risk trajectories and evolves the policy from RTG-conditioning to direct bidding optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TUGB significantly outperforms SOTA baselines. Notably, full-scale deployment on JD Search Ads achieved a 2.32% increase in cost and 3.57% in target cost, validating its industrial efficacy, while its successful adaptation to subsequent mechanism upgrades and JD Food Delivery Ads further validates TUGB's superior generalization capability.
APPLIEDHOB: A Holistically Optimized Bidding Strategy under Heterogeneous Bidding Environments
Qi Li (Alibaba Group) · Wendong Huang (Tsinghua University) · Qichen Ye (Alibaba Group) · Wutong Xu (Tsinghua University) · Rongquan Bai (Alibaba Group) · Cheems Wang (Tsinghua University) · Wei Yuan (Alibaba Group) · Miao Xu (Alibaba Group) · Zhiyu Mou (Alibaba Group) · Guan Wang (Alibaba Group) · Chuan Yu (Alibaba Group) · Jian Xu (Alibaba Group)
Abstract
Optimizing a single advertising campaign across heterogeneous channels is a central challenge in industrial autobidding. Auction mechanisms vary across channels in ranking rules (pure eCPM vs. UE-augmented scoring), pricing formats (first- vs. second-price), and bidding conventions (uniform vs. non-uniform), while advertisers impose shared campaign-level constraints. We propose HOB, which makes marginal cost (MC) computable and alignable across heterogeneous channels, especially for first-price auctions (FPA) with organic–paid coexistence, where existing bidding formulations do not yield a practical aligned MC form. At the global level, HOB derives channel-specific MC forms and coordinates disparate channels through a shared MC target. At the local level, HOB models free-win probability and winning-price uncertainty with a zero-inflated exponential distribution, yielding an efficient surplus-optimal bidding strategy for non-uniform first-price auctions. We show that any interior optimum satisfies MC equalization across channels. Experiments on a controlled offline benchmark, industrial log replay, and large-scale online A/B tests demonstrate that HOB consistently delivers significant performance gains. Deployed on a large-scale commercial DSP, HOB delivers a 3.0% lift in GMV while maintaining return on advertising spend (ROAS) constraints.
APPLIEDBidding-Aware Retrieval for Multi-Stage Consistency in Online Advertising
Bin Liu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Yunfei Liu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Ziru Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Zhi Kou (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Yeqiu Yang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Han Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jian Xu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
Online advertising systems typically use a cascaded architecture to manage massive requests and candidate volumes, where the ranking stages allocate traffic based on eCPM (predicted CTR × Bid). With the increasing popularity of auto-bidding strategies, the discrepancy between the computationally sensitive retrieval stage and the ranking stages becomes increasingly critical, as the former cannot access precise, real-time bids for the vast ad corpus. This misalignment inevitably leads to revenue leakage for the platform and sub-optimal ROI for advertisers. To tackle this problem, we propose Bidding-Aware Retrieval (BAR), a model-based retrieval framework that addresses multi-stage discrepancy by incorporating ad bid value into the retrieval scoring function. The core innovation is Bidding-Aware Modeling, utilizing bid signals through monotonicity-constrained learning and multi-task distillation to ensure economically coherent representations, while Asynchronous Near-Line Inference enables real-time updates to the embedding for market responsiveness. Furthermore, the Task-Attentive Refinement module selectively enhances feature interactions to disentangle user interest and commercial value signals. Extensive offline experiments and full-scale deployment across Alibaba's display advertising platform validated BAR's efficacy: 4.32% platform revenue increase, with a 22.2 percentage-point gain in the Impression Improved Ratio for ads receiving positive operational adjustments.
APPLIEDMine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Semantic Search Retrieval
Jiaqi Xi (DoorDash Inc.) · Raghav Saboo (DoorDash Inc.) · Luming Chen (DoorDash Inc.) · Johny Rufus (DoorDash Inc.) · Aditya Dodda (DoorDash Inc.) · Ved Sampath (DoorDash Inc.) · Kenny Chi (DoorDash Inc.) · Elyse Winer (DoorDash Inc.) · Akshad Viswanathan (DoorDash Inc.) · Martin Wang (DoorDash Inc.) · Sudeep Das (DoorDash Inc.)
Abstract
Embedding-based retrieval (EBR) for large-scale e-commerce search faces three intertwined challenges: graded (non-binary) relevance where engagement signals are noisy and intent-varying while business relevance guidelines admit acceptable-but-not-exact matches, false negatives in hard sample mining, and unstable similarity score separability across relevance levels, the last of which complicates hybrid search score fusion and downstream ranking. We propose Mine and Refine, a two-stage contrastive training framework that addresses all three. A lightweight LLM, fine-tuned with engagement-driven audit, serves as a guideline-aligned scalable labeler throughout training. Stage 1 establishes a robust global embedding space via label-aware supervised contrastive learning; Stage 2 mines hard samples, re-annotates them with the LLM labeler to mitigate spurious negatives, and refines the model through a multi-level extension of circle loss that enforces margin-controlled separation across relevance levels. Deployed in production e-commerce search across multiple product verticals, the approach delivers statistically significant lifts in user engagement and gross order value, and substantially improves retrieval and end-to-end relevance metrics.
APPLIEDBridging Queries and Brands: Entity Linking for Large-Scale Product Search
Dong Liu (Amazon) · Sreyashi Nag (Amazon)
Abstract
Associating user search queries with the correct brand entity is critical for e-commerce product retrieval, yet remains challenging due to the brevity of queries (three to four words on average), their lack of grammatical structure, and a catalog of hundreds of thousands of distinct brands. We formulate this as a brand entity linking task and develop two complementary solutions deployed at scale: (1) a cascaded pipeline that first detects brand mentions via sequence labeling and then disambiguates against a brand knowledge base, and (2) a single-stage approach that frames linking as extreme multi-class classification, directly mapping queries to brand identifiers. Through extensive multilingual evaluation (11 languages) and a controlled online experiment, we demonstrate that the proposed methods substantially improve brand recall while maintaining high precision, leading to measurable gains in customer engagement.
APPLIEDSAM-D2Q: Aligning Multimodal Doc2Query with Search Demand and Conversion for E-commerce
Hui Zhou (Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group) · Jian Hui Ji (Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group) · Lei Ma (Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group) · Rong Xiao (Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group) · Xiaoyi Zeng (Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group)
Abstract
E-commerce search often suffers from vocabulary mismatch between user queries and merchant-authored product titles, since short titles cannot fully cover diverse user expressions or visual product attributes. Although Doc2Query alleviates this issue by generating pseudo-queries for document expansion, traditional methods are text-only and not optimized for e-commerce business objectives. As a result, they may produce semantically plausible but commercially ineffective expansions and miss key attributes present in product images. To this end, we propose E-commerce Search-Aligned Multimodal Doc2Query (SAM-D2Q), a business-aligned multimodal document expansion framework for e-commerce search under Boolean retrieval constraints. SAM-D2Q consists of three stages: (1) task-adapted multimodal supervised fine-tuning to enhance vision-language understanding of product titles, images, and user queries; (2) multimodal data augmentation to improve perception of key visual attributes and expansion coverage; and (3) reinforcement-learning-based preference alignment toward search business objectives, encouraging the model to generate pseudo-queries that better match user intent and commercial value. Offline experiments show that SAM-D2Q substantially improves retrieval performance over traditional Doc2Query methods. Deployed in the AliExpress production search system, SAM-D2Q improves online business metrics, increasing GMV by +3.38% and Pay Count by +2.27%.
APPLIEDLEAPS: An LLM-Empowered Adaptive Plugin in Taobao AI Search
Lei Wang (Taobao & Tmall Group, Alibaba) · Jinhang Wu (Taobao & Tmall Group, Alibaba) · Zhibin Wang (Taobao & Tmall Group, Alibaba) · Biye Li (Taobao & Tmall Group, Alibaba)
Abstract
The rapid rise of large language models has shifted user search behavior from discrete keywords to natural-language, multi-constraint queries—a shift existing e-commerce search architectures struggle to accommodate. Users face a dilemma: precise natural-language queries often trigger zero-result scenarios, while forced simplification yields noisy, generic results that overwhelm decision-making. To address this, we propose LEAPS (LLM-Empowered Adaptive Plugin in Taobao AI Search), which upgrades traditional search pipelines via a "Broaden-and-Refine" paradigm by attaching plugins at both ends. (1) Upstream, a Query Expander generates adaptive, complementary query combinations to maximize the candidate set, trained via a three-stage strategy of inverse data augmentation, posterior-knowledge supervised fine-tuning, and diversity-aware reinforcement learning. (2) Downstream, a Relevance Verifier filters noise by synthesizing multi-source signals (e.g., OCR text, reviews) with chain-of-thought reasoning. Extensive offline experiments and online A/B testing show that LEAPS significantly enhances the conversational shopping experience, while its non-intrusive architecture preserves established short-text retrieval performance and enables low-cost integration with diverse back-ends. Fully deployed on Taobao AI Search since August 2025, LEAPS serves hundreds of millions of users monthly.
APPLIEDGraph-GRPO: Dependency-Aware Credit Assignment for Generative E-commerce Search Relevance
Jiarui Che (Nankai University) · Yifei Chen (JD.COM) · Zhixing Tian (JD.COM) · Chenyang Wang (JD.COM) · Ziguang Cheng (JD.COM)
Abstract
Search relevance modeling is a core task in e-commerce search systems, assessing how well a user query matches candidate products. Rather than relying on a single holistic matching signal, relevance judgment often requires structured reasoning over query understanding, product understanding, and facet-level matching. With large language models (LLMs), this process is increasingly formulated as chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and optimized with reinforcement learning (RL). However, existing RL methods mainly rely on outcome-level rewards and treat the entire reasoning chain as a single optimization unit. This makes it difficult to distinguish faulty reasoning steps from correct intermediate ones, leading to misaligned credit assignment. Although process-reward methods provide denser supervision, they often treat reasoning steps independently and ignore dependency-driven error propagation, making responsibility attribution difficult and limiting the optimization of structured relevance reasoning. </par> <par>We propose Graph-GRPO, a graph-structured extension of GRPO for multi-component relevance reasoning. Graph-GRPO constructs a relevance reasoning dependency graph, where CoT steps are modeled as nodes and their logical dependencies as edges. It propagates outcome-level rewards over the graph to derive step-level credit signals, enabling more accurate fine-grained credit assignment. We further introduce a main-loss-driven controller that adaptively adjusts edge-wise credit-propagation coefficients. Together with CoT random masking for supervised policy initialization and graph-node-based multi-head distillation, we build a trainable and deployable framework for generative relevance modeling. Extensive offline evaluations and online A/B tests on a leading e-commerce platform demonstrate that the Graph-GRPO-based framework improves relevance classification metrics and key engagement metrics. The resulting lightweight model has been deployed in the JD e-commerce search system, serving hundreds of millions of users.
APPLIEDEfficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL
Jianbo Zhu (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Xing Fang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Jing Wang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Mingmin Jin (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Bokang Wang (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Guangxin Song (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Zhenyu Xie (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba) · Junjie Bai (Taobao & Tmall Group of Alibaba)
Abstract
Generative retrieval offers a promising alternative by unifying the multi-stage retrieval process into a single end-to-end model. However, its practical adoption in industrial e-commerce search remains challenging, given the massive and dynamic product catalogs, strict latency requirements, and the need to align retrieval with downstream ranking goals. In this work, we propose a retrieval framework tailored for real-world recall scenarios, positioning generative retrieval as a recall-stage supplement rather than an end-to-end replacement. Our method, CQ-SID (Category-and-Query constrained Semantic ID), employs category-aware and query-item contrastive learning along with Residual Quantized VAEs to encode items into hierarchical semantic cluster identifiers, significantly improving click and exposure metrics and reducing beam search size and inference time. Additionally, we develop EG-GRPO (Expert-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization), a reinforcement learning approach that aligns generative recall with downstream ranking under sparse rewards by injecting ground-truth samples to stabilize training. Offline experiments on TmallAPP search logs show that CQ-SID achieves up to 26.76% and 11.11% relative gains in semantic and personalized click hitrate over RQ-VAE baselines. EG-GRPO further improves multi-objective performance. Online A/B tests confirm gains in GMV (+1.15%) and UCTCVR (+0.40%). The generative recall channel now contributes substantially in production, accounting for 50.25% of exposures, 58.96% of clicks, and 72.63% of purchases, demonstrating a viable path for deploying generative retrieval in real-world e-commerce systems.
APPLIEDSSR-GRPO: Integrating Supervision and Semantic IDs into Reinforcement Learning for Dense Retrieval in E-commerce
Guangxin Song (Alibaba Group) · Xing Fang (Alibaba Group) · Mingming Jin (Alibaba Group) · Jing Wang (Alibaba Group) · Bokang Wang (Alibaba Group) · Zhentao Song (Alibaba Group) · Junjie Bai (Alibaba Group) · Jianbo Zhu (Alibaba Group)
Abstract
Embedding-based retrieval (EBR) is a prevailing method in modern e-commerce search, retrieving relevant items from billions of candidates in response to users' queries. While recent methods often fine-tune large language models (LLMs) for representation learning, they typically lack robust mechanisms for handling complex and implicit semantics. To address this, Retrieval-GRPO (R-GRPO) was recently proposed as a multi-objective Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for dense retrieval. It computes rewards using top-K items dynamically retrieved per query. While this approach partially mitigates retrieval challenges, the limited candidate pool sampled per batch often introduces noisy samples into the top-K results. Moreover, the LLM used for computing relevance rewards in R-GRPO is trained with an RL framework similar to R-GRPO itself. This inherent similarity makes it difficult to provide unbiased and impartial assessment results. To tackle these issues, we propose Supervised Retrieval-GRPO with Semantic Identifiers (SSR-GRPO). Specifically, our method first proposes a dual-perspective framework for relevance assessment. It leverages both Semantic Identifiers (SIDs) produced by quantization learning and dense representation vectors to generate more unbiased relevance scores. Furthermore, leveraging the hierarchical similarity relationships of the generated SIDs, we mine a set of hard negative samples that serve two purposes: (1) to design a masking function integrated into R-GRPO, effectively filtering intra-group noisy samples; and (2) to construct a Retrieval-DPO task composed of positive and negative sample pairs, enabling the model to capture fine-grained semantic distinctions from a pair-wise perspective. By integrating these optimization strategies, we propose SSR-GRPO. Extensive offline and online experiments validate SSR-GRPO's effectiveness, and it has been deployed on a large-scale e-commerce platform.
APPLIEDSemantic Search At LinkedIn
Fedor Borisyuk (LinkedIn) · Sriram Vasudevan (LinkedIn) · Muchen Wu (LinkedIn) · Guoyao Li (LinkedIn) · Benjamin Le (LinkedIn) · Shaobo Zhang (LinkedIn) · Qianqi Kay Shen (LinkedIn) · Yuchin Juan (LinkedIn) · Kayhan Behdin (LinkedIn) · Liming Dong (LinkedIn) · Kaixu Yang (LinkedIn) · Shusen Jing (LinkedIn) · Ravi Pothamsetty (LinkedIn) · Rajat Arora (LinkedIn) · Sophie Yanying Sheng (LinkedIn) · Vitaly Abdrashitov (LinkedIn) · Yang Zhao (LinkedIn) · Lin Su (LinkedIn) · Xiaoqing Wang (LinkedIn) · Chujie Zheng (LinkedIn) · Sarang Metkar (LinkedIn) · Rupesh Gupta (LinkedIn) · Igor Lapchuk (LinkedIn) · David N. Racca (LinkedIn) · Madhumitha Mohan (LinkedIn) · Yanbo Li (LinkedIn) · Haojun Li (LinkedIn) · Saloni Gandhi (LinkedIn) · Xueying Lu (LinkedIn) · Chetan Bhole (LinkedIn) · Ali Hooshmand (LinkedIn) · Xin Yang (LinkedIn) · Raghavan Muthuregunathan (LinkedIn) · Jiajun Zhang (LinkedIn) · Mathew Teoh (LinkedIn) · Adam Coler (LinkedIn) · Abhinav Gupta (LinkedIn) · Xiaojing Ma (LinkedIn) · Sundara Raman Ramachandran (LinkedIn) · Morteza Ramezani (LinkedIn) · Yubo Wang (LinkedIn) · Lijuan Zhang (LinkedIn) · Richard Li (LinkedIn) · Jian Sheng (LinkedIn) · Chanh Nguyen (LinkedIn) · Yen-Chi Chen (LinkedIn) · Chuanrui Zhu (LinkedIn) · Claire Zhang (LinkedIn) · Jiahao Xu (LinkedIn) · Deepti Kulkarni (LinkedIn) · Qing Lan (LinkedIn) · Arvind Subramaniam (LinkedIn) · Ata Fatahibaarzi (LinkedIn) · Steven Shimizu (LinkedIn) · Yanning Chen (LinkedIn) · Zhipeng Wang (LinkedIn) · Ran He (LinkedIn) · Zhengze Zhou (LinkedIn) · Qingquan Song (LinkedIn) · Yun Dai (LinkedIn) · Caleb Johnson (LinkedIn) · Ping Liu (LinkedIn) · Shaghayegh Gharghabi (LinkedIn) · Gokulraj Mohanasundaram (LinkedIn) · Juan Bottaro (LinkedIn) · Santhosh Sachindran (LinkedIn) · Qi Guo (LinkedIn) · Yunxiang Ren (LinkedIn) · Chengming Jiang (LinkedIn) · Di Mo (LinkedIn) · Luke Simon (LinkedIn) · Jianqiang Shen (LinkedIn) · Jingwei Wu (LinkedIn) · Wenjing Zhang (LinkedIn)
Abstract
Semantic search with large language models (LLMs) enables retrieval by meaning rather than keyword overlap, but scaling it requires major inference efficiency advances. We present LinkedIn’s LLM-based semantic search framework for AI Job Search and AI People Search, combining an LLM relevance judge, embedding-based retrieval, and a compact Small Language Model trained via multi-teacher distillation to jointly optimize relevance and engagement. A prefill-oriented inference architecture co-designed with model pruning, context compression, and text–embedding hybrid interactions boosts ranking throughput by over 75× under fixed latency constraint while preserving near–teacher-level NDCG, enabling one of the first production LLM-based ranking systems with efficiency comparable to traditional approaches and delivering significant gains in quality and user engagement.

FULLLatent Query Retrieval of Acoustic-Prosodic Evidence for Speech Toxicity Detection
Yunsu Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Shinyu Park (Sungkyunkwan University) · Jihyun Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Eunil Park (Sungkyunkwan University)
Abstract
Speech toxicity detection is increasingly important in real-time voice-based interactions, where harmful speech can affect listeners before an utterance is fully observed. Existing approaches often treat speech as either transcribed text or a single audio embedding. However, toxic expressions can be lexically diverse, while vocal delivery may contain recurring acoustic-prosodic cues such as intensity, stress, rhythm, voice quality, or sarcastic tone. Motivated by this, we propose a latent query-guided acoustic-prosodic retrieval framework that learns class-specific latent queries to retrieve prediction-relevant local cues from speech tokens without relying on ASR transcripts or manually written prompts. Experiments on the combined English DeToxy+MuTox datasets show that our framework outperforms single-encoder, fusion, and retrieval baselines and improves early detection under prefix cropping. Analyses further show that the learned queries attend to temporally diverse regions and capture acoustic-prosodic differences associated with toxic and non-toxic speech. Latency measurements also indicate a lower-latency alternative to ASR-based text pipelines for real-time toxicity detection.
FULLDeconstructing Harmful Memes: Fine-Grained Analysis of Subtle Semantics
Xiaofan Zheng (Xi'an Jiaotong University) · Xinghao Wang (Xi'an Jiaotong University) · Yanwei Liao (Xi'an Jiaotong University) · Minnan Luo (Xi'an Jiaotong University)
Abstract
Memes, widely shared on the internet as a form of cultural expression, present a challenge in identifying harmful content due to their compact format and subtle meanings. Current detection methods employ pre-trained models to extract image and text features from memes, subsequently combining these features through deep neural networks for classification. However, these approaches often overlook the underlying meanings embedded in memes, focusing solely on shallow semantics and surface-level harmful signals. This makes it difficult to capture the cultural connotations and subtle expressions inherent in memes. Moreover, they lack explanations for their judgments. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework for explainable harmful meme detection. This framework combines the advantages of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and fine-grained heterogeneous semantic graphs. By leveraging multi-hop reasoning, we utilize MLLMs' extensive knowledge to provide comprehensive meme analyses, addressing meme literacy gaps. We extract key objects, relationships, and attributes from images to produce detailed scene graphs, which support a deeper understanding of the meme. The fine-grained heterogeneous semantic graphs filter and integrate multiple information sources to uncover hidden harmful elements. Additionally, through multi-hop reasoning and scene graphs, our approach generates reliable explanations via MLLMs. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches on widely used datasets.
FULLSemantic-Guided Fine Alignment and Asymmetric Contrast for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation
Chengqiuze Du (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Hongru Ji (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Yuyin Fan (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Huixiang Zhang (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Chao Gao (Northwestern Polytechnical University)
Abstract
Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation (MERC) aims to identify the emotion of each speaker in every utterance by leveraging multimodal conversational signals. Existing methods typically employ graph structures to model contextual dialogue interactions; however, they often neglect fine-grained affective correspondences and implicitly assume equal reliability across modalities, making multimodal representations susceptible to modality-specific noise and semantic interference. To address these limitations, we propose SFAC, a semantic-guided fine alignment and asymmetric contrast framework with alignment-aware conversational graph modeling for MERC. Specifically, an optimal-transport-based fine-grained alignment objective captures flexible many-to-many correspondences among textual tokens, acoustic frames, and visual frames before conversational graph modeling. In addition, a semantic-guided asymmetric contrastive mechanism employs stop-gradient textual representations as semantic anchors to regularize acoustic and visual modalities after graph-based contextual reasoning, thereby preserving complementary multimodal information while mitigating interference from noisy auxiliary signals. Finally, the refined multimodal representations are fed into a decoder that formulates emotion recognition as an autoregressive text generation task. Extensive experiments on the IEMOCAP and MELD benchmarks demonstrate that SFAC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the effectiveness of semantic-guided fine alignment and asymmetric contrastive learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/SFAC.
FULLDGR-Net: Dynamic Gating and Retrieval-Enhanced Network for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
Xiangfeng Liu (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Shenjie Jiang (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Zhuoyu Wang (Fudan University) · Xianghua Li (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Huixiang Zhang (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Chao Gao (Northwestern Polytechnical University)
Abstract
Inferring human sentiment through the combined processing of language, audio, and vision signals is the core focus of multimodal sentiment analysis. Its effectiveness critically depends on high-quality multimodal representations that capture both modality-invariant and modality-specific features, while properly modeling the unequal contributions of different modalities. To address these challenges, we propose DGR-Net, a framework that jointly performs feature decomposition, hybrid dynamic gating, and complementary retrieval in a synergistic manner. Unlike prior purely work, our hybrid dynamic gating (HDG) module combines semantic attention with energy-based uncertainty for sample-level modality weighting, and our modality-specific retrieval (MSR) module is designed to selectively extract key cues from modality-specific features, thereby boosting the final prediction performance. Extensive experiments on MOSI and MOSEI demonstrate that DGR-Net achieves highly competitive performance and validate the contribution of each proposed module. Code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/DGR-Net.
FULLVGMR: Cross-Modal Value-Gated Modality Refiner for Robust Multimodal Learning
Jiyuan Liu (Adelaide University) · Liangwei Zheng (Adelaide University) · Wei Emma Zhang (Adelaide University) · Xinpei Wang (Shandong University) · Weitong Chen (Adelaide University)
Abstract
Multimodal learning combines heterogeneous signals, such as text, audio, and vision, to improve prediction. However, adding modalities does not always help, because modalities may contain useful complementary cues together with noisy, redundant, or contextually unreliable components that interfere with full-modality learning. In this work, we propose Cross-Modal Value-Gated Modality Refiner (VGMR), a pre-fusion refinement module that estimates context-conditioned value evidence before modality features enter the backbone. VGMR models summary-level cross-modal agreement and discrepancy, estimates global-level and channel-level value signals, and uses them with raw and projected features to generate fine-grained gates over the original modality features. Different from conventional attention or generic gating, VGMR treats value as signed, context-conditioned impact evidence rather than a direct preservation probability, allowing the gate generator to learn whether each component should be enhanced, retained, or suppressed. We evaluate VGMR on MOSI and MOSEI with a Transformer backbone, and on MOSI, MOSEI, UCF101, AVE, and CREMA-D with a ResNet+Concat backbone. On MOSEI with the Transformer backbone, VGMR achieves 0.8446 Accuracy and 0.8029 Macro-F1, outperforming the strongest baselines by 1.09 and 0.89 percentage points, respectively. Ablation, controlled comparison, modality removal, noise robustness, optimization, and qualitative analyses suggest that VGMR can reduce unreliable modality responses before fusion and improve robustness under noisy multimodal inputs.
FULLRebalancing Multimodal Learning via Adaptive Bidirectional Alignment
Yuhan Zheng (Nanjing University of Science and Technology) · Yang Yang (Nanjing University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Multimodal learning often suffers from modality imbalance, leading to an optimization dilemma. A key reason is that different modalities exhibit asynchronous learning dynamics during joint training. A representative line of existing methods seeks to rebalance multimodal learning through cross-modal alignment. However, such alignment is usually imposed in a static, symmetric, and fully coupled manner, making it prone to unreliable cross-modal interactions. To address this issue, we argue that cross-modal alignment under modality imbalance should be space-aware and status-aware, reducing feature-space discrepancy while selectively aligning transferable components according to modality learning status. Based on this principle, we propose an Adaptive Bidirectional Alignment (ABA) method. ABA first constructs class-conditional statistical projections to establish more robust semantic correspondences between heterogeneous modality spaces. It then employs feature-level partial optimal transport to selectively align reliable and transferable feature components. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic bidirectional regulation mechanism to adaptively adjust the direction and strength of cross-modal knowledge transfer according to modality learning status, enabling more effective cross-modal collaboration. Empirical experiments on widely used datasets reveal the superiority of our method through comparison with various state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal learning baselines. The source code is available at our repository (https://github.com/yilnr/ABA)
FULLAccelerating Feature Aggregation for Imbalanced Multimodal Learning
Xinger Li (Nanjing University of Science and Technology) · Xiaoxue Wei (Nanjing University of Science and Technology) · Qi Yan (Nanjing University of Science and Technology) · Yang Yang (Nanjing University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Imbalanced multimodal learning remains a critical challenge, as models often over-rely on dominant modality while under optimizing non-dominant one, ultimately limiting overall performance. Essentially, we observe that such over-reliance is closely associated with discrepancies in feature aggregation capability across modalities. More concretely, non-dominant modality lags in forming compact and stable representations, whereas dominant modality exhibits superior aggregation capability. To address this issue, we propose a simple yet effective approach called Dynamic Sample Retrieval for Efficient Feature Aggregation (DSR-EFA). Specifically, we first introduce a retrieval-driven near-neighbor sample augmentation strategy to build a candidate pool for each modality. Based on these pools, we propose a modality-aware dynamic ensemble scheme that allocates retrieval budget according to modality importance and constructs additional informative samples for classification. Consequently, DSR-EFA effectively reduces feature aggregation disparities and improves multimodal learning performance. Extensive experiments on widely used datasets verify the effectiveness of DSR-EFA.
FULLMultimodal Active Learning via Emotion-Aware Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning
Meiyun Zuo (Renmin University of China) · Shao Chen (Renmin University of China) · Suyun Zhao (Renmin University of China) · Chenlong Li (Renmin University of China)
Abstract
Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) leverages diverse modalities such as text, vision, and audio to infer emotional states, yet suffers from prohibitively high annotation costs. As a promising solution, Active Learning (AL) strategically selects the most valuable data for annotation, enabling competitive model performance with substantially reduced labeling effort. To address this issue, this study proposes MALCC, a novel multimodal active learning framework that leverages emotion-aware cross-modal contrastive learning for emotion recognition. Specifically, to achieve task-specific alignment across modalities, we first design an emotion-aware cross-modal contrastive learning module, which embeds multiple modalities into a unified emotion-aligned representation space. Within this space, we propose a comprehensive reliability-aware query strategy that prioritizes cross-modal semantic consistency and modality contribution balance as two key reliability criteria, while incorporating informativeness and representativeness as complementary utility criteria to select more valuable instances for annotation. By leveraging this strategy, we then design a novel multimodal active learning algorithm tailored for emotion recognition. We further provide theoretical analysis to justify our design and conduct extensive experiments on three widely used MER datasets, demonstrating superior performance over state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Our code and supplementary materials are available at https://github.com/Atlantis-esh/malcc0425.

FULLTRACE: Tracing Temporal Constraints for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
Shiqi Fan (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University) · Shi Li (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University) · Xiangzhi Mao (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Zeqing Zhang (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Hongyi Nie (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Tong Li (Northwestern Polytechnical University) · Wen Hua (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
Abstract
Complex temporal knowledge graph question answering (TKGQA) requires composing multiple time-dependent facts under constraints such as validity intervals, temporal ordering, overlap, and set-style operations. Recent LLM-based approaches improve temporal reasoning through retrieval, decomposition, or planning, but the temporal constraints produced during intermediate reasoning are often left implicit: retrieved evidence may be temporally invalid, intermediate answers may be propagated without verification, and deterministic temporal operations may still be handled by free-form generation. We propose TRACE, a temporal-constraint-aware recursive framework that traces temporal constraints across retrieval, answer verification, constraint propagation, and execution. TRACE grounds temporal anchors and operators from sub-questions and intermediate answers, performs operator-aware temporal retrieval, verifies child-derived answers using grounding, bridge evidence, and operator consistency, and invokes symbolic temporal execution when root-level temporal operations are deterministically resolvable. Experiments on MultiTQ and TimelineKGQA show that TRACE improves multi-step and operator-sensitive temporal reasoning under the evaluated settings. Detailed analyses further show that verified answer propagation reduces error accumulation, while symbolic temporal execution is particularly effective for compositional temporal relations such as intersection and union. These results demonstrate that complex TKGQA benefits not only from retrieving or decomposing temporal questions, but also from explicitly tracing, verifying, and executing temporal constraints throughout the reasoning process.
FULLTime-Constrained Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
Tianjie Yan (Fudan University) · Chengrong Wu (Fudan University)
Abstract
Temporal question answering over temporal knowledge graphs (TKGQA) requires retrieving evidence that is not only semantically relevant but also temporally valid. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approaches primarily rely on semantic retrieval and often fail to enforce temporal constraints during retrieval, leading to temporally inconsistent evidence, especially for questions involving multiple events and implicit temporal dependencies. In this paper, we propose a time-constrained retrieval-augmented question answering framework for temporal knowledge graphs. Given a temporal question, our method decomposes it into an ordered sequence of structured event queries, each optionally associated with a temporal constraint and an event-time variable. Retrieval is conducted in a stepwise manner, where temporal constraints are enforced throughout the retrieval process via hard temporal filtering followed by semantic--temporal fusion re-ranking. Semantic relevance is modeled jointly from entity-, relation-, and sentence-level representations, while temporal relevance is incorporated as an additional ranking signal. We evaluate our approach on two temporal question answering benchmarks, MultiTQ and CronQuestions. CronQuestions involves year-level interval facts, whereas MultiTQ uses day-level time-stamped facts and includes questions with mixed temporal granularities and compositional temporal constraints. Experimental results show that our method achieves the best overall Hits@1 among the compared methods on both benchmarks. Ablation studies on MultiTQ further validate the effectiveness of structured temporal decomposition and time-constrained retrieval.
FULLSSR: Star-Shaped Rules for Link Prediction on Temporal Knowledge Graphs
Qinghao Chi (Beihang University) · Chenglin Liu (Beihang University) · Ting Deng (Beihang University) · Ping Lu (Beihang University) · Yutong Ye (Beihang University) · Chao Tian (The Queen's University Belfast)
Abstract
Link prediction on temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs), a.k.a. TKG link prediction, aims to predict missing facts from historical facts. Existing rule-based methods mainly rely on sequential temporal rules that propagate variables along chronological paths. However, such path-shaped rules cannot naturally capture a common prediction pattern in which a historical source-target interaction first identifies a candidate target, while subsequent source-side events provide contextual support before the query time. In this paper, we propose a new class of star-shaped temporal rules (SSRs) for TKG link prediction and a rule-based framework called PLSSR that discovers and applies SSR rules for link prediction. To discover SSRs, PLSSR employs a top-k pattern growth strategy over localized contextual relations. During inference, SSR rules are aggregated through Noisy-OR scoring, while sparse candidate sets are supplemented using subject-history and relation-level target priors. Experimental results demonstrate that PLSSR outperforms current embedding-based, rule-based, and LLM-assisted baselines with average relative MRR gains of 78.3%, 66.4%, and 57.9%, respectively, while preserving explicit, interpretable reasoning traces.
FULLHiTS-CL: A Continual Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Temporal Knowledge Graph Extrapolation
Yansong Liu (Beihang University) · Rui Liu (Beihang University) · Yuan Zuo (Beihang University) · Hongwei Zhao (Beihang University) · Da Fu (Beihang University) · Fuwei Zhang (Beihang University) · Fuzhen Zhuang (Beihang University) · Yong Chen (Bejing University of Posts and Telecommunications) · Zhe Li (Hubei Engineering University)
Abstract
Extrapolative temporal knowledge graph reasoning (TKGR) predicts future facts from historical snapshots. Most existing methods train once on an early prefix of the timeline and then use a frozen model for all future timestamps. We argue that this fixed-prefix protocol is misaligned with extrapolation. It learns from a static prefix, whereas the target stream is non-stationary: new entities and facts emerge, temporal dependencies shift across regimes, and recurring historical signals must be refreshed online. As a result, models trained only on early snapshots become outdated and degrade over long horizons. We address this mismatch by formulating extrapolative TKGR as continual learning over streaming snapshots. Under this view, effective extrapolation must jointly handle current dynamics, stable knowledge, and recurring historical evidence. Based on these requirements, we propose History-enhanced Two-Step Continual Learning (HiTS-CL), a backbone-agnostic continual learning framework for extrapolative TKGR. HiTS-CL tracks current dynamics via continual fine-tuning, preserves stable knowledge via multi-teacher adaptive distillation, and retains recurring historical evidence via a selective memory of recent and frequent facts. We integrate HiTS-CL into five representative TKGR backbones and evaluate it on four benchmark datasets. HiTS-CL consistently improves extrapolation accuracy, reduces long-horizon degradation, and outperforms strong continual-learning baselines, including a recent method for temporal knowledge graphs. Source code and data are available at https://github.com/liuyansong98/HiTS-CL.
FULLHGNN-EAGE: Continual Event Knowledge Graph Evolution via Hypergraph Neural Evidence and Layered Alignment
Chunyan An (Inner Mongolia University) · Zhihong Hao (Inner Mongolia University) · Hui Yin (Inner Mongolia University) · Qiang Yang (University of Florida) · Zhixu Li (Renmin University of China)
Abstract
Event knowledge graphs (EKGs) must evolve continuously as new events emerge, while preserving temporal integrity and structural consistency. However, existing triple-completion and embedding approaches assume closed-world settings and lack mechanisms for open-world alignment and interpretable updates. Furthermore, real-world streaming data often suffers from out-of-order arrivals and information fragmentation, which exacerbates update conflicts and causal inversion in continuous evolution. We define the task of Continuous Event Knowledge Graph (C-EKG) Updating and introduce HGNN-EAGE, a unified framework that addresses these challenges through adaptive stream scheduling and hypergraph neural alignment. Specifically, we propose an adaptive dependency-aware sorting strategy that dynamically prioritizes information-rich and temporally antecedent events to initialize the topological basis. For event alignment, HGNN-EAGE models events as hyperedges and learns numerically stable embeddings via a degree-regularized hypergraph neural network. It decouples semantic, structural, temporal, spatial, type-level, salient-entity, and consistency cues into orthogonal evidence dimensions, driving a hierarchical decision process that maps interpretable alignment outcomes to atomic, version-controlled graph operations (insert, supplement, link-subevent). Extensive experiments on EventKG and DuEE-fin benchmarks demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms strong baselines in retrieval and classification accuracy. Moreover, the proposed streaming strategy substantially mitigates topological redundancy under high-load out-of-order data streams while maintaining near-linear scalability.
FULLFew-Shot Guided Knowledge Graph Population with Implicit Ontology Compliance from Partially Linked Tables
Simon Gottschalk (Leibniz Universität Hannover) · Yichen Zhong (Leibniz Universität Hannover) · Sara Abdollahi (Leibniz Universität Hannover) · Wolfgang Nejdl (Leibniz Universität Hannover)
Abstract
Knowledge graphs (KGs) rely on structured representations of entities and relations to enable effective information access and integration. Building and populating KGs from semi-structured sources such as tables remains a challenging task, particularly due to the need to adhere to strict ontology constraints on valid entity types and relations. Large Language Models (LLMs) provide strong capabilities for understanding and generalising from text, but ensuring that their outputs conform to a target KG schema without explicitly providing the full ontology remains an open problem. In this paper, we propose WikiTabLLM, a few-shot, example-driven framework for ontology-compliant knowledge graph population. Instead of explicitly specifying ontology constraints, WikiTabLLM leverages partially linked Wikipedia tables to implicitly induce valid typing and relation patterns. Each table is partitioned into (i) rows containing entities already linked to the Wikidata knowledge graph, which serve as in-context supervision signals, and (ii) rows with unlinked entities, for which we aim to generate RDF triples for KG population. WikiTabLLM learns to infer valid properties and relations by conditioning on the structured patterns exhibited in existing triples, effectively enforcing ontology compliance through examples. We evaluate WikiTabLLM on a newly constructed dataset of Wikipedia tables and compare against Semantic Table Interpretation, relation extraction baselines, and zero-shot LLM prompting. Results show that our approach produces more accurate and schema-consistent triples (up to a 3x improvement in macro F1), demonstrating the effectiveness of leveraging in-context examples to guide ontology-constrained knowledge graph population.
FULLGrOIL: Graph-Grounded Domain Ontology Induction with Constrained LLM Mediation
Maruf Ahmed Mridul (Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute) · Abid Talukder (Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute) · Oshani Seneviratne (Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute)
Abstract
Constructing formal ontologies from domain documents requires simultaneously enforcing corpus grounding, vocabulary consistency, axiom-level expressivity, and end-to-end provenance, a combination no existing automatic system delivers. We present a seven-stage graph-grounded pipeline that converts domain documents into a complete, auditable Web Ontology Language (OWL) Terminological Box (TBox) without any unconstrained generation step. Documents are first encoded as Unified Discourse-Hypergraphs (UDH) capturing entity participation and discourse dependencies; subsequent stages transform this graph evidence into a class hierarchy, typed object and datatype properties, and restriction axioms, with Large Language Model (LLM) usage restricted to narrow, graph-grounded mediation tasks. A paired Assertional Box (ABox) population procedure grounds named individuals in the induced TBox, enabling SPARQL-based functional evaluation. Every emitted term carries a full decision chain from raw source passages through each pipeline stage, making the TBox directly auditable and suitable for targeted human refinement. Evaluated on the life insurance domain using two established benchmarks and a new 100-contract corpus spanning ten product types, our pipeline achieves strong results across all evaluation dimensions, outperforming direct and multi-agent LLM baselines on competency-question (CQ) coverage (0.85 vs. 0.63 and 0.62 on one term-life contract; 0.77 vs. 0.40 and 0.44 on another contract), while also attaining high keyphrase coverage comparable to a manually-constructed reference ontology and strong performance on structured gap-and-overlap reasoning, all without any manual TBox engineering. Ontology growth analysis provides evidence consistent with vocabulary saturation at scale, demonstrating that the pipeline produces stable, reusable domain representations from large document corpora.
FULLTaxoEvolve: Self-Evolving Taxonomy based LLM Memory Construction for Continually Growing Corpora
Sajratul Yakin Rubaiat (University of Idaho) · Syed Nazmus Sakib (University of Idaho) · Hasan Jamil (University of Idaho)
Abstract
Modern LLM-based applications increasingly rely on external memory for storing prior interactions, user-provided files, enterprise records, and domain-specific documents that can be reused in later interactions. However, as memory grows, current infrastructures provide limited support for understanding what the memory contains, how it is organized, and where retrieved evidence comes from. Vector indexes expose memory mainly through flat top-k similarity search, Knowledge graphs often require predefined schemas and fine-grained conversion of raw information into entities and relations which is difficult to navigate, meanwhile existing taxonomy construction methods are commonly static or one-shot. These limitations make current approaches difficult to maintain for continuously growing LLM memory. We present TaxoEvolve, an incremental framework that organizes memory items into a self-evolving taxonomy. It routes items to existing nodes, creates classes for emerging concepts, and refines overloaded nodes using a distribution-based split score that favors coherent groups with enough support. The taxonomy exposes an inspectable, editable memory structure, allowing humans or LLM-based agents to browse, search selected regions, and trace evidence through class paths and history tags. On TaxoBench, TaxoEvolve achieves stronger organization quality than clustering-based and LLM-based baselines, while some one-shot LLM baselines cannot process the full input due to context-window limits. Across scientific, medical, and financial retrieval tasks, taxonomy-guided search improves Recall@20, reaching 0.918 with hybrid retrieval and 0.923 with tag-aware retrieval.

FULLAdaptive-Path Wavelet Interpretation Maps for Auditing Neural Content Scorers
Zhibo Jin (University of Technology Sydney) · Zhiyu Zhu (University of Technology Sydney) · Jiayu Zhang (Suzhou University of Technology) · Huijie Xu (University of Technology Sydney) · Biaoliang Chen (University of Technology Sydney) · Nan Yang (The University of Sydney) · Fang Chen (University of Technology Sydney) · Jianlong Zhou (University of Technology Sydney)
Abstract
Modern information and knowledge systems increasingly rely on frozen neural content scorers to rank, filter, recommend, moderate, and curate image, audio, and multimedia content. For trustworthy deployment, operators need attribution tools that explain not only salient input regions, but which structured signal components can locally restore or strengthen the scalar scores consumed by downstream ranking, filtering, and human-review workflows. We propose Adaptive-Path Wavelet Interpretation Maps (AP-WIM), a reference-input-free attribution method that computes nonnegative ascent-sensitivity maps in an invertible wavelet coefficient space. AP-WIM starts from the observed sample, advances along the local gradient field under an amplitude-proportional budget, and accumulates score-increasing sensitivity for input-aligned frequency-structured heatmaps. We characterize the origin-neighborhood risk of zero-baseline straight-line paths and, under local smoothness, derive a conditional score-improvement lower bound; the sign update is first-order optimal within its prescribed coordinate-wise budget box. On ESC-50 audio classifiers, paired-bootstrap tests show significant insertion gains under community-standard perturbation protocols, and a five-fold attribution stability check confirms that the insertion advantage is not unique to one audio fold. On a scorer-level Tiny-ImageNet query-gallery ranking audit, AP-WIM achieves the highest mean insertion AUC across target-score, Recall@1/5, MRR, and nDCG@10 endpoints, and significantly improves relevant-item score restoration over the strongest non-AP baseline. Together, the ranking audit, multimodal attribution benchmarks, runtime measurements, and robustness checks position AP-WIM as a resource-aware, frequency-structured explainability interface for frozen neural content-scoring pipelines. Code is available at: https://github.com/Davidjinzb/AP-WIM.
FULLGenerating Intervention Hypotheses using Explainable Explanations on Graphs: G2I, a Two-Stage Greedy Framework
Mulin Tian (University of Southern California) · Ajitesh Srivastava (Northeastern University)
Abstract
Real-world decision-making in public health and social science can greatly benefit from predictive models, yet translating predictions into effective interventions requires explaining the model behavior. While Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are well-suited for modeling relational data, existing explanation methods largely operate at the node level and fall short of supporting actionable, network-level intervention design. Existing counterfactual GNN explainers, such as CF-GNNExplainer and CF2, rely on continuous mask optimization over features and edges, which implicitly assume feasible edge manipulation, may allocate effort to immutable or non-actionable attributes, and incur substantial computational overhead. Further, the method of arriving at the explanation itself is difficult to explain to a domain specialist who is not an AI expert. Can simple methods generate good explanations? To explore this, we reframe counterfactual explanation as an intervention design problem. At the local level, we generate counterfactuals via a greedy search that directly identifies minimal, actionable changes to node features and neighbor-level conditions. We derive conditions under which the greedy search provides guarantees, and empirically show that these conditions are approximately met. These counterfactuals are converted into interpretable rules suitable for real-world intervention. At the network level, we formulate intervention selection as a Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF) coverage problem under a budget constraint, which is nondecreasing and approximately submodular, enabling a greedy algorithm with theoretical guarantees. Experiments on synthetic graphs and real-world suicide risk networks demonstrate that our approach produces scalable, cost-effective intervention strategies with significantly improved efficiency over mask-based counterfactual methods.
FULLAHFI: Adaptive Hierarchical Fairness Intervention for Fair Graph Neural Networks
Zihao Huang (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Ke Lu (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences) · Jian Xue (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)
Abstract
Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are widely used for learning from relational data, but they can also propagate and amplify biases associated with sensitive attributes. Recent fair GNNs have moved from single-level debiasing toward multi-level intervention, but the strength of these interventions is still commonly governed by fixed coefficients, task-specific modules, or manually selected objectives. We propose Adaptive Hierarchical Fairness Intervention (AHFI), a fair GNN framework that performs adaptive constraint control at the input, representation, and output levels. AHFI monitors group disparity at each level with a geometric fairness proxy and assigns level-specific fairness pressure through learnable dual variables. To stabilize optimization, AHFI uses scale-invariant constraint violations, adaptive moving targets, and a finite-sample floor that prevents the controller from over-penalizing noise-level disparity. Experiments on six standard fair node classification benchmarks show that AHFI provides favorable fairness-utility trade-offs compared with representative fair GNN baselines across common message-passing backbones. Ablation studies show that the multi-stage design and the adaptive controller both affect the final fairness-utility trade-off. These results suggest that stage-wise adaptive control is an effective strategy for fairness-aware graph learning. Codes can be found at https://github.com/Dr-HZH/AHFI.
FULLFair Graph Anomaly Detection via Multi-Disentangled Representation Processing
Ruiqiang Li (GuangXi University) · Qingfeng Chen (GuangXi University) · Debo Cheng (Hainan University) · Chuxun Liu (Hainan University) · Jiuyong Li (Adelaide University) · Lin Liu (Adelaide University)
Abstract
Graph anomaly detection (GAD) identifies nodes deviating from normal graph patterns and is crucial in high-stakes applications such as fraud and social risk detection. However, existing GAD methods mainly prioritize accuracy while overlooking fairness. Sensitive information can be encoded in node attributes, homophilous links, and graph structures, and message passing may entangle these signals with anomaly evidence, causing group-imbalanced scores. Existing fair GAD methods are often detector-specific, limiting reuse and intensifying the fairness-utility trade-off. To address these issues, we propose Multi-Disentangled processing for Fair graph Anomaly Detection MDFairAD, built upon a Multi-Disentangled Fair Processor MDFP that serves as an upstream fair representation module jointly optimizable with off-the-shelf anomaly detectors. It performs multi-view disentanglement with causal- and representation-level debiasing to reduce attribute and structural leakage, and then nonlinearly fuses the disentangled branches to preserve cross-view anomaly evidence while suppressing sensitive information. The refined representations are further fine-tuned with anomaly detectors through a detection head. Experiments on real-world datasets show that MDFairAD achieves competitive detection performance while substantially improving fairness over existing baselines.
FULLUncovering Locally-Persistent Bias with Formal Guarantees and Debiasing
Anahita Baninajjar (Lund University) · Ahmed Rezine (Linköping University) · Amir Aminifar (Lund University)
Abstract
We propose the notion of Persistent-Bias-Aware (PBA) fairness and an approach to formally quantify locally-persistent bias. PBA fairness captures the bias in a model's predictions towards a certain outcome for a given input, compared to its counterfactual (where the sensitive attribute of the original input is flipped), in an entire region. As such, PBA fairness allows us to isolate the effect of the sensitive attribute, enabling formal identification of fairness disparities that are consistently present in the model behavior within a neighborhood. We evaluate our proposed approach under both fairness-agnostic and fairness-aware training methods and compare it to well-established fairness metrics on three benchmark datasets: Adult, COMPAS, and German Credit. The results demonstrate that our proposed approach identifies fairness disparities overlooked by other approaches and offers additional insights into model behavior. To address this challenge, we further propose a debiasing scheme by penalizing persistent bias. The results show that the models obtained under such debiasing scheme are consistently less prone to locally-persistent bias compared to the state of the art.
FULLFairRank: Fairness-Certified Premium Prioritization for Trustworthy Tiered Service Platforms
David Li (Yeshiva University) · Angela Li (Brown University)
Abstract
Tiered service platforms in mobility, delivery, and cloud computing accelerate premium requests, and aggressive prioritization can silently degrade the experience of regular users. We study premium admission as an auditable admission-control problem over streaming telemetry: given per-region arrival rates, service-time moments, and a declared tolerance δ on the mean delay inflation of regular users, how many premium requests may be prioritized? Building on a two-class M/G/1 model with probabilistic gap insertion and head-of-line promotion, we derive a closed-form fairness certificate that maps three telemetry statistics and the platform's prioritization parameters to an admissible premium-to-regular ratio, prove its monotonicity, and show that it is a conservative surrogate of the exact nonpreemptive-priority formula whenever promoted requests wait at most one mean service time. The certificate composes across heterogeneous regions through a per-region cap layer and a shared-slack pooling rule with explicitly declared per-region budgets, and it acts as a state-dependent gate for online controllers. Certificate-gated admission reduces mean regular-user delay inflation about five-fold relative to unconstrained prioritization at the evaluated operating points, and the telemetry-updated adaptive variant attains the lowest inflation of all tested policies. Because the certificate is model-conditional, we also isolate which assumptions matter: a synthetic study shows that heavy-tailed service times leave the certificate intact while bursty arrivals roughly double realized inflation, and a diagnostic on the real trace explains the remaining gap and gives operators a conservative parameterization that meets the nominal tolerance in every zone.
FULLFairStream: Adaptive Fairness Constraints for Streaming AutoML
Vikash Maheshwari (University of Tartu) · Radwa El Shawi (University of Tartu)
Abstract
Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) systems are increasingly deployed in settings where data arrives continuously and evolves over time. In such streaming environments, fairness presents a distinct challenge: data distributions change, sensitive-group proportions fluctuate, models are updated incrementally, and fairness measurements become noisy and time-varying. Existing fairness-aware AutoML approaches are designed for static data and enforce fixed fairness thresholds, while streaming AutoML systems largely neglect fairness. To address this gap, we introduce FairStream, a fairness-aware AutoML framework for data streams that treats fairness as a dynamic control signal. FairStream introduces a streaming evaluation framework that jointly models predictive performance and group-based fairness through signals capturing temporal variation, estimation uncertainty, and both performance and fairness drift. These signals drive an adaptive fairness control mechanism that maintains a time-varying feasibility envelope and accumulated fairness debt to enforce consistent fairness over time. We formulate model selection as a sequence of online constrained optimization problems and solve it using constrained Bayesian optimization, enabling principled exploration under evolving fairness constraints. Experiments on diverse streaming benchmarks show that FairStream achieves strong predictive performance while substantially reducing fairness violations compared to fairness-agnostic and fixed-threshold fairness-aware baselines.
FULLCoShapley: Context-Structure Coupled Data Valuation for Data Markets
Danyang Yue (Huazhong University of Science and Technology) · Yonghui Yang (National University of Singapore) · Le Wu (Hefei University of Technology) · Xiaofeng Ding (Huazhong University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Data valuation is a fundamental problem in emerging data markets, where the value of data is inherently shaped by both the market context and the internal structure of the dataset. However, existing approaches typically capture only one side of this interplay. Classical Shapley-based methods treat data value as an intrinsic property of a fixed dataset, leading to inconsistent valuations across participants, while recent approaches that rely on global data distributions improve consistency at the cost of overlooking structural redundancy and incurring substantial computational overhead. In this work, we argue that data valuation should be understood as a context–structure coupling problem, where value arises from the interaction between global context and local data structure. Based on this perspective, we propose CoShapley (Contextual-Structural Shapley), a hierarchical valuation framework that explicitly models this coupling, producing valuations that are both stable across varying market contexts and sensitive to redundancy and correlation within the data. To make this formulation scalable, we introduce a signed decomposition that removes pairwise coupling in Shapley estimation, together with a hybrid two-stage sampling strategy that enables batch updates of all data points from a single model evaluation. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that CoShapley achieves superior valuation effectiveness and improves downstream task performance, while significantly reducing computational cost, achieving up to 14× fewer iterations to convergence and 4× speedup in end-to-end execution.

FULLOPERA: Automated Intra-Operator Parallel Pattern Generation for Distributed Transformer Training
Wei Shang (National University of Defense Technology) · Peng Liang (National University of Defense Technology) · Mingxiang Zhu (National University of Defense Technology) · Yuan Lang (National University of Defense Technology) · Linbo Qiao (National University of Defense Technology) · Kaixi Yang (National University of Defense Technology) · Sidun Liu (National University of Defense Technology) · Dongsheng Li (National University of Defense Technology) · Shanshan Li (National University of Defense Technology) · Xiangke Liao (National University of Defense Technology)
Abstract
Designing intra-operator parallel patterns for large-scale Transformer training remains labor-intensive because it requires jointly coordinating tensor partitioning, local computation, and communication under hardware constraints. Existing automatic parallelization systems commonly select from predefined pattern libraries, limiting their ability to explore fine-grained execution alternatives. We present OPERA, a reinforcement learning framework for automatically generating executable intra-operator parallel patterns.OPERA formulates parallel pattern generation as a Markov Decision Process in which the environment tracks tensor placements, computation progress, and feasible computation and communication actions. A Transformer decoder encodes the history of layout and execution decisions, while its policy and value heads guide Monte Carlo Tree Search toward promising feasible trajectories. The resulting trajectories are reused to train the policy-value network, enabling the agent to progressively refine its decisions. A distributed program translator converts completed trajectories into executable programs and evaluates their numerical correctness, runtime, and resource consumption. Experiments on an eight-GPU NVIDIA A100 platform using BERT-Large and workloads derived from LLaMA and GPT configurations show that OPERA recovers 9 established intra-operator parallel patterns and generates additional feasible execution trajectories from primitive actions rather than selecting fixed templates.
