Rather than assuming synthetic anomalies are valid proxies for deployment-relevant faults, we ask whether benchmark anomalies cover KPI regimes occupied by controlled-real faults, and we operationalize this question as origin-aware benchmark auditing: a deployment-oriented evaluation workflow that conditions evaluation on anomaly origin. Across two public 5G/Open RAN testbed corpora, the audit exposes a failure hidden by aggregate metrics: synthetic-only training can retain strong performance on synthetic anomalies while missing controlled-real fault regimes under deployment-relevant operating conditions. We provide evidence that this failure reflects an operating-regime coverage gap rather than a model-specific limitation or feature leakage, and that modest controlled-real calibration improves controlled-real detection where additional synthetic or normal data, and synthetic reweighting do not. We release a reproducible audit toolkit and artifacts, and an operator checklist for deployment-oriented benchmark validation, together with industrial validation as a pre-production shadow-mode CI gate within Nokia's anomaly-detection pipeline.
A151SHORTPairWatch: Pair-Aware Anomaly Transformer for Detecting Adversarial Rendezvous in Public Satellite Catalogs
Young Eun Kwon (Korea University) · Ji Won Yoon (Korea University)
Abstract
Documented adversarial rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) appear in the public TLE catalog, yet existing TLE-based maneuver detectors treat each satellite in isolation—mistaking routine station-keeping for adversarial behavior and missing RPO entirely when the target stays passive. We argue that the right unit is the satellite pair and the right inductive bias is the kinematic symmetry between approach and recede. We instantiate both with PairWatch, a pair-aware AnomalyTransformer whose attention prior is augmented with a sign-symmetric geometric similarity over relative-motion features, and release an open benchmark of 359 windows from public Space-Track data spanning 11 documented RPO events, 100 Clohessy–Wiltshire synthetic adversarial windows, and a five-class hard-negative set culminating in the TerraSAR-X / TanDEM-X helix formation. Under the deployment-relevant criterion of a single threshold separating real RPO from operational negatives—a necessary property for catalog-scale screening—PairWatch is the only model that succeeds, with the property holding in 100% of bootstrap resamples versus 0–19.5% for three neural baselines and under 0.1% for four physics-informed detectors. A per-source analysis exposes a shortcut-learning failure mode of single-number AUROC: simpler baselines attain higher overall AUROC by shortcutting a synthetic-vs-formation contrast with no operational meaning; removing this single cell flips the test ranking entirely (LSTM-AD), and these baselines fail the security-relevant task the benchmark was built to measure.
A152FULLTanca: Topology-Anchored Neural Causal Architecture for Event Prediction in Critical Infrastructure Networks
Jiahui Xu (Sichuan University) · Linna Wang (City University of Hong Kong) · Siying Li (Sichuan University) · Li Lu (Sichuan University)
Abstract
In critical infrastructure networks such as microwave communication systems, accurate prediction of asynchronous event streams is crucial for proactive operations and maintenance as well as root-cause localization. Although deep temporal point process (TPP) models, exemplified by the Transformer Hawkes Process (THP), have made progress in temporal dependency modeling, their application to industrial-scale physical networks faces a fundamental topology--causality paradox: data-driven self-attention mechanisms tend to infer spurious causal associations from co-occurrence noise, whereas static physical topology priors struggle to capture latent cross-layer dependencies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Topology-Anchored Neural Causal Architecture (Tanca). Built upon standard temporal contextual attention, Tanca introduces a physical-distance prior bias and a learnable latent causal bias, thereby jointly modeling temporal dependencies, physical constraints, and data-driven causal evidence at the attention-logit level. Furthermore, it introduces a Topology-Enhanced Causal Gating (TECG) module, which uses distance-aware exponential decay gating and learnable smooth conflict gating to enable the model to respect physical boundaries while suppressing spurious local-neighbor propagation and retaining long-range latent causal paths. To evaluate the effectiveness of Tanca, we conduct extensive experiments on real-world alarm datasets and synthetic datasets. The results demonstrate that Tanca consistently outperforms multiple representative baseline models in terms of event-type prediction accuracy and test log-likelihood.
A153SHORTSyDE-Net: Shapelet Synergy Discovery and Evidence Modeling for Multivariate Time Series Classification
Lanlan Chen (Harbin Institute of Technology) · Ye Yuan (Harbin Institute of Technology) · Chunyu Wang (Harbin Institute of Technology) · Dawei Li (Competition Policy and Assessment Center of State Administration for Market Regulation) · Jian Zhang (Competition Policy and Assessment Center of State Administration for Market Regulation) · Lingling Zhao (Harbin Institute of Technology)
Abstract
Multivariate time series classification (MTSC) often depends on sparse but discriminative joint local evidence. Shapelet methods provide interpretable local evidence units and are appealing in limited-label settings. However, existing models often represent many shapelet or subsequence features as separate fine-grained evidence units and infer their class relevance through implicit interactions, which may mask sparse joint evidence among redundant or weakly relevant local features. We propose SyDE-Net, a Shapelet Synergy Discovery and Evidence Network for MTSC, which captures complementary class evidence from coordinated shapelets through explicit synergy discovery and hierarchical evidence modeling. SyDE-Net mines class-specific synergy priors with Rank-JIG and injects them into the Synergy-Class-Decision Evidence Bottleneck (SCD-EB), where shapelet features are progressively organized into compact synergy, class, and decision evidence. Specifically, global temporal context modulates the selection of class-relevant synergy evidence. Experiments on UEA and HAR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SyDE-Net, with the best average rank in the UEA main comparison and competitive performance under full-data and limited-training HAR settings.
A154FULLGadMIL: Granularity-Aware Association Discovery for Multi-Instance Time Series Classification
Lingzheng Zhang (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)) · Boyang Li (Peking University) · Lifeng Shen (Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications) · Yuxuan Liang (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)) · Fugee Tsung (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
Abstract
Time series classification (TSC) aims to identify discriminative temporal evidence that determines sequence-level labels. Multi-instance learning (MIL) models each sequence as a bag of temporal instances and enables instance-level evidence aggregation. However, existing MIL-based methods rely on a fixed instance granularity, implicitly assuming that discriminative patterns emerge at a single temporal resolution. In practice, temporal evidence is inherently multi-granularity, spanning long-term trends and short transient motifs. While multi-granularity architectures construct representations at different resolutions, they do not explicitly model how cross-granularity interactions contribute to bag-level decisions under the MIL formulation. Consequently, multi-granularity representation, structured cross-granularity interaction, and instance-level evidence aggregation remain disconnected. We propose GadMIL, the first granularity-aware multi-instance learning framework that unifies these components through structured association discovery. GadMIL constructs hierarchical instance bags across temporal granularities and introduces a structure-constrained input-adaptive masking mechanism to selectively activate informative cross-scale interactions. A positive instance clustering objective reinforces reliable hierarchical associations, and a granularity-wise expert fusion strategy adaptively integrates scale-specific predictions at the decision level. Extensive experiments on 46 UEA and UCR datasets demonstrate consistent state-of-the-art performance over strong Transformer-, multi-granularity-, and MIL-based baselines, validating the effectiveness of sparse cross-granularity association discovery for better time series classification.
A155FULLPitfalls with Downsampled Data in AutoML for Clustering
Philipp Jahn (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München) · Gabriel Marques Tavares (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München) · Anna Beer (Webster Vienna Private University) · Udo Schlegel (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München) · Thomas Seidl (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München)
Abstract
Finding the best-suited hyperparameters for applied algorithms is challenging in practice and in scientific evaluation. AutoML provides a reliable way to search for these. Still, a major issue in AutoML is scalability, as repeated evaluations are time-consuming, especially for large datasets. For classification tasks, downsampling has been shown to be effective for handling large datasets. In AutoML for unsupervised ML tasks such as clustering, recent research has also begun to integrate downsampling. However, finding suitable hyperparameters for clustering is quite underexplored and an even bigger challenge. We describe and demonstrate three key issues to address when applying downsampling to this task. Particularly, sampling may alter the instantiation of the underlying distribution, an aspect to which clustering methods are typically sensitive. Furthermore, we provide guidance for practitioners on mitigating some of these problems. Finally, we establish directions for future research to better support AutoML users for clustering.
A156SHORTCandidate-Fate Accounting for Transparent Sensor Diagnostic Pipeline Search
Haotao Xie (Beihang University) · Yutian Chen (Beihang University) · Yangqi Liu (Jinan University) · Xiaoyu Jiang (Beihang University)
Abstract
Industrial sensor diagnostics relies on preprocessing, representation, and classification pipelines, making automated pipeline search useful for reducing manual design cost. However, existing automated machine/deep learning (AutoML/AutoDL) reports typically retain only fitted trials, scores, and winners, omitting generated candidates that are invalid, pruned, skipped, cached, or unfitted. This omission limits reviewers' ability to check signal constraints, budget use, and unevaluated legal alternatives. To address this, we propose candidate-fate accounting, a candidate-level audit framework for diagnostic search traces. It records each observed candidate as auditable evidence: hashes merge repeated observations, legality checks flag invalid candidates, allocation rationales explain budget decisions, and a closed fate ledger assigns one terminal fate to each candidate. Experiments on three bearing-diagnostic datasets show that the framework detects invalid candidates and identifies 30–41 candidates omitted by fitted-trial-only reports, with closed fate records verifying complete candidate accounting while maintaining competitive diagnostic performance. The code is available at https://github.com/XXIE999/candidate-fate-accounting.
A157SHORTChi-Square Weighted k-Means for Fast and Interpretable Text Clustering
Amine Ferdjaoui (Université Paris Cité) · Séverine Affeldt (Université Paris Cité) · Mohamed Nadif (Université Paris Cité)
Abstract
Document-term matrices are sparse, imbalanced, and naturally interpreted through relative frequency profiles, yet many feature-weighted clustering methods still rely on Euclidean distance. We introduce CW-kmeans, a simple extension of k-means that combines the Chi-square distance with automatic feature weighting. The resulting objective preserves Lloyd-style updates, learns discriminative term weights, and remains efficient on high-dimensional sparse text. Across six standard text clustering benchmarks, CW-kmeans is competitive with or better than strong sparse baselines and compares favorably with sentence-embedding pipelines while retaining explicit term-level interpretability. Weight inspection further shows that the learned weights identify removable low-information terms and produce concise, specific cluster descriptors.
A158SHORTCLARE: Cluster-Number-Independent Latent Representation Learning with Graph Autoencoders for Deep Clustering
Yongdam Kim (Sogang University) · Sungwon Jung (Sogang University)
Abstract
Deep clustering uncovers latent structure in the data, but the number of clusters K is rarely known in advance. Because the true K is unknown, data analysts cluster the data under many candidate values of K and compare the results to find the most reasonable clusters. Many recent deep clustering methods improve accuracy using self-supervised methods, such as pseudo-labeling, but K is defined in the training objective. Evaluating each candidate K requires retraining the model from scratch, making a complete sweep across all K values computationally expensive. We propose CLARE (Cluster-number-independent LAtent REpresentation learning), a representation learning framework that does not use K during training. CLARE builds an adaptive kNN graph that reflects the clustering objective and keeps an edge only when it is consistent with a node's local neighborhood. A graph autoencoder then learns a single embedding from this graph, and we can group the data into any number of clusters without retraining. We further introduce a cluster-number-independent clustering loss that sharpens the cluster structure by extending the global clustering coefficient to two-hop connections. Across eight text and three image benchmarks, CLARE reaches state-of-the-art accuracy on long-text and on two of the four short-text datasets, remains competitive on medium-text, and sets a new state of the art on fine-grained image clustering.
A159FULLACMDG: An Effective and Scalable Active Clustering via Multi-granularity Diffusion Graph
Bin Zhang (Southwest Petroleum University) · Wen-Bo Xie (Southwest Petroleum University) · Zi-Han Dong (Southwest Petroleum University) · Xuan-Lin Zhu (Southwest Petroleum University) · Xin Wang (Southwest Petroleum University) · Zhen Liu (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
Active clustering injects minimal human feedback into clustering via pairwise constraints, which is highly useful in data mining pipelines but difficult to scale in practice. Existing methods are expensive in two stages: initialization often requires building costly global structures, and each interaction round may trigger heavy recomputation. Meanwhile, substantial accuracy gains still demand many constraints. We present ACMDG, an effective and scalable active clustering framework built on a multi-granularity diffusion graph. ACMDG constructs a sparse yet connected multi-granularity diffusion graph structure by progressively modeling data relationships from fine-grained nearest-neighbor links to coarse-grained representations. Within an iterative refinement framework, it selects informative nodes in batch mode, categorizes them efficiently via a neighborhood-set-based interaction strategy, and refines clustering by diffusion-based label propagation. The overall framework runs in O(n log n) time. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets show that ACMDG outperforms its counterparts in most cases in terms of clustering quality and scalability, while requiring significantly fewer constraints. Code is available at: https://github.com/BZhXuang/ACMDG_CIKM2026
A160FULLOffline Competence-Gap Mining for Motion Forecasting via Mode-Consistent Predictive Instability
Yige Wei (University of Edinburgh) · Guolong Tang (University of Edinburgh) · Yi Wang (Tsinghua University) · Haoran Tang (University of Edinburgh) · Dingsheng Luo (Peking University)
Abstract
Large motion-forecasting logs contain substantially more scenes than practitioners can inspect, motivating budgeted, model-aware data triage. We formulate competence-gap discovery as an offline retrieval problem for a frozen stochastic multimodal forecaster. A dropout-free reference pass supplies its highest-confidence mode as a per-scene reference future, and each stochastic pass is aligned to that future by nearest-mode selection. The resulting model-specific predictive-instability score combines trajectory displacement and confidence volatility for the tracked reference mode. On nuScenes and Argoverse, the method yields the strongest high-error retrieval and sparsification performance among the tested confidence and representation-distance selectors; on Argoverse, it also outperforms the tested diversity and representativeness selectors. Fine-tuning LAformer on 500 mined Argoverse samples under mixed-batch replay reduces held-out tail minADE by 3.9%, compared with 2.0% for low-confidence selection, while producing the smallest full-set minADE degradation among the tested deployable selectors. The same LAformer-mined subset reduces HiVT tail minADE by 3.4%, demonstrating that the selected samples remain useful for a second forecasting backbone. These results support the use of mode-consistent predictive instability for offline audit prioritization.
A161SHORTParameter-Space Incremental Drift Adaptation for Regression
Ryuta Matsuno (NEC Corporation)
Abstract
This paper addresses incremental drift adaptation, aiming at accurate online prediction using past data streams under incremental drift, i.e., temporal changes in mixing weights over fixed base parameters in the parameter space. Existing online updating and model-pool methods are largely drift-agnostic, while the few structure-aware approaches focus on data-space mixing rather than parameter-space incremental drift. In this paper, we propose IDA, an Incremental Drift Adaptation method, which explicitly exploits parameter-space structure. We first show that minimizing squared errors under incremental drift requires modeling both the conditional and marginal distributions. Based on this, IDA models these distributions with Gaussian, learns the base parameters offline, and adapts online by estimating mixing weights over time. Experiments on six real-world drifting datasets show that IDA achieves the best average rank against strong baselines, demonstrating the benefit of structure-aware drift adaptation for regression.
A162SHORTOut-of-Distribution Detection with Anisotropic Cosine Similarity
Minjae Sung (Seoul National University) · Jonghun Park (Seoul National University)
Abstract
While cosine similarity is widely used in out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, its assumption of isotropy often leads to suboptimal detection boundaries in anisotropic embedding spaces. To account for this limitation, Mahalanobis++ attempted to extend feature dispersion modeling to the normalized feature space. However, it applied Mahalanobis distance under a Euclidean interpretation, even though the features reside on a hyperspherical manifold. This mismatch can introduce geometric distortion. To better respect the underlying geometry of normalized features, we propose anisotropic cosine similarity (ANCO) that rescales angular deviations based on direction-dependent in-distribution dispersion. By leveraging the Fr\'echet mean and tangent-space covariance, ANCO aims to incorporate anisotropic dispersion into cosine similarity while preserving the manifold geometry. Extensive evaluations on ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-100 indicate that both ANCO and its adaptations to NNGuide achieved state-of-the-art results. These findings suggest that ANCO provides a principled way to incorporate directional sensitivity into cosine similarity across a wide range of applications, including OOD detection.
A163FULLEvidence-Consistent Generative Detection under Scenario-Level Distribution Shift
San Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Jinyeong Bak (Sungkyunkwan University)
Abstract
Conventional in-distribution evaluation can overestimate robustness when training and test data share recurring task-specific patterns or surface cues. This risk is especially relevant in social-engineering fraud detection, where attackers can preserve malicious intent while changing the scenario, impersonated entity, or wording. We study this problem as scenario-level out-of-distribution (SL-OOD) detection for SMS and voice phishing, where entire attack scenarios are held out from training while the label space remains fixed. This setting tests whether models can generalize to unseen attack scenarios using decision-relevant evidence rather than familiar scenario-specific cues. Using this SL-OOD evaluation, we find that high in-distribution performance does not reliably predict held-out robustness across feature-, encoder-, and decoder-based baselines. We interpret this gap as scenario memorization: reliance on recurring scenario-specific lexical or entity cues rather than decision-relevant evidence. We propose ECoG, an evidence-consistent generative framework that combines evidence-span supervision with a rationale-label consistency objective during training. On the 0.5B decoder, relative to the same backbone trained without consistency regularization, ECoG raises Macro-F1 on OOD challenging instances by 3.22 points, reduces the share of predictions whose generated rationale supports the opposite label by 4.22 points, and increases token-level overlap with reference evidence spans by 8.38 points; the reduction in prediction-rationale inconsistency is consistent across four decoder backbones. These results suggest that compact generative detectors can benefit from evidence supervision and rationale-label consistency under social-engineering shift.
A164FULLUGDACal: Nodewise Calibrator for Unsupervised Graph Domain Adaptation
Jiaren Xiao (Fujian Medical University) · Liang Zhang (Sun Yat-sen University) · Quanyu Dai (Huawei Technologies Ltd.)
Abstract
Unsupervised graph domain adaptation (UGDA) aims to enable node classification on an unlabeled target graph by transferring knowledge from a labeled source graph. Calibrating classifiers is essential to produce reliable probability estimates that support trustworthy decision-making. However, the prior art on UGDA primarily focuses on improving classification accuracy, largely ignoring the calibration of probability estimates. This paper proposes a novel nodewise calibrator (i.e., UGDACal) specifically designed for UGDA models. UGDACal computes the nodewise calibration parameter using an attention-based network that incorporates the structural information around a node. In addition, UGDACal is designed to generate an ensemble comprising nodewise-temperature-calibrated, uncalibrated, and uniform predictions to enhance calibration performance. A pseudo-labeled set is constructed from the unlabeled target graph and employed to train UGDACal, mitigating the impact of domain divergence. Extensive experiments on benchmark UGDA tasks demonstrate that UGDACal outperforms state-of-the-art calibration methods in calibrating UGDA models. The code is available at https://github.com/JiarenX/UGDACal.
A165FULLKnowledge-Informed Local Causal Discovery of Optimal Adjustment Sets
Seong Woo Ahn (Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CentraleSupélec, LISN UMR 9015) · Alessandro Leite (INSA Rouen Normandy, University of Rouen Normandy, LITIS UR 4108) · José Lucas De Melo Costa (Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CentraleSupélec, LISN UMR 9015) · Fabrice Popineau (Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CentraleSupélec, LISN UMR 9015) · Bich-Liên Doan (Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CentraleSupélec, LISN UMR 9015) · Arpad Rimmel (Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CentraleSupélec, LISN UMR 9015)
Abstract
Local causal discovery is a scalable alternative to global structure learning. However, it can struggle to identify valid adjustment sets in data-scarce settings because of finite-sample uncertainty, incomplete local neighborhoods, and unresolved Markov equivalence. Although many application domains provide structured background knowledge, its integration into local causal discovery remains limited. We propose b-LOAD, a knowledge-informed extension of the LOAD algorithm for local discovery of optimal adjustment sets. b-LOAD incorporates prior edge constraints directly into the local structure-learning procedure and uses Meek's rules to expand the discovery frontier dynamically, yielding a knowledge-constrained MPDAG over the relevant local subgraph. This strategy helps prevent structurally relevant nodes introduced by prior knowledge from being excluded by local search. We prove that, under sound background knowledge, the procedure monotonically refines the admissible equivalence class and can enlarge the set of identifiable causal queries, enabling recovery of optimal adjustment sets that are not identifiable from observational conditional-independence information alone. Empirically, b-LOAD improves downstream causal effect estimation relative to purely data-driven and standard knowledge-augmented baselines, particularly in data-scarce and structurally complex regimes. Results on real-world biological networks show that locally targeted prior knowledge provides the largest gains and remains beneficial under moderate structural noise. These findings position b-LOAD as a scalable approach for converting fragmented domain knowledge into more reliable causal-effect estimation.
A166SHORTWhen Can Pre-Trained Policies Be Reused? Inference-Time Policy Composition from Fixed Policy Libraries
Ihor Vitenko (National Technical University of Ukraine “Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute”) · Noha Ibrahim (Grenoble INP) · Sihem Amer-Yahia (CNRS, Univ. Grenoble Alpes)
Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) policies are typically trained for fixed objectives, making adaptation to new tasks expensive and often requiring retraining from scratch. We study inference-time policy reuse: given a fixed library of pre-trained policies and a new objective, can a high-quality policy be constructed entirely offline without additional environment interaction? We introduce MOSAIC, a framework for retrieving and composing policies from reusable policy libraries. Beyond the framework itself, we investigate a more fundamental question: under what conditions can policy reuse succeed? Experiments on GridWorld environments reveal two distinct regimes. When objectives can be solved by reusing previously observed behaviors, inference-time composition achieves performance close to training from scratch while substantially reducing computation cost. In contrast, performance degrades when solving new objectives requires long-horizon planning across behaviors that are not jointly represented in the library. Additional experiments show that reuse remains robust under moderate reductions in library coverage and that policy retrieval and ranking become increasingly important when exploration is limited. Overall, our findings provide insight into when reusable policy libraries can serve as a practical alternative to retraining.
A167SHORTPredict to Generate: Enhancing Diffusion World Models with JEPA-based Latent Dynamics for Traffic Management
Jiahang Li (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China) · Jia Wu (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
This paper addresses the cooperative control of connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) and traffic signals by introducing a Predict-to-Generate traffic management framework. The proposed method employs a diffusion-based world model to generate desired future traffic states, and a Scenario-Agnostic Head (SAH) to decode state-transition representations into signal phases and CAV speed recommendations. To overcome the limited ability of conventional diffusion models to explicitly learn action-conditioned traffic evolution, we augment the framework with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) auxiliary task, which predicts future traffic representations in latent space under action conditioning, while SIGReg regularization prevents representation collapse. Extensive simulations on SUMO demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the lowest average delay in four scenarios and maintains competitive throughput across all tested settings. Ablation studies confirm the essential contributions of JEPA-based latent dynamics modeling and the SAH decoding mechanism to performance improvement.
A168SHORTBeneath the Noise: Uncovering and Distilling the Encoding Bottleneck of Quantum Models
Seungkwon Lee (Korea University) · Chaeyeon Kim (Korea University) · Seok Bin Son (Korea University) · Joongheon Kim (Korea University) · Hoh Peter In (Korea University)
Abstract
Quantum machine learning (QML) has attracted growing interest for its potential to match large classical models with far fewer parameters. This derives from encoding classical data representations into a Hilbert space exponentially larger than the number of qubits. In practice, however, noise mitigation limits these models to few qubits and shallow parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs), shrinking the accessible Hilbert space. This avoids noise but exposes a deeper problem of information loss that varies across samples: encoding compression. We uncover this bottleneck with the Hilbert-space encoding margin (HEM), partitioning inputs into a collapsed-encoding (CE) region and a preserved-encoding (PE) region, and find baseline accuracy on CE lagging PE by 43–58 pp across six setups. We propose quantum region-aware distillation (Q-RAD), a dual-PQC architecture that distills knowledge from a classical teacher separately on CE and PE samples. Under oracle routing, Q-RAD improves overall accuracy by up to +8.9/+8.1 pp over single-PQC and parameter-matched depth-doubled baselines. These results show that the encoding bottleneck can be exploited via its sample-level structure and architectural separation. Our code is available at https://github.com/skwonbb/Q-RAD/.
A169FULLAnytime-Budget Embedding Allocation for DLRMs via Continuous-Capacity Multiple-Choice Knapsack
Cheng Guo (Arizona State University) · Rui Xue (Independent Researcher) · Jeff Zhang (Arizona State University)
Abstract
Embedding tables dominate the memory footprint of deep learning recommendation models (DLRMs), yet existing compression methods usually assume that the deployment memory budget is fixed before training. This is inconvenient in production, where the same recommender may be served across hardware tiers, multi-tenant resource conditions, or changing A/B-test operating points. We study anytime-budget embedding allocation: train one DLRM once, then export a hard budget-feasible embedding layout for any memory target in a specified range. We propose Continuous-Capacity Entropy-Smoothed MCKP (CC-MCKP), a differentiable allocation layer that integrates the real-valued budget directly into the multiple-choice knapsack partition function through a smooth feasibility gate. Differentiating this continuous-capacity partition function yields per-table action marginals for training and an analytic budget shadow price for sensitivity analysis, while final deployment still uses a hard MCKP solve with conservative discretization to guarantee feasibility. We provide smoothness, marginal, shadow-price, hard-limit, finite-gate, and grid-consistency results for the layer. Across Criteo Kaggle and Criteo Terabyte, one CC-MCKP-trained model approaches independently trained per-budget specialists (within about 10-3 AUC on average) and provides the strongest average single-run accuracy, with its clearest gains at intermediate and unseen budgets and small reversals at the minimum-budget corner, where the feasible layout is unique. Hard export preserves zero budget violations, while one training run costs about 2× a plain model instead of the 13× of a per-budget specialist suite.
A170SHORTConRAC-SE: Evidence-Agreement Routing for Cost-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Security Classification
Yeseul Chang (Chung-Ang University) · Woosang Lim (Independent Researcher) · Rahul Kailasa (San Jose State University) · Simon Shim (San Jose State University) · Jaewoo Lee (Chung-Ang University)
Abstract
Enterprise document security-level classification must balance rare high-risk recall, precision, and inference cost. Static ML pipelines lose recall as sensitivity patterns drift, whereas retrieval-augmented classification (RAC) grounds predictions in auditable precedents but still struggles on boundary cases, and verifying every document with an LLM is expensive and can inject variance when the evidence already agrees. We introduce ConRAC-SE, a deterministic evidence-agreement routing controller for cost-aware RAC: it commits top-1/top-2 evidence-consensus cases without an LLM, verifies only non-consensus cases with a small LLM against a top-3 evidence vote, and escalates only verifier–evidence disagreements to a high-capacity LLM. On the WikiLeaks and DISC security corpora, RAG-style RAC always-LLM decoding helps when the retrieval backbone is weak but regresses when it is strong; under a limited call budget on the strong backbone, ConRAC-SE instead improves quality consistently while lowering average latency and LLM cost. LLMs are thus most useful here as residual adjudicators rather than always-LLM decoders, and the routing additionally surfaces the ambiguous tail for review.
A171APPLIEDThreatLens: Evidence-Guided Ranking of High-Priority CVEs
Soroush Motamedi Sedeh (Simon Fraser University) · Panteha Shahrivar (Simon Fraser University) · Malaika Qureshi (Simon Fraser University) · Ali Devjiani (Simon Fraser University) · Mohammad A. Tayebi (Simon Fraser University)
Abstract
Security teams must prioritize vulnerabilities before exploitation evidence is complete. Existing signals, such as CVSS, EPSS, advisories, and public exploits, are useful but fragmented and time-sensitive; retrospective rankings can therefore overstate performance by using evidence unavailable at decision time. We present ThreatLens, a simple yet effective and deployment-realistic framework for CVE prioritization. ThreatLens ranks vulnerabilities at each review point using only cutoff-valid evidence and learns from future CISA KEV entries as weak supervision for exploitation relevance. Under forward-in-time, CVE-disjoint evaluation, ThreatLens significantly outperforms CVSS, EPSS, and rule-based evidence-fusion baselines. On the held-out test split, ThreatLens surfaces 80.0% of future KEV CVEs in the top 20, over three times EPSS at the same budget, and reaches 95.9% in the top 50. Early-warning analysis further shows that ThreatLens identifies a substantial fraction of subsequent KEV entries before formal catalog inclusion, supporting timely, evidence-grounded triage.
A172FULLA Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Formulaic Alpha Factor Generation and Adaptive Composition
Yu Liu (East China Normal University) · Cen Chen (East China Normal University) · Yanhao Wang (East China Normal University) · Hua Wei (Didichuxing Co. Ltd) · Junjun Zhang (Didichuxing Co. Ltd)
Abstract
Alpha factor mining aims to automatically construct predictive signals from raw market features and is fundamental to stock return forecasting. Recent reinforcement learning (RL) approaches formulate formulaic alpha discovery as a sequential decision problem yet face three key challenges. First, factor generation suffers from delayed and sparse rewards: informative feedback is typically available only after a complete expression is generated, making credit assignment for intermediate decisions difficult and limiting exploration efficiency. Second, overly rapid policy convergence limits the diversity and novelty of discovered expressions, further exacerbating factor crowding. Third, static factor composition fails to adapt to non-stationary market conditions. To address these challenges, we propose AlphaHRL, a new hierarchical RL framework for joint factor generation and adaptive composition. At the low level, we introduce process-level reward shaping to provide dense supervision during expression generation, including validity and stability signals. Then, we perform a tree-structured decomposition and a memory-based comparison to reshape terminal rewards using novelty, redundancy, and marginal utility signals relative to a maintained factor pool. At the high level, we learn a dynamic allocation policy that reweighs factors based on recent information coefficient (IC) trajectories, enabling regime-aware composition of a mega-alpha. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AlphaHRL consistently improves both factor quality and portfolio performance relative to state-of-the-art baselines. Our code is published anonymously at https://github.com/ECNU-CILAB/AlphaHRL.
A173SHORTDecision-Focused Learning with Differentiable Micro-Demand Aggregation for Electricity Retail Procurement
Masaki Takahashi (NTT DOCOMO, INC.) · Wataru Yamada (NTT DOCOMO, INC.)
Abstract
Retail procurement decisions are made by forecasting future demand and then optimizing procurement plans under time-varying unit procurement costs and operational constraints. In this predict-then-optimize pipeline, even the same magnitude of prediction error can induce different downstream procurement costs because prices vary over time, and operational constraints can make forecasted demand infeasible when used directly as a procurement plan. As a result, minimizing standard prediction losses, even with weighting schemes, does not necessarily minimize downstream procurement cost. This motivates Decision-Focused Learning (DFL), which trains predictors with respect to downstream decision objectives. Applying DFL to large numbers of consumers requires demand aggregation to smooth noisy individual demand, stabilize forecasts, and prevent downstream optimization from yielding noise-driven decisions while preserving heterogeneity relevant to procurement decisions. We propose a DFL framework with differentiable micro-demand aggregation that jointly trains consumer clustering, aggregate demand forecasting, and downstream procurement optimization in an end-to-end pipeline. In numerical experiments on demand forecasting and electricity retail procurement optimization, the proposed method reduced procurement regret, defined as the cost gap between prediction-based decisions and the full-information optimum, by 25.6% versus a k-means-based prediction-focused baseline and by 3.3% versus its DFL counterpart. Furthermore, this approach exhibits robustness to the number of clusters.
A174SHORTDoes AlphaFold Rediscover the Hydrophobic–Polar Model?
Ioan Sima (Babes-Bolyai University) · Daniela-Maria Cristea (University '1 Decembrie 1918') · Emilia-Loredana Pop (Babes-Bolyai University)
Abstract
AlphaFold predicts protein structure from sequence with remarkable accuracy, yet which physical principles are reflected in its predicted structures and internal representations remains opaque. We ask whether AlphaFold rediscovers the hydrophobic–polar (HP) model (the classical abstraction in which folding is driven by maximizing contacts between hydrophobic residues) using the HP model as an interpretability lens rather than a prediction target. Mining predicted structures from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database for the E. coli proteome, we reduce each sequence to a binary HP string under a standard hydrophobicity scale and test the central HP hypothesis with a label-permutation null model. AlphaFold structures robustly over-represent hydrophobic contacts (median ≈ 1.8× enrichment, >97% of proteins), an effect stable across hydrophobicity assignments and contact definitions; yet on short chains they fall short of the extremal compaction an HP optimum would demand, indicating a directional preference rather than an optimized objective. As a complementary probe, we show that AlphaFold's internal representation linearly encodes residue burial—the structural signature of the hydrophobic effect—well beyond amino-acid identity, and more sharply than a sequence-only language model. Together these analyses bridge a learned predictor and a classical combinatorial model, providing an interpretable account of how hydrophobic structural information is reflected in AlphaFold’s predictions and representations.
A175FULLKnowledge World Model: Latent Rollouts for Learning Path Recommendation
Jongwoo Kim (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) · Seongyeub Chu (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) · Jeongwhan Choi (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) · Jiwon Jeong (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) · Mun Yong Yi (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology)
Abstract
We replace the recursive observation-feedback rollout used in offline Learning Path Recommendation (LPR) with a latent transition predictor, thereby reducing pseudo-response error accumulation and per-step rollout computation. RL-based LPR commonly trains policies inside learner-model simulators. Existing rollouts ask the simulator to score the recommended problem, threshold the score into a pseudo-response, append that response to the history, and re-encode the history before the next decision. We refer to this detour as the Interaction Bottleneck, which induces pseudo-response error accumulation and repeated history re-encoding. The proposed Knowledge World Model (KWM) uses a latent transition predictor to map the current latent state and recommended problem to the next latent state. The same mastery readout then computes mastery estimates and rewards. Across five datasets and four RL-based LPR agents, KWM improves target mastery gain with an average relative gain of 14.47%. In efficiency measurements, KWM increases training episode throughput by 35.53% on average and achieves an average per-step latency speedup of 1.93x on ASSIST09. KWM also improves scores for sparse histories and target concepts absent from observed histories, while reducing long-horizon state drift. These results indicate that offline LPR can plan more reliably by rolling out latent states instead of recursively generating response histories.
A176FULLEVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation
Geonwoo Bang (Sungkyunkwan University) · Dongho Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Moohong Min (Sungkyunkwan University)
Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) for learning path recommendation (LPR) faces two coupled obstacles. First, the policy must commit to a sequence of L concepts without intermediate feedback, producing a combinatorial search space that grows super-exponentially with L and provides reward only at the final step. Second, expert learning paths would be the natural cure for sparse-reward RL, but they do not exist in educational data, because student logs record what learners did, not what they should have done. We address both obstacles by importing a recipe from simulator-based demonstration learning in robotics: the knowledge tracing simulator is used both to synthesize per-learner expert demonstrations through evolutionary search and to train a deployment-free policy that distills these demonstrations into a feed-forward learner. Our framework EVOL instantiates this pipeline with an asymmetric actor-critic where the actor commits to deployment-realistic blind planning while the critic exploits the privileged simulator state during training. Across three datasets (ASSIST15, Junyi, EdNet; 39–189 concepts) and path lengths L∈5,10,20, EVOL surpasses 8 baselines spanning heuristic, sequential, RL, graph-enhanced RL, and LLM-enhanced methods. We further compare three imitation strategies (BC, AWR, DAPG) and show that final performance is governed by the quality of evolutionary experts rather than by the particular imitation objective.
A177FULLFreKT: Model-Agnostic Frequency-Domain Enhancement and Fusion for Knowledge Tracing
Hao Wu (Beijing Normal University) · Jiong Wang (Beijing Normal University) · Xingwei Zeng (Guangzhou College of Applied Science and Technology) · Tengju Li (Beijing Normal University) · Shengquan Yu (Beijing Normal University)
Abstract
Knowledge tracing (KT) aims to estimate learners' latent knowledge states from historical interactions and predict their future performance. However, by treating learning histories mainly as temporal dependencies over discrete interactions, existing KT methods lack an explicit mechanism to distinguish stable knowledge progression from stage-wise learning rhythms and short-term response perturbations. Frequency-domain modeling offers a promising complementary view for KT, but existing attempts to introduce frequency modeling into KT remain insufficiently adapted to KT. They often rely on post-hoc spectral analysis over temporally compressed representations, lack semantic alignment between frequency patterns and knowledge-state transitions, and are tightly coupled with specific KT architectures, limiting their generality. To address these limitations, we propose FreKT, a model-agnostic frequency-domain KT framework. FreKT introduces a strictly causal parallel frequency branch to directly capture local spectral fluctuations from learning interactions. It further performs exercise-aware band reconstruction and aggregation to identify prediction-relevant frequency components and aligns the selected spectral patterns with temporal knowledge states through a task-aligned fusion module. With its model-agnostic design, FreKT can be flexibly integrated into different temporal KT backbones without changing their original prediction paradigms. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets show that FreKT consistently improves the performance of various temporal KT models. Further analyses also verify the effectiveness of frequency-domain modeling in capturing learning behavior variations.
A178FULLBeyond Structured Vitals: Semantic-Temporal Alignment for Full-Record ICU Risk Forecasting
Zhichong Zheng (Tongji University) · Xiaohang Nie (Shanghai Innovation Institute) · Xueqi Wang (Shanghai East Hospital, School of Medicine, Tongji University) · Yuanjin Zhao (Tongji University) · Haitao Zhang (Shanghai East Hospital, School of Medicine, Tongji University) · Yichao Tang (Tongji University)
Abstract
Traditional Electronic Health Record (EHR) datasets heavily favor structured data, often missing the nuanced progression of patients in intensive care. To address this gap, we introduce FRICU, a newly constructed dataset integrating structured vitals with full-record clinical narratives across complete admission trajectories using expert-verified, event-level annotations. Recognizing that the pathological impact of historical events depends on their semantic content rather than mere chronological proximity, we propose Semantic-Temporal Alignment (SeTA), a semantic-guided temporal attention mechanism that dynamically calibrates temporal receptive fields for query-specific evidence retrieval. For supervision, expert-verified risk labels are transformed into continuous trajectories via bidirectional Gaussian decay, providing smooth event-level supervision for gradual risk evolution. On FRICU, SeTA achieves a Sample AUPRC of 0.428, improving over TALE-EHR by 21.2%. On MIMIC-IV, SeTA achieves the best AUPRC on IMV and mortality prediction and remains competitive on sepsis prediction, demonstrating generalization beyond text-intensive full-record trajectories. To facilitate reproducibility, our code is available at https://github.com/violetesk/SeTA-FRICU.
A179SHORTCG-Probes: Recovering Guardrail Directions from Patient Query Embeddings
Marko Řeháček (Masaryk University) · Vítězslav Dušek (University Hospital Brno) · Martin Rusinko (Masaryk Memorial Cancer Institute) · Vít Nováček (Masaryk University)
Abstract
Patient-facing AI assistants promise valuable support to patients, but incoming queries can pose medical risks. To create guardrails, we work with oncologists to define three ordinal risk axes: Medical Urgency, Psychological Urgency, and Topic Sensitivity. We propose Clinical Guardrail Probes (CG-Probes) to measure the risks from query embeddings. We probe for each axis in the normalized embedding space of frozen embedders via the difference-in-means method, treating each axis as a potential linear direction. To train the probes, we cluster 79,658 Czech oncology search queries with BERTopic and use these clusters to generate pairs of queries with contrastive risk levels via few-shot prompting. We evaluate the approach on 200 queries (90 real, 110 synthetic), each graded by two oncologists, against two open-weight LLMs and a frontier LLM. We find that urgency-based axes are recoverable as linear directions, and the probes are competitive with open-weight LLMs (no significant differences in quadratic-weighted ?) at a fraction of the latency. Each axis yields a scalar score that clinicians can inspect and use to set escalation thresholds. The pipeline requires only search logs, axis definitions, and black-box access to the embedding model, suggesting transferability across healthcare domains. Robust validation on new queries and axes remains future work.
A180APPLIEDRouting Patient Messages in Primary Care Using Explainable Ontology-Guided Large Language Models
Malak Younis (University of Haifa) · Meira Levy (Shenkar College of Engineering, Design and Art) · Dikla Agur-Cohen (Technion - Israel Institute of Technology) · Efrat Moshe (Shenkar College of Engineering, Design and Art) · Adir Solomon (University of Haifa)
Abstract
Accurately routing patient-generated messages is a major challenge in primary care, where clinicians must manage large volumes of unstructured text. In this work, we propose a novel method for message routing in family medicine that integrates large language models (LLMs) with a domain-specific clinical ontology. Developed in close collaboration with pharmacists and physicians, the ontology encodes textual indicators relevant to message routing decisions. We incorporate this ontology by leveraging two LLMs, aiming to improve routing accuracy while generating natural language explanations that clarify the rationale behind each decision, thus enhancing primary care experts' trust in the system. We evaluate our method using a large-scale dataset from a healthcare provider, comprising a substantial volume of patient messages. This setting introduces an additional challenge, as the messages are written in Hebrew, a morphologically rich language. Despite this complexity, our results show high classification accuracy alongside high-quality, interpretable explanations. We further evaluated the proposed method in a real-world online setting, demonstrating its practical value for supporting message triage in clinical practice.
A181SHORTOntology Concept Overlap as a Training Signal: Knowledge-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Clinical Question Answering
Aditya Tanna (Dhirubhai Ambani University) · Abhishek Jindal (Dhirubhai Ambani University)
Abstract
Reinforcement learning post-training for language models relies on two reward designs: human preferences (RLHF, DPO) and binary verifiers (RLVR). Clinical question answering fits neither. Near-correct answers differ by a single substituted entity, and no executable check decides clinical correctness. We instantiate a soft verifier from a maintained controlled vocabulary: UMLS Concept Unique Identifier overlap (via scispaCy, set-level F1) gives a graded, externally specified reward computed without a model in the loop. We combine it inside GRPO with an entropy-normalised LLM judge, which covers the safety and evidence axes overlap cannot see, and a small consistency penalty on padding and repetition that keeps early-training samples scorable. This three-term composite improves over SFT on Phi-3-mini (3.8B) over MedQA by 2.9% on EM (0.700 vs 0.680) and 39% on Token-F1 (0.202 vs 0.145); on Llama-3.2-3B the corresponding gains are 14% on EM and 35% on Token-F1. We report Token-F1 as the primary metric because it credits partially-correct clinical content that EM discards at this open-generation scale. Main-table results are means over 3 seeds with standard deviations below 0.005. The method transfers to PubMedQA, where training on the PubMedQA train set with the same composite reward improves Token-F1 over SFT by 22% on Phi-3-mini and 17% on Llama-3.2-3B without retuning. A reward ablation on Phi-3, varying the judge-ontology split at a fixed consistency weight, attributes 3 EM points to the ontology term, the contribution that catches entity substitutions the judge cannot. Three negative findings constrain the design: DPO under random negatives underperforms SFT for strong-prior models but helps the weakest-prior one; PPO under a sparse neural reward diverges; GRPO with KL-in-loss collapses at 7B. The recipe is designed to transfer to any domain with a maintained controlled vocabulary, a generalisation we leave to future work.
A182SHORTReliability-Guided Video Token Learning for Contactless Vital Sign Estimation
Shadman Sakib (University of Maryland, Baltimore County) · Haley Patel (University of Maryland, Baltimore County) · Nirmalya Roy (University of Maryland, Baltimore County)
Abstract
Contactless vital-sign estimation from video remains difficult because physiological cues are weak, spatially localized, and easily corrupted by illumination changes, motion artifacts, pose variation, and sensor noise. Existing methods typically learn deterministic mappings from video to physiological waveforms or rates, but they rarely model which visual evidence is reliable or when a prediction should be trusted. We propose a reliability-guided video token learning framework for uncertainty-aware physiological signal estimation. The framework learns to mine informative spatiotemporal tokens, suppress unreliable visual evidence, and infer structured physiological dynamics through masked video-token modeling, signal-guided alignment, and supervised vital-sign estimation. In addition to predicting physiological waveforms and rates, the model outputs an uncertainty score that reflects visual ambiguity and prediction reliability. We evaluate the framework across heterogeneous contactless sensing settings, including respiratory and rPPG benchmarks. In addition to standard accuracy metrics, we assess reliability using uncertainty separation, high-error detection, and risk--coverage analysis. Results show that explicit visual-evidence reliability modeling improves robustness across datasets and provides a practical confidence measure for contactless physiological monitoring.
A183SHORTCAPA: Context-Aware Prototype Adaptation for Weakly Supervised Histopathology Segmentation
Hyoju Ahn (Sungkyunkwan University) · Heejin Kim (Sungkyunkwan University) · Eunil Park (Sungkyunkwan University)
Abstract
Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) reduces the need for costly pixel-level annotations in histopathological image analysis. However, CAM-based WSSS often suffers from ambiguous tissue boundaries, inter-class visual similarity, intra-class morphological variation, and a missing spatial context in patch-level processing. We propose CAPA, a Context-Aware Prototype Adaptation framework that improves CAM generation through two components: Neighbor Context Attention, which incorporates information from spatially adjacent patches, and Reliability-Aware Contrastive Loss, which adapts subclass prototypes while suppressing unreliable CAM-derived samples. By jointly modeling spatial tissue continuity and sample reliability, CAPA provides more discriminative and stable supervision for CAM generation. Experiments on BCSS-WSSS and LUAD-HistoSeg show that CAPA improves the mIoU by 6.4 and 4.2 pp over the previous best method, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining neighborhood context modeling with reliability-aware prototype adaptation for weakly supervised histopathological segmentation.
Poster & Demo Session 1 · DemosMonday, 9 Nov · 14:00 – 15:3015 demos
Demo Area · 15 demos
B01DEMOReal-Time Adaptive Tour Recommendation with Agentic AI
Kwan Hui Lim (Singapore University of Social Sciences) · Aldy Gunawan (Singapore Management University) · Carmen Kar Hang Lee (Singapore University of Social Sciences)
Abstract
Tour-recommendation systems, including the recent wave of LLM-based travel planners, typically stop at plan generation: given a user request, they produce a single itinerary and stop. Once the trip starts, however, tourists are left to handle disruptions such as rain, growing queues, transit breakdowns, or user fatigue. We present AdaptTour, an agentic system that continues replanning after departure; its contribution is the overall control architecture. Mid-trip signals (weather, queue length, transit disruption, user fatigue, and free-text feedback) are fused into a single context snapshot, typed triggers pass through a debounced registry, and a replanner locks the executed prefix and re-optimises the tail, re-enforcing every constraint at each pass: money budget, accessibility, per-member vetoes and boosts, and carbon preference. The LLM is used only to score candidates, with a deterministic fallback for omitted candidates, and to generate the rationale presented to the traveller; selection, sequencing, routing, and constraint checking remain deterministic. Weather is live, while crowd, transit, and fatigue are simulated for the demonstration and explicitly labelled as such in the interface. The system provides a curated five-city catalogue of POIs (Singapore, Melbourne, London, New York, Paris), per-city fare tables, five travel modes, and OSRM-routed map polylines cached on disk for offline-capable visualisation. Source code, tests, and JSONL scenario traces are publicly available to support reproduction.
B02DEMOXAnnoRank: A Comprehensive Web-Based Framework for Evaluating Explainability in Rankings
Elyanne Oey (University of Amsterdam) · Lisanne Wallaard (University of Amsterdam) · Daniele Borghesi (University of Pisa) · Salvatore Ruggieri (University of Pisa) · Clara Rus (University of Amsterdam)
Abstract
XAnnoRank is a web-based framework designed to support explainability studies in rankings via user-centered evaluation. XAnnoRank provides an easily adaptable user interface (UI) that enables systematic assessment of explainability methods by presenting ranked lists with and without explanations, while collecting both implicit and explicit user feedback. Its flexibility facilitates diverse user design, including different explanation types, datasets, ranking models, and researcher-defined configurations. The tool has been successfully demonstrated and validated in a high-stakes domain through a study on explainability in recruitment conducted as part of the EU-funded FINDHR (https://findhr.eu/) project. (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101070212) By streamlining the UI setup, XAnnoRank reduces implementation efforts and enables reproducibility across studies. The code and documentation (https://github.com/ClaraRus/AnnoRank/tree/XAnnoRank) are publicly available, together with a demonstration video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHJLbgGNaxs).
B03DEMOTabClaw: An Interactive and Self-Evolving Agent for Spreadsheet Manipulation and Table Reasoning
Mingyue Cheng (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Shuo Yu (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Daoyu Wang (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Qingchuan Li (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Xiaoyu Tao (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Qingyang Mao (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Yitong Zhou (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China) · Qi Liu (State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China)
Abstract
Spreadsheets and tables are used representations for structured data analysis, but effective analysis still requires substantial manual effort and domain expertise. Recent large language model (LLM) agents can automate parts of this process, but they provide limited transparency into intermediate decisions, rely on implicit assumptions, struggle with multi-table comparison, and repeat workflows without adapting to a user's preferences. This paper presents TabClaw, an open-source interactive AI agent for spreadsheet manipulation and table reasoning. Users upload CSV or Excel files and issue natural-language requests; TabClaw clarifies ambiguous intent, exposes an editable execution plan, streams a ReAct-style tool-using analysis loop, dispatches specialist agents for parallel multi-table reasoning, and synthesizes findings with explicit consensus and uncertainty markers. Beyond one-off analysis, TabClaw records completed workflows, extracts persistent user memory, distills reusable skills from repeated tool-use patterns, supports package-style skill import, and versions external skills after repeated failures. Experiments on spreadsheet manipulation and table reasoning benchmarks show that TabClaw improves executable task completion and reasoning performance while preserving an inspectable user workflow. This paper shows how TabClaw turns spreadsheets and tables into inspectable analytical workflows while personalizing itself to recurring data-analysis tasks across diverse real-world data-analysis settings. Our code is available. (https://github.com/ustc-table-mining/TabClaw)
B04DEMOMADClean: Statistical Profiling and Multi-Agent Large Language Model Reasoning for Automatic Data Cleaning
William Mgbemena (Utrecht University) · Mossad Helali (Concordia University) · Melisachew Wudage Chekol (Utrecht University) · Mourad Ouzzani (QCRI, HBKU) · Abdulhakim Qahtan (Utrecht University)
Abstract
High-quality data is essential for effective decision-making, data analytics, and training machine learning models. Numerous data cleaning tools and systems have been proposed in both academia and industry. Several recent tools utilize Large Language Models (LLMs), but most rely entirely on their unverified reasoning capabilities, struggling to effectively handle dirty datasets with heterogeneous error types. In this demo, we describe MADClean, a tabular data cleaning system that uses statistical profiling and a multi-agent architecture to achieve strong performance in several data cleaning tasks. MADClean uses dedicated LLM agents to recommend cleaning operations, generate executable source code, and iteratively verify and improve its outputs. We show that MADClean reliably handles dirty data across three real-world data cleaning scenarios, and scales to datasets with hundreds of thousands of rows in our evaluation.
B05DEMOSMBench: No-code Benchmarking of Deep Entity Resolution
Oleh Astappiev (L3S Research Center at Leibniz University Hannover) · Franziska Neuhof (L3S Research Center at Leibniz University Hannover) · Marco Fisichella (L3S Research Center at Leibniz University Hannover) · George Papadakis (National and Kapodistrian University of Athens)
Abstract
Entity Resolution (ER) is typically addressed through the Filtering-Verification framework. Despite numerous existing techniques, there is currently no interactive system that allows users to experimentally explore, compare, and understand the combined impact of Filtering and Verification under realistic conditions. We present SMBench, the first open-source, no-code web application for end-to-end ER that unifies Filtering and learning-based Verification in a single workflow. Unlike existing ER tools that focus on one step in isolation, SMBench allows for studying how candidate generation affects downstream matching under realistic conditions, while also exposing runtime, memory, and effectiveness trade-offs through an interactive interface. The demo will enable users to configure complete ER pipelines with a few selections, compare alternative methods on the same dataset, and inspect the resulting candidate pairs and predictions to understand why certain pipelines succeed or fail. Given that our system is modular and containerized, the same workflow can be reused for new datasets and methods with minimal effort, making SMBench useful both as a research benchmark and as a practical exploratory tool.
B06DEMOPROBE-Web: An Interactive System for Probing Evaluation Landscapes of Knowledge Graph Completion Models
Sooho Moon (Chung-Ang university) · Yunyong Ko (Chung-Ang University)
Abstract
Knowledge graph completion (KGC) models are commonly evaluated using rank-based metrics such as MRR and Hits@K, despite different users often requiring different evaluation perspectives. In this demo, we present PROBEWeb, an interactive system for probing diverse evaluation landscapes for KGC models. PROBEWeb enables users to flexibly evaluate KGC models by adjusting two critical perspectives: (P1) predictive sharpness and (P2) popularity-bias robustness. Through a user-friendly GUI, users easily evaluate multiple KGC models and analyze their strengths and weaknesses. PROBEWeb provides four key functionalities: (1) conventional evaluation toolkit, (2) flexible perspective-aware evaluation, (3) explainable case studies, and (4) evaluation landscape exploration. We believe that PROBEWeb can help users better understand KGC models aligning with their objectives.
B07DEMOSearchLog: A Web Browser Extension for Capturing Search Logs in Laboratory Studies
Jiaman He (RMIT University) · Riccardo Xia (Independent Researcher) · Dana McKay (RMIT University) · Damiano Spina (RMIT University) · Johanne R Trippas (RMIT University)
Abstract
Natural search logs are valuable for studying search behavior in information seeking settings. We present SearchLog, an easy-to-install web browser extension for collecting natural search logs during lab-based studies. SearchLog enables participants to search the open web in a browser while recording structured interaction data from the mouse, keyboard, search activity, and browser state modules. The extension captures clicks, scrolling, hovered text, typed words, search queries, result rankings, AI-generated summaries when available, tab activity, and window changes. A local Flask backend stores each session as an ordered JSON event stream, including HTML snapshots and preprocessed search result data for later analysis. These logs can be used to derive measures such as query reformulation, page visits, dwell time, scroll behavior, tab switching, search path complexity, and exposure to AI-generated search content. By supporting natural browser-based search with structured experimental metadata, SearchLog provides a reusable resource to study search behavior across traditional and AI-enhanced search interfaces. SearchLog is available at https://github.com/peanutH/SearchLog-chromium-extension.
B08DEMOVietCheckMed: A Scalable Retrieval-Augmented Engine for Zero-Day Regulatory Oversight
Tam Nguyen (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Khanh Quoc Tran (University of Information Technology, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Hoang-An Vo (University of Information Technology, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Khoa Anh Ta (University of Information Technology, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Truong Phu Le (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Thu Le (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Thi Dang (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Dat Thanh Pham (University of Information Technology, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Duyen Ngo (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Han Nguyen (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City) · Lizi Liao (Singapore Management University) · Binh Nguyen (University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City)
Abstract
The exponential growth of adversarial multimedia in digital advertising poses a critical regulatory challenge, where malicious actors exploit cross-modal semantics to obfuscate unauthorized physical interventions. Conventional fact-checking systems, constrained by static weights and modality bias, suffer from legislative concept drift and multimodal camouflage. We present VietCheckMed, an interactive, retrieval-augmented platform that operationalizes training-free causal reasoning for high-throughput regulatory oversight. Architected as a dynamic Knowledge-as-a-Service (KaaS) ecosystem, it circumvents model retraining via dynamic axiom injection and hybrid retrieval. To dismantle cross-modal evasion, the backend orchestrates the MM-RegCheck algorithm, employing Training-Free Bayesian Evidence Aggregation (TF-BEAR) to mathematically isolate visual violations against retrieved statutory constraints. By synergizing a 9B-parameter backbone with advanced API context caching, VietCheckMed achieves a state-of-the-art 0.898 Macro-F1 score while aggressively amortizing inference costs to approximately $0.0004 per sample, establishing a highly scalable, economically viable blueprint for next-generation RegTech.
B09DEMOTabgenQA: A Platform for Non-Relational, Multi-Tabular, Numerical QA Benchmark Generation and LLM Evaluation
Michele Luca Contalbo (University of Modena and Reggio Emilia) · Matteo Paganelli (University of Modena and Reggio Emilia) · Paolo Papotti (EURECOM) · Francesco Guerra (University of Modena and Reggio Emilia)
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are widely used for tabular data analysis, but their performance often does not transfer from standard Table QA benchmarks to real-world settings, where tables are typically non-relational, with hierarchical headers, merged cells, inconsistent units, noise, and implicit cross-table dependencies. We present TabgenQA, an interactive system for generating verifiable non-relational multi-table QA benchmarks and evaluating LLMs on them. Users configure domain-specific benchmark settings, inspect and refine generated instances, and compare API-based or locally deployed models through live leaderboards and error analysis views. Across procurement, failure diagnosis, and benchmark curation scenarios, TabgenQA provides an end-to-end workflow for deployment-oriented assessment of LLMs on real-world tabular data.
B10DEMOTSGuard: A Real-Time Framework for Detecting and Imputing Missing Data in Streaming Time Series
Imane Hocine (University of Luxembourg) · Asma Abboura (University of Hassiba Benbouali of Chlef) · Soror Sahri (Université Paris Cité) · Abhijith Senthilkumar (University of Luxembourg) · Yacine Hakimi (école Nationale Supérieure d'Informatique) · Grégoire Danoy (University of Luxembourg)
Abstract
Streaming sensor applications routinely suffer from delayed or missing observations caused by faults, communication losses, or environmental interference. Although recent imputation methods exploit temporal and spatial dependencies effectively, most either assume offline access to future observations or prioritize throughput without enforcing domain plausibility. We present TSGuard, a real-time demonstration system for monitoring, validating, and imputing missing values in streaming time series. TSGuard combines a lightweight graph-aware temporal imputation model with constraint-aware validation, fallback estimation, and operator-facing explanations. Rather than treating imputation as an isolated prediction task, TSGuard integrates it into a broader data-quality loop: detect problematic observations, impute missing values, validate estimated against physical and spatial constraints, and either retain the original value as a plausible anomaly or replace it when it violates domain constraints. Using environmental sensing as a motivating setting, the demo enables users to inspect delayed sensors, compare imputers, define constraints, and validate flagged values in real time. The combination of lightweight online spatiotemporal imputation, domain-aware validation, and explicit retain-or-replace decisions is our central contribution, while interactive explanations make these decisions inspectable and actionable. for operators.
B11DEMOAwareML: Transparent, Controllable, and Sustainable Streaming AutoML
Vikash Maheshwari (University of Tartu) · Radwa El Shawi (University of Tartu)
Abstract
Streaming AutoML has emerged as a powerful paradigm for building adaptive machine learning pipelines over non-stationary data, yet existing frameworks remain largely opaque: users cannot inspect why a framework was selected, how it responds to concept drift, or what its computational and environmental cost is. This opacity prevents domain experts from making principled deployment decisions and limits trust in automated model selection, particularly in resource-constrained, fairness-sensitive, or interpretability-critical settings. To address this, we developed a preference-aware meta-learning recommender that translates user-defined objectives into structured profiles for pre-run algorithm selection across accuracy, runtime, energy, and CO2 criteria. In this demonstration, we introduce AwareML, a web-based interactive platform that unifies five streaming AutoML frameworks—AutoStreamML, AutoClass, EvoAutoML, OAML, and ChaCha—under a single dashboard for transparent, controllable, and sustainable comparison. AwareML enables users to specify optimisation goals in natural language via LLaMA 3, monitor live temporal performance and concept-drift adaptation, inspect online fairness behaviour, receive streaming-window SHAP and LIME explainability summaries, and track energy and CO2 sustainability indicators via CodeCarbon. A usability study with 25 participants confirms an 80% task-completion rate across six representative tasks, with 73.3% of users reporting improved confidence in model-selection decisions, demonstrating AwareML's potential as a practical tool for transparent, fair, and sustainable streaming AutoML deployment.
B12DEMOAgentPDM: Context-Driven Agentic Reasoning for Predictive Maintenance
Shuaicheng Zhang (Virginia Tech) · Tuo Wang (Virginia Tech) · Lecheng Zheng (Virginia Tech) · Stephen Adams (Virginia Tech National Security Institute) · Don Williams (Deloitte & Touche LLP) · Derek Snaidauf (Deloitte & Touche LLP) · Balaji Veeramani (Deloitte & Touche LLP) · Dawei Zhou (Virginia Tech)
Abstract
Predictive Maintenance (PDM) uses sensor signals to assess machine health and guide actions such as continued operation, monitoring, or repair. Existing data-driven classifiers and knowledge-driven condition-monitoring tools each capture only part of the expert diagnostic workflow, which also requires reasoning over sensing modality, operating context, bearing geometry, spectral signatures, model uncertainty, and maintenance implications. LLM/VLM agents offer a way to coordinate these heterogeneous inputs, but free-form fault prediction remains unreliable. We present Agentpdm, an interactive multi-agent system for context-aware bearing diagnosis. It combines a four-backbone signal ensemble, bearing-physics tools, structured visual evidence, a conservative Decision Agent, and fixed-label report generation. Agentpdm proposes fault hypotheses, verifies them against operating context, spectral evidence, and model disagreement, and then accepts, overrides, or escalates the diagnosis before reporting. On cross-domain scenarios from CWRU, HUST, and Paderborn, Agentpdm improves accuracy from 84.3% to 87.7% with zero correct-to-wrong regressions. These results show that LLM/VLM agents are most reliable in industrial PDM when embedded in a bounded diagnostic workflow rather than used as unconstrained fault predictors.
B13DEMOMap of Science: Charting Worldwide Open Scientific Literature
Katherine Quinn (Georgetown University) · Rebecca Gelles (Georgetown University) · Adrian Thinnyun (Georgetown University) · Brian Love (Georgetown University) · Catherine Aiken (Georgetown University)
Abstract
The increasing pace of scientific production makes tracking worldwide research trends and emerging fields a nearly Sisyphean task. To tackle this challenge, we develop the Map of Science, a visualization tool for analyzing clusters of global research to support identification of emerging scientific and technological areas. To build our tool, we group more than 144 million scholarly articles from 197 countries into over 91,000 research clusters using citations and text embeddings. Along with regularly updating research clusters as new scientific articles are published, we add LLM-enabled summarization, filtering capabilities, and extreme growth predictions. We visualize the resulting clusters in the interactive, publicly available Map of Science tool, available at https://sciencemap.eto.tech/. The tool demonstrates usability and monthly usage increases, with improved modularity, topic separation, entity resolution, and searching and sorting capabilities. The Map of Science and our clustering code are available for public use, and a short video demonstration is available https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EbTIqLgC3sY.
B14DEMOManipulativeAgent: A Multi-Agent System for Generating Interactive Mathematical Manipulatives
Xiaoli Zeng (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Xiatong Peng (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Ziyuan Hu (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Tengteng Cheng (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University) · Zitao Liu (Guangdong Institute of Smart Education, Jinan University)
Abstract
Virtual interactive manipulatives help elementary students transition from concrete to abstract mathematical thinking through hands-on digital activities. However, creating them requires both pedagogical and programming expertise, while existing platforms only offer fixed templates that cannot adapt to individual teaching needs. We present ManipulativeAgent, a multi-agent system that allows teachers to create customized manipulatives from natural language descriptions of their instructional goals, with human-in-the-loop checkpoints for review and revision at each stage. Rather than relying on a single large language model (LLM) for end-to-end generation, ManipulativeAgent distributes the task across specialized agents that collaborate through a shared component library of pre-tested virtual tools. This design separates pedagogical reasoning from code implementation, enabling each agent to focus on its strength while the component library ensures interaction reliability. Evaluation on 40 real teaching scenarios shows improvements over commercial platforms and general-purpose LLMs, with the largest gain in interaction richness. A user study with 89 frontline teachers from 15 provinces shows that 92.1% would continue using the system for lesson preparation. A demonstration video is available at https://youtu.be/7eclhXhRy0A.
B15DEMOFlagger: A Platform for Operationalizing AI-Driven Early Warning Predictions to Find Personalized Interventions Faster
